methodology.Fees: Fees paid by PAR and paUSD borrowers in the Classic Vaults: the borrowing fee (interest), the 0.2% origination fee and the liquidation fee, all added to the vaults' debt. Measured as the change in the income accrued by each VaultsCore (the debt above the PAR or paUSD the core minted, as VaultsCoreState.availableIncome() computes it, plus the interest accrued since each collateral type's last refresh), plus the income released by the FeeDistributor that day.
methodology.Revenue: The fees without the Insurance Fund's 20%: the shares the FeeDistributor mints to the DAO Treasury and to the PRL stakers' payee, 80% of the fees. Revenue is protocol revenue plus holders revenue.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: The DAO Treasury's share of the fees, from the FeeDistributor's payees, without the 15% for PRL holders: 80% before that share began on 1 May 2025, 65% since. Under PGP-42, from 25 May to 1 October 2026, the Treasury received 80%, but 15% of the fees went on to PRL holders (buybacks, then September's staking rewards paid by hand), so 65% is counted here.
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: 20% of the fees, minted by the FeeDistributor to the Insurance Fund, which covers the vaults' bad debt.
methodology.HoldersRevenue: The 15% of the fees for PRL holders since 1 May 2025, 0 before, measured at the fee source as that share of the day's fees. It is passed on to PRL stakers (sPRL1, sPRL2) through the RewardMerkleDistributor, and read from the FeeDistributor's payees. Under PGP-42, from 25 May to 31 August 2026, the DAO Treasury received that 15% to buy PRL back and burn it: a buyback funded by the fees, counted here at the fee source. September 2026, paid to PRL stakers by hand by the DAO Treasury on 1 October 2026, counts as staking rewards. The buybacks the DAO Treasury pays from its own holdings are not counted.

methodology.Fees: Net gaming revenue (NGR) settled to the bankroll, measured as WINR received via ProfitReceived minus WINR paid out via LossCovered. This is an NGR figure standing in for a Fees field that conventionally carries GGR: gross wagered turnover is not observable on-chain because games run off-chain, and creator rewards, affiliate commissions and VIP cashback are already deducted in the off-chain escrow ledger before settlement. NGR is the most complete figure derivable from chain data, and this is a known limitation rather than an omission.
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: Equal to Fees. All settled net gaming revenue accrues to bankroll liquidity providers through share price appreciation; there is no separate distribution transaction.
methodology.Revenue: Zero. No protocol share is deducted on-chain - a 30 day reconciliation shows 100% of settled net gaming revenue accruing to bankroll liquidity providers through share price appreciation, with no leakage to any other on-chain party. The protocol does capture revenue at the application layer, but it is charged and accounted entirely off-chain and is not derivable from chain data, so it is deliberately not estimated here.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: Zero, for the same reason as Revenue: no protocol share is taken on-chain, and application-layer revenue is not observable from chain data.

methodology.Revenue: The governance fee, plus everything spent buying and burning HPO.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: The governance fee, deducted from the pool's reward before it reaches stakers. Its rate is set by Hipo's governor and can be zero.

methodology.HoldersRevenue: GRAM sent to Hipo's buy-and-burn contract, read from that contract's own income log so that returned change is excluded. It stakes the GRAM, buys HPO with the resulting hGRAM on DeDust, and burns it, lowering the total supply of HPO. Two sources pay it: the borrower fee forwarded by the treasury, and the realized profit of Hipo's HPO trading bot.

methodology.Fees: Every fee charged on a DeepBook trade, paid by both the taker and the maker. The headline rate is 0.1% on volatile pairs and 0.01% on stable pairs, but three pools (DEEP/SUI, DEEP/USDC, wUSDC/USDC) are fee-free and traders who stake enough DEEP pay half the taker fee, so the rate actually collected is lower.
methodology.Revenue: Trading fees left after maker rebates and referral payouts. DeepBook has no way to move collected fees to a treasury, so this money is either burned as DEEP or stays locked in the pool vaults permanently.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: Zero. DeepBook's contracts have no function to move collected trading fees out of a pool, so none of them reach a treasury. The only fee that does is the 500 DEEP charged to create a pool, which is too small to count.
methodology.HoldersRevenue: DEEP burned out of collected trading fees, which permanently shrinks the token supply. Burns are settled in batches, so the amount burned on a given day does not match that day's fees.
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: The share of trading fees handed back out: rebates claimed by market makers who stake DEEP, plus fees routed to referrers. Rebates are counted when a maker claims them, which can be days after the trades that earned them. Before April 2025 DeepBook reported claims in a form that gave no reliable date, so supply side revenue is understated for that period and revenue is correspondingly overstated.

methodology.ProtocolRevenue: Both the management and performance fees are paid to the protocol, so protocol revenue equals the total fees collected.

Later dividend distribution and compounding are not counted again. Pool fees cover factory-deployed launches only; router app fees also cover third-party tokens traded through Sentry. Downstream treasury reallocations, independent non-launch hooks, direct custodial-wallet skims and third-party domain referrals are outside this contract-event scope.

methodology.SupplySideRevenue: Creator allocations, launch-token dividends, community reward/growth allocations, liquidity reinvestment and router referrals. Legacy creator LP fees are actual payouts on the collection date; they may have accrued over earlier days. Assets without a DefiLlama price remain native-token balances, not invented USD values.

methodology.Volume: USDC.e paid to buy outcome shares and received from selling them. When a buyer trades with a seller the same money is reported by both of them, so it is only counted once. When two buyers are matched a new pair of shares is created, and when two sellers are matched a pair is redeemed — in those trades each side puts up its own money, so both sides are counted.
methodology.NotionalVolume: Outcome shares traded, where each share pays $1 if its outcome wins. Counted on the same basis as volume: once for a buyer-versus-seller trade, and on both sides when two buyers or two sellers are matched.
methodology.Fees: Trading fee taken out of each filled order's proceeds. Sellers pay it in USDC.e; buyers pay it in outcome shares, valued at the price they traded at. Both sides of a trade are charged.
methodology.Revenue: All trading fees. predictstreet keeps the full fee — there are no maker or liquidity-provider rebates.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: All trading fees. Predictstreet keeps the full fee — there are no maker or liquidity-provider rebates.

Not all TeraSwap volume reaches that contract: routes filled by 0x, CoW Swap and Bebop collect the identical 0.1% through those venues' own partner-fee parameters instead of the FeeCollector, emit no SwapWithFee event, and are therefore NOT counted here.

methodology.SupplySideRevenue: Share of swap fees kept by liquidity providers: 0% on gauged pools (LPs there earn GIGA emissions instead), 97% on non-gauged pools.

methodology.Volume: ETH traded on PEEPS bonding curves.
methodology.Fees: 1.25% fee on every bonding-curve trade, 0.40% paid to the token creator and 0.85% allocated to the PEEPS.WTF platform and ecosystem.
methodology.Revenue: 0.85% platform fee from every bonding-curve trade, allocated to the PEEPS.WTF platform and ecosystem.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: 0.85% platform fee from every bonding-curve trade, allocated to the PEEPS.WTF platform and ecosystem.
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: 0.40% creator fee from every bonding-curve trade, paid to the creator of the launched token.

methodology.Volume: ETH side of every bonding-curve trade: ETH paid in on buys (fee-inclusive) and gross ETH taken out of the curve reserve on sells. Post-graduation Uniswap V3 swaps are not counted.
methodology.Fees: A 1.25% fee charged on the ETH leg of every bonding-curve buy and sell, read per trade from the Trade event's protocolFee and creatorFee fields. HoodMint has no launch fee and no graduation fee.
methodology.Revenue: The protocol slice of the bonding-curve trade fee.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: Same as Revenue — the protocol slice of the bonding-curve trade fee.
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: The creator slice of the bonding-curve trade fee, claimable by each token's creator.

methodology.Fees: The 1% Uniswap V3 pool fee paid on every swap of tokens launched via ArrowPad (measured on the WETH leg).
methodology.UserFees: The 1% Uniswap V3 pool fee paid on every swap of tokens launched via ArrowPad (measured on the WETH leg).
methodology.Revenue: The protocol's immutable 20% share of the pool fees.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: The protocol's immutable 20% share of the pool fees.
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: The 80% share of pool fees that streams to the token creators.

methodology.Fees: All fees paid by traders on the Lighter Robinhood perpetuals deployment: maker, taker, transfer, withdrawal and liquidation fees. Scoped to perp markets (spot is tracked separately as lighter-spot).
methodology.Revenue: Protocol revenue from maker, taker, transfer and withdrawal fees. Liquidation fees are excluded — they go to the LLP (see SupplySideRevenue).
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: Same as Revenue: maker, taker, transfer and withdrawal fees retained by the protocol.
methodology.HoldersRevenue: Fees going to governance token holders
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: Liquidation fees, which are paid to the Lighter Liquidity Pool (LLP) — i.e. to liquidity providers, not the protocol.

methodology.Fees: Builder code fees paid by users trading Hyperliquid perps via CCXT.
methodology.Revenue: Builder code fees collected by CCXT from Hyperliquid perps trades.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: Builder code fees collected by CCXT from Hyperliquid perps trades.

methodology.Fees: Builder code fees paid by users trading Hyperliquid perps via Owly.fi.
methodology.Revenue: Builder code fees collected by Owly.fi from Hyperliquid perps trades.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: Builder code fees collected by Owly.fi from Hyperliquid perps trades.

methodology.Fees: Total borrow interest paid by borrowers: for every trade, the face value of the debt (units) minus the loan tokens the borrower received (sellerAssets), i.e. the fixed-rate discount locked in at execution.
methodology.Revenue: Protocol fees kept by Morpho: the settlement fee (taker-paid spread on each trade) plus the continuous fee accrued on new lender credit. Both are disabled at launch, so Revenue is currently 0.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: Same as Revenue: settlement fee plus continuous fee. Currently 0 while both fees are disabled.
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: Interest distributed to lenders: total borrow interest minus the protocol settlement and continuous fees.

methodology.Volume: Sum of swap volume routed through the PurrFlow Aggregator Router on Bitkub Chain.
methodology.Fees: Router-skim fee deducted from every Swapped event (currently 0.60%), hard-capped at 1.00% per route.
methodology.Revenue: All the router-skim fees deducted from each swap accrue to the protocol treasury.
methodology.Protocol Revenue: All the router-skim fees deducted from each swap accrue to the protocol treasury.

methodology.Fees: Total staking rewards by running validators on Hyperliquid.
methodology.Revenue: Staking rewards commission collected by protocol.
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: Staking rewards are distributed to stakers after commission cut.

methodology.Fees: Fees extracted per round: 1% admin fee on all deployed ETH, 1% admin fee on the losers pool, and a 10% vault fee on the losers pool after admin. On rounds where nobody hit the winning block, the entire pot (minus the admin fee) is routed to the Treasury vault. Variable effective rate depending on winner/loser ratio.
methodology.UserFees: Same as Fees — all fees are paid by players out of their deployed ETH.
methodology.Revenue: All extracted fees: the sum of protocol revenue (admin fees) and holders revenue (vault fees).
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: Admin fees (1% of deployed ETH + 1% of losers pool) accruing to the protocol fee wallet.
methodology.HoldersRevenue: Vault fee ETH funds automated PEA buybacks — 95% of bought PEA is permanently burned, 5% is distributed to PEA stakers as yield.

methodology.Fees: Total Uniswap V3 trading fees earned by all AutoRange vaults' positions, realized on rebalance or when the vault owner manually claims — the full amount before the platform/owner split.
methodology.Revenue: The platform's performance-fee cut of those trading fees, set per-vault by PlatformConfig and capped by the vault owner.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: The platform's performance-fee cut of those trading fees, set per-vault by PlatformConfig and capped by the vault owner.
methodology.HoldersRevenue: Money going to governance token holders
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: The vault owner's (LP's) net share of trading fees, after the platform's cut.

methodology.Volume: Gross collateral notional (ETH and USDG, fees included) of buys and sells executed on RH.fun bonding curves, from the factory Buy/Sell events. Post-graduation swaps happen on the chain's Uniswap V2 DEX and are not counted here.
methodology.Fees: All fees generated by the protocol: the 1% trade fee on bonding-curve buys/sells, token taxes (curve phase and post-graduation DEX phase, counted when the TaxProcessor realizes them), and graduation fees (fixed migration fee + dust). Legs denominated in the launched tokens themselves are not counted.
methodology.UserFees: Same as Fees — all fees are paid by traders.
methodology.Revenue: Protocol revenue: the 1% curve trade fee, graduation fees, and the protocol fee bucket of tax dispatches. RH.fun has no protocol token, so there is no holders revenue and Revenue equals ProtocolRevenue.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: The 1% curve trade fee, graduation fees, and the protocol fee bucket of tax dispatches.
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: Token tax routed to the launched token's own side: market recipients (creator/community), token-holder dividends, buyback-and-burn, and permanently locked liquidity.

methodology.Fees: On Base/Robinhood: gross Doppler pool trading fees (2.5%), extrapolated from Squeeze’s 47.5% Doppler fee-collect receipts. On Solana: LaunchLab *platform* fees claimed to Squeeze’s claim wallet only (not creator/protocol/referral cuts).
methodology.Revenue: Squeeze platform share — EVM: 47.5% of Doppler swap fees claimed via collectFees; Solana: LaunchLab platform fees to the claim wallet.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: Squeeze platform share — EVM: 47.5% of Doppler swap fees claimed via collectFees; Solana: LaunchLab platform fees to the claim wallet.
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: On EVM: extrapolated creator share (47.5%) and Doppler protocol-owner share (5%). On Solana: not attributed in v1 (those cuts never hit the Squeeze claim wallet).

methodology.UserFees: Swap fees paid by traders, borrow interest paid by borrowers into LP reserves, and protocol-retained lending fees paid by borrowers and over-repayers.
methodology.Fees: Swap fees inferred from each swap's actual input minus the no-fee input required by the pre-swap reserve invariant for the observed output, the LP reserve-growth portion of borrow interest emitted by InterestAccrued, and protocol-retained lending fees minted to the Ammalgam fee recipient. Ammalgam swap fees are dynamic; see https://docs.ammalgam.xyz/docs/developer-guide/contracts/libraries/QuadraticSwapFees.
methodology.Revenue: Protocol-retained lending fees minted to the Ammalgam fee recipient. No protocol fees are taken from swaps.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: Protocol-retained lending fees minted to the Ammalgam fee recipient. No protocol fees are taken from swaps.
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: Swap fees and the LP reserve-growth portion of borrow interest accrue to liquidity providers.
methodology.Volume: Swap volume from Ammalgam pairs deployed by the Ethereum mainnet factory. Volume is counted from the input side of each Swap event only: amountXIn for tokenX and amountYIn for tokenY.

methodology.Fees: Uniswap V3 swap fees accrued on each launched token's pool, collected via the AaroLauncher contract.
methodology.Revenue: The 20% treasury share of collected swap fees.
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: The 80% creator share of collected swap fees.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: The 20% treasury share of collected swap fees.

methodology.Fees: Gross accumulated ticket fees recognized when WindfallFeeShare emits FeeDistributed. Recognition is aligned with the allocation period so gross fees equal protocol revenue plus supply-side revenue in every reporting window.
methodology.Revenue: The portion of each FeeDistributed amount allocated to hostTreasury. Donor shareholder payouts are excluded and classified as supply-side revenue.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: The hostTreasury allocation, including all host shares and the integer-division remainder assigned exclusively to the host.
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: The portion of each FeeDistributed amount allocated to active donor shareholders. Each active donor receives one distribution share.

methodology.Fees: Net yield earned by Unitas strategies on XAUt-backed XGLD, estimated from the exchange rate increase credited to XGLD holders and their documented 80% share. Excludes the USDu product (tracked in fees/unitas-usdu).
methodology.Revenue: The 10% of net strategy yield allocated to the Unitas treasury and platform operations.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: The 10% of net strategy yield allocated to the Unitas treasury and platform operations.
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: The 80% of net strategy yield credited to XGLD holders through the exchange rate (NAV) increase and the 10% set aside in the Insurance Fund that backs XGLD holders. Excludes XGLD held on Base, which is immaterial.

methodology.Volume: Total volume of swaps on the Prismapad legacy launchpad, valued in USDT0. (v2/v3: not tracked as that swap volume belongs to stableswap-xyz-v3)
methodology.Fees: A flat 1% fee on every trade, valued in USDT0: charged by the bonding curve on legacy v1 tokens, and by the 1% Uniswap v3 pool tier on v2/v3 tokens. Buy-side pool fees are charged on the USDT0 input (exact); sell-side pool fees are charged in the traded token and valued as their USDT0 equivalent at that swap's own price (usdtOut/99).
methodology.UserFees: Traders pay the 1% trade fee; there is no token-creation fee.
methodology.Revenue: 50% of every trade fee accrues to the Prismapad treasury.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: 50% of every trade fee accrues to the Prismapad treasury.
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: 50% of every trade fee accrues to the launched token's creator (v1: claimable from the launchpad; v2/v3: collected from the locked pool position).

methodology.Volume: Total ETH wagered across all lottery rounds, derived from staker rewards (a flat 6% of each round's pot).
methodology.Fees: The 10% rake taken from every round's pot: 6% to veSTEEL stakers, 2% to the keeper, and 2% to the motherlode.
methodology.Revenue: Gross profit: 6% distributed to veSTEEL stakers plus the 2% keeper cut.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: The 2% keeper self-funding cut retained by the protocol.
methodology.HoldersRevenue: All staker rewards — the ETH distributed to veSTEEL stakers (RewardNotified events on VeSteelV2).
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: The 2% of each pot routed to the motherlode, paid back out to winning players.

methodology.Volume: Gross ETH paid by purchasers for acquisitions (pulls), net of refunded, expired, or slippage-cancelled requests.
methodology.Fees: Net Acquisition fees paid by NFT purchasers, plus settlement fees taken from listing backings.
methodology.Revenue: Team share of the protocol's cut of acquisition and settlement fees, plus any fees diverted to FWA-token buybacks.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: Team share of the protocol's fee cut, per the Splitter contract's live split, minus the FWA-token buybacks counted under HoldersRevenue.
methodology.HoldersRevenue: FWA-token buybacks funded from protocol fees, plus retroactive scheduled buybacks funded from previously earned team fees.
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: Share of net acquisition fees distributed to NFT depositors (equal split across active listings plus the top-listing pot), plus the snapshot soulbound-NFT holders' share of protocol fees via the Splitter.

methodology.Fees: All Uniswap V3 trading fees collected by the positions each Tirelire Hypervisor manages, summed on-chain from ZeroBurn events.
methodology.Revenue: The 10% performance fee taken from collected trading fees and sent to the protocol treasury (fees / fee, with the divisor read from each ZeroBurn event).
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: Same as Revenue — the 10% performance fee retained by the protocol treasury.
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: The 90% of collected trading fees that are compounded back to LPs.

methodology.UserFees: User pays fees on each swap.
methodology.Fees: Includes swap fees and bribes paid by protocols
methodology.Revenue: Revenue going to the protocol + Token holder Revenue.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: Swap fees going to the protocol
methodology.HoldersRevenue: Swap fees distributed to holders and all the bribes go to holders
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: Swap fees distributed to LPs (from gauged pools).

methodology.Fees: Quote-denominated swap fees from Hook Trade events plus token-launch payment events across configured suites. Legacy launch-token-denominated swap fees are excluded because reliable historical USD valuation is unavailable. Crypto uses token balances; Stocks use the event-time factory tick reference price under the documented $4,000 opening-cap convention, with historical DefiLlama prices only when that reference is unavailable.
methodology.Revenue: Actual platform and protocol-owned fixed-component swap credits, plus token-launch fees. Includes anti-snipe surcharges, referral fallback and rounding retained by the protocol. Claims do not count again.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: Swap and launch fees retained by the protocol treasury.
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: Actual swap credits allocated to creators and referrers, including amounts still unclaimed.

methodology.Volume: Sum of the input amount of every executed order, taken from the router's OrderExecuted logs. Only the input leg is counted, so a single trade is never counted twice. Cancellations, which the previous router encoded as an OrderExecuted with orderType 255, are excluded.
methodology.Fees: Protocol fee deducted from the output token of each executed order. The rate is signed by the maker as part of the order and capped on-chain at 1%.
methodology.Revenue: All the protocol fees deducted from the output token of each executed order. The router has no liquidity providers, so nothing is shared out.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: All the protocol fees deducted from the output token of each executed order. The router has no liquidity providers, so nothing is shared out.
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: None. Liquidity is Uniswap's; its pool fees are not counted here.

methodology.Volume: Gross USDG notional of BowYard bonding-curve trades.
methodology.Fees: USDG token-creation fees plus all trading fees from BowYard's classic and Agent bonding curves and post-graduation DEX pools.
methodology.UserFees: All creation and trading fees paid by BowYard users, denominated in USDG.
methodology.Revenue: Fees paid to the BowYard protocol treasury: the full classic token-creation fee, the classic protocol share of curve/DEX fees, and the immutable 20% protocol share of Agent trading fees.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: The full classic token-creation fee, the classic protocol share of curve/DEX fees, and 20% of Agent trading fees.
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: Classic creator fee shares plus the Agent market shares routed to creators, operating recipients, and attributed ecosystem recipients.

methodology.Fees: 1% swap fees from bow.fun factory-launched Uniswap V3 pools on Robinhood Chain, filtered for pools with at least $1,000 TVL.
methodology.Revenue: 65% of swap fees retained by the bow.fun protocol, filtered for pools with at least $1,000 TVL.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: 65% of swap fees retained by the bow.fun protocol, filtered for pools with at least $1,000 TVL.
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: 35% of swap fees routed to launched-token creators, filtered for pools with at least $1,000 TVL.

methodology.Fees: Total swap fees, priced in the valued leg's token. Per-swap fee = amount x (pool.fee / 1e6) where pool.fee is the value live at the swap's block_time (sourced from init_dex plus every update_fee_and_revenue_cut call, window-joined via effective range). Exact-in swaps are valued on the input leg (amount_in call argument), exact-out swaps on the output leg (amount_out call argument). Per-pool token identity comes from the swap calls, with dex_call_init_dex as a fallback for pools that have never traded.
methodology.Revenue: Jupiter's share of the protocol cut: fees x (revenue_cut/1e6) x 50%.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: Jupiter's share of the protocol cut: fees x (revenue_cut/1e6) x 50%.
methodology.HoldersRevenue: Money going to governance token holders
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: LP share of swap fees plus Fluid's protocol share. LP share = fees x (1 - revenue_cut/1e6). Fluid receives 50% of the protocol cut per Jupiter Lend / Fluid arrangement.

methodology.Fees: Total fees paid by users on AGNT: (1) the 1.095% Doppler V4 terminal pool fee on tokens launched via the launchpad on Base + Robinhood Chain, derived from the observed on-chain platform fee share (WETH on Base; WETH plus RWA numeraires — tokenized stocks like AAPL that a Robinhood launch pairs against, e.g. $BEER — on Robinhood, priced by DefiLlama; the unpriced launched-token leg is excluded, a conservative lower bound); plus (2) the 0.40% platform fee on in-app swaps (Base), measured as WETH + USDC paid by Relay to AGNT's app-fee recipient wallet; plus (3) fees from PonsV2 launches on Robinhood Chain, read from each token's AgntFeeWedge Split events (native-ETH leg = total user-paid fee); plus (4) native-ETH paid by buyers to mint AGNT's own AGNTS PFP collection on Robinhood Chain; plus (5) AGNTS activation fees on Robinhood Chain (ETH fee + $AGNTS cost, from the Activated event); plus (6) AGNTS NFT swap fees on Robinhood Chain (random packs and exact picks; the fee is read from the swap engine at each swap's block).
methodology.Revenue: Fees kept by AGNT: the 32% platform share of launchpad pool fees (WETH released by the Doppler initializers on Base + Robinhood, to 0x5bF5805e…C5f0) plus 100% of the 0.40% swap fee (WETH + USDC paid by Relay on Base to the app-fee recipient wallets — 0x585b6854…0598 pre-repoint and 0x5bF5805e…C5f0 post-repoint) plus AGNT's ~2/7 (28.57%) protocol cut of PonsV2 launch fees on Robinhood (the `toAgnt` leg of each AgntFeeWedge Split; the remaining 5/7 is forwarded to each token's own engine) plus 100% of AGNTS NFT mint proceeds on Robinhood (a first-party collection, so there is no creator split) plus 100% of AGNTS activation ETH fees and swap fees, and the full $AGNTS activation cost (the treasury share plus the burned share).
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: Revenue kept by the AGNT treasury: everything in Revenue except the burned share of the $AGNTS activation cost.
methodology.HoldersRevenue: The share of each AGNTS activation's $AGNTS cost that is burned (burnBps, 50% today).
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: The 68% of launchpad pool fees paid to third-party token creators (63%) and the Doppler protocol (~5%), estimated from the observed platform WETH share.

methodology.Volume: Total ETH wagered across all bets each round, derived from staker rewards (a flat 8% of wagers).
methodology.Fees: The 10% rake taken from every round's wagers: 8% distributed to veNFT stakers plus 2% routed to the vault.
methodology.Revenue: All staker rewards — the ETH distributed to veNFT stakers (RewardDistributed events on CashVoteEscrowStaking).
methodology.HoldersRevenue: All staker rewards — the ETH distributed to veNFT stakers.
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: The 2% of wagers routed to the vault pool, which is paid back out to winning players.

methodology.Volume: Everything planted on the grid across both game versions: ETH from the v1 Planted and PlantedMany events, and ETH or AAPL from the v2 Planted events (v2 lets players plant from an AAPL balance).
methodology.Fees: Every plant pays an admin fee at the configured adminFeeBps rate (1% at time of writing) on the AAPL it buys — taken inside the plant on v1, and at the round's seal on v2 (where AAPL-denominated plants pay the same rate on their value and batched plants an extra batchFeeBps, 0 at time of writing). Every revealed round with a winner pays that round's configured rakeBps on the loss pool (the stakes on the 24 plots that did not bloom), split into a fixed 10% to SEED stakers (STAKERS_BPS, a contract constant), the round's configured jackpotBps share to the Golden Apple jackpot, and the remainder to the treasury. Rounds where the blooming plot is empty take no rake — the whole pot rolls into the jackpot.
methodology.UserFees: Same as Fees — both the admin fee and the rake are paid by players out of what they planted.
methodology.Revenue: Gross profit: the admin fee plus the stakers and treasury cuts of the rake. The jackpot cut is excluded because it is paid back out to players.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: The admin fee, withdrawn by the owner via collectAdmin: reconstructed per plant on v1, and on v2 measured as the growth of adminAccrued over the window plus the amounts withdrawn inside it.
methodology.HoldersRevenue: Value reaching SEED holders: the fixed 10% of each round's rake flushed to SeedStaking as AAPL yield for stakers, plus the treasury remainder that buys SEED back on the DEX and burns it.
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: The round's configured jackpotBps share of its rake, routed to the Golden Apple jackpot and paid back out to players when it hits.

methodology.Fees: The 12% taken from every mining round's pot (8% to LUNA stakers, 2% to the Motherlode jackpot, 1% to the Eclipse prize pool, 1% to the protocol), plus the 15% taken from every Eclipse beacon purchase (10% to stakers, 5% to the protocol).
methodology.Revenue: ETH distributed to LUNA stakers plus the protocol's retained cut.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: The 1% of each mining round pot and 5% of each Eclipse beacon purchase retained by the protocol.
methodology.HoldersRevenue: ETH distributed to LUNA stakers — 8% of each mining round pot and 10% of each beacon purchase.
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: The 2% Motherlode jackpot and 1% Eclipse prize pool funded by each mining round, both paid back out to players.

methodology.Volume: cardSales: Total card pack sales in the given time period.
methodology.Fees: cardSales (card pack sales) - cardBuybacks (card repurchases) + otherFees (platform fees).
methodology.Revenue: Net revenue retained by the protocol after buybacks.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: Revenue kept by the protocol.
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: Revenue allocated to suppliers/partners (currently 0).

methodology.Fees: Protocol fee charged on shielded withdrawals and swaps, always collected in ETH or USDG (ProtocolFeeCharged events), converted to USD.
methodology.Revenue: All the fees charged on shielded withdrawals and swaps are retained by the protocol.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: 100% of the fees charged on shielded withdrawals and swaps are retained by the protocol.

methodology.UserFees: Equals total swap fees paid by users.
methodology.Fees: Users pay each pool's configured fee tier on every swap.
methodology.Revenue: No protocol fee is taken, all swap fees go to liquidity providers.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: No protocol fee is taken.
methodology.HoldersRevenue: Money going to governance token holders
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: 100% of swap fees are distributed to liquidity providers.
methodology.Volume: Swap volume from all BetterSwap V3 pools deployed via the V3 factory.

methodology.Fees: Gross USDC product payments (subscriptions, pay-per-deploy, Architect builds, first-party agent income) entering the on-chain revenue splitter, summed from PaymentSplit events.
methodology.Revenue: The protocol's share of every payment — operating, dev, protocol-owned-liquidity reserve and DAO buckets — i.e. gross payments minus third-party affiliate payouts.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: Same as Revenue: all non-affiliate buckets are protocol-controlled.
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: The 3-level affiliate share (6% / 2.5% / 1.5%) credited to third-party referrers, from AffiliateCredited events.

methodology.Volume: Total USDT0 volume from all buys and sells on the launchpad.
methodology.Fees: Trade fees on every buy and sell, read directly from the Buy/Sell `fee` field emitted by the contract.
methodology.Revenue: Protocol share of trade fees: total fees minus creator cuts emitted via CreatorFeeAccrued.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: Protocol share of trade fees: total fees minus creator cuts emitted via CreatorFeeAccrued.
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: Creator share of trade fees, read directly from CreatorFeeAccrued events, claimable by each token's creator.

methodology.Fees: Swap fees charged by the KOLSwap protocol.
methodology.Revenue: Protocol fee routed to the protocol fee router.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: Protocol fee routed to the KOLMarket protocol fee router.
methodology.HoldersRevenue: Money going to governance token holders
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: Creator fee routed to the creator allocation and LP fee paid to liquidity providers.
methodology.Volume: Gross quote notional; sell fees are added back to net quote output.

methodology.Fees: Borrow interest paid by borrowers on Bitcoin-collateralised USDC loans.
methodology.Revenue: Protocol reserve share of borrow interest (reserveRateBps), from the protocolCut field of the InterestAccrued event.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: Protocol reserve share of borrow interest (reserveRateBps), from the protocolCut field of the InterestAccrued event.
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: Borrow interest distributed to USDC liquidity providers (LPs), from the lenderCut field of the InterestAccrued event.

methodology.Volume: Swap volume is back-calculated from fees received by the Yieldzio fee wallet. The standard fees use a 0.02% rate ($1 per $5,000). AVLT fees on Ethereum and HyperEVM use a 0.1% rate ($1 of fees per $1,000 of volume) due to the majority of the AVLT volume coming from the liquidation service which charges a 10bps fee.
methodology.Fees: All ERC-20 payments (0.1% swap fees on AVLT volume, 0.02% on other volume) received by the Yieldzio fee wallet are counted as fees.
methodology.UserFees: Yieldzio charges 0.1% (10 bps) on AVLT volume on Ethereum and HyperEVM, and 0.02% (2 bps) on other volume.
methodology.Revenue: 100% of fees (0.1% swap fees on AVLT volume, 0.02% on other volume) received by the fee wallet are protocol revenue.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: 100% of fees (0.1% swap fees on AVLT volume, 0.02% on other volume) received by the fee wallet are protocol revenue.

methodology.Fees: Users pay a 1% fee in ETH on every bonding-curve buy and sell, plus a one-time 0.001 ETH launch fee per token. After a token graduates (6.9 ETH raised) its liquidity is locked in a full-range Uniswap V3 position whose LP fees accrue to the protocol.
methodology.Revenue: 70% of bonding-curve trading fees, all launch fees (0.001 ETH per token), and the claimed LP fees of graduated tokens' locked liquidity positions.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: 70% of the 1% bonding-curve trading fee, all launch fees (0.001 ETH per token), and the claimed LP fees of graduated tokens' locked liquidity positions.
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: 30% of bonding-curve trading fees, paid instantly to token creators.

methodology.Volume: Gross ETH traded on card buys/sells plus pack shop primary mint sales
methodology.Fees: Trading fees paid by users on card buys/sells (pack primary-mint proceeds are counted as volume, not fees)
methodology.UserFees: Trading fees paid by users on card buys/sells
methodology.Revenue: Trading fees retained by the protocol treasury — fees minus the prize-pool, referral, and creator payouts
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: Same as Revenue — the protocol treasury's retained cut of trading fees
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: Prize-pool rewards distributed to card holders, referral rewards, and creator rewards

methodology.Volume: SOL paid into fanex_curve bonding-curve buys (the decoded buy instruction arg sol_in, fanex_solana.fanex_curve_call_buy). Buy-side only for now — the emit_cpi! Trade event that carries realized sell SOL is not yet decoded by Dune; sells are a negligible share of early volume. Post-graduation Raydium CPMM trading is excluded (counted by Raydium).
methodology.Fees: All value received by the Fanex fee wallet on Solana: the 6% fundraise share plus the 1% platform swap fee taken on every fanex_curve buy/sell, the 3% cut on creator dividend distributions, and harvested Raydium CPMM LP fees.
methodology.Revenue: All value received by the Fanex fee wallet on Solana: the 6% fundraise share plus the 1% platform swap fee taken on every fanex_curve buy/sell, the 3% cut on creator dividend distributions, and harvested Raydium CPMM LP fees.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: All value received by the Fanex fee wallet on Solana: the 6% fundraise share plus the 1% platform swap fee taken on every fanex_curve buy/sell, the 3% cut on creator dividend distributions, and harvested Raydium CPMM LP fees.

methodology.Volume: Sum of `price * amount` for every TradeRecorded event emitted by Primit's TradeRecorder contract (0xC005A9bb11f162329f3EfCCc35F69F9Bb635EeC6 on Avalanche C-Chain) during the UTC day, excluding self-trades where taker == maker. Both `price` and `amount` are 1e18 fixed-point, so the product is scaled by 1e36 and normalized down to floating USD before returning. Data is 100% reconstructable on-chain — no dependency on any Primit-operated HTTP endpoint. Every fill matched or routed by Primit is captured by this single TradeRecorder event stream, so there is no separate broker-level attribution to deduplicate against.
Gross WETH deployed across the game grid, including both direct and AutoMiner deployments, taken from the Game's Deployed events.

methodology.ProtocolRevenue: Round admin fees allocated to the configured admin recipient, plus any early-claim fees sent to a non-dead-address recipient.
methodology.HoldersRevenue: Treasury-vaulted WETH funds ROAR buybacks whose acquired tokens are burned and distributed to stakers. Early-claim ROAR sent to the dead address is also treated as holder revenue through permanent removal from circulation; that transfer does not reduce the token contract's totalSupply.

methodology.Fees: Everything users paid the protocol: all native revenue arriving at the chain's fee collector — the PlatformFeeCollector on Robinhood Chain, a bridging collector on each satellite — from the 2% presale service fee, launch tokens' master fee, the bonding pad's 0.5% per-trade skim, the instant-launch fee and the locker's fee-claim cut (FeesReceived logs), PLUS the 10% referrer share carved off the user-attributed streams before they reach the collector (ReferralPaid logs). methodology.SupplySideRevenue: The 10% referrer share, the one part of a fee the protocol does not keep — paid out by the ReferralRegistry to the trader's referrer before the remainder reaches the collector (ReferralPaid logs).
methodology.HoldersRevenue: The share of every home-chain distribution delivered to GovernanceToken holders as native-ETH dividends (FeesDistributed logs; distributions happen only on Robinhood Chain).
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: The share of every home-chain distribution delivered to the protocol owner (FeesDistributed logs; distributions happen only on Robinhood Chain).

methodology.Volume: Gross ETH notional (fees included) of buys and sells executed on Frontier bonding curves (v1 and v1.2), taken directly from each shared BondingCurve contract's Buy/Sell events, plus the ETH leg of every swap on a Frontier Uniswap V4 pool (graduated curves and v1.2 direct-seed launches alike), read from the canonical PoolManager's Swap events and filtered to the pools registered on Frontier's FactoryHook, excluding wash trading by the same rule as the uniswap-v4 adapter (pools whose daily trades come from too few distinct addresses to be organic, unless the coin is a core asset or CoinGecko-listed). Those V4 swaps are also counted by the uniswap-v4 adapter on Robinhood Chain, which is why this adapter is flagged doublecounted.
methodology.Fees: The bonding-curve trade fee charged on every buy and sell (1.5% of the trade's cost at the time of writing), the fees a token pays out of the ETH it raised when its curve fills and seeds its Uniswap V4 pool, the FactoryHook fee taken on every swap of a Frontier V4 pool (a hook delta on top of the pool's LP fee, so not part of uniswap-v4's fees), and the LP fees of the protocol's permanently locked seed positions, counted on a realized basis when they are collected (Harvester.collect is permissionless, so a collection carries the fees accrued since the previous one and lands on the collection day, not the days they were earned). v1 reconstructs the trade fee from the on-chain txFee timeline and graduation payouts from WETH transfers; v1.2 reads everything exactly from CurveFeeDistributed, GraduationFeesPaid, SwapFeeDistributed and the PolDistributor's FeesDistributed.
methodology.UserFees: Same as Fees: every fee is paid by traders out of their trade or out of the ETH they raised.
methodology.Revenue: Protocol revenue across both deployments: on v1, the protocol's 25% of the bonding-curve trade fee net of referrer rewards plus the factory owner's graduation share; on v1.2, the residual share of the trade fee after referrer and creator cuts (creator share owner-tunable via creatorShareBps), the protocol's graduation share, the protocol owner's share of the hook fee on every V4 swap, and the protocol's share of collected seed-position LP fees. Frontier has no protocol token, so there is no holders revenue and Revenue equals ProtocolRevenue.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: v1: 25% of the curve trade fee net of referrer rewards, plus WETH sent to the factory owner at graduation. v1.2: residual share of the curve trade fee (50% at the time of writing, net of referrer rewards), its share of graduation payouts (0% at the time of writing), the protocol owner's share of the V4 hook fee (protocolFeeRatio, owner-tunable) and the protocol's share of collected seed-position LP fees.
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: v1: the creator's 75% of every curve trade fee, referrer rewards, and the 5% graduation fee to the token creator. v1.2: the creator's share of every curve trade fee (50% at the time of writing), referrer rewards, the 5% graduation fee to the creator, the graduation refund to the caller (0% at the time of writing), and the after-protocol remainder of the V4 hook fee and of collected seed-position LP fees, split between the coin's staking vault and its fee recipient (the creator).

methodology.SupplySideRevenue: The creator share of launch-tax fees for standard pools; self-burn pools have no creator payout.

methodology.Fees: The arbitrage profit the hook realises and distributes, summed from the ProfitCurrencyDistribute event the first hook emits on every distribution; for the v2 hook (since 4 October 2026), every leg its executor pays — the swapper's cashback and the LPs' share it declares in ProfitCurrencyDistribute, plus the ProtocolRevenue, ReferralRewarded and PartnerRevenue it pays on top, including on the DELTA integration that shares the executor; plus the profit the HOOKR integration reports in its own ArbitrageProfitSplit and ProfitRecaptured events. The hook closes the price gap a swap opens between connected pools within the same transaction, so this is value recaptured from MEV rather than a fee charged to anyone.
methodology.Revenue: The share of that profit retained by the protocol treasury: the executor's ProtocolRevenue event (90% on WTH's own pools, 40% on pools that integrate WTH, since 2 September 2026; on the v2 hook's distributions and on the DELTA integration's, paid on top of the declared amounts) plus any profit donated into WTH's own pools, which was the treasury's income before that event existed. On an arbitrage run by the HOOKR integration it is the wthProtocolAmount leg of the ArbitrageProfitSplit event, and on a recapture the treasuryAmount of the ProfitRecaptured event.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: Same as Revenue — nothing is distributed to token holders on chain.
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: Everything not retained: the cashback paid to the trader whose swap created the opportunity, the profit donated to the liquidity providers of integrating pools, any referral share paid to an integrating partner, an integrating partner's cut (PartnerRevenue — DELTA's, on arbitrage started in its pools), and, on an arbitrage run by the HOOKR integration, the whole of the profit the protocol did not keep — the partner pays the trader, the trigger pool and its own treasury out of it; on a recapture, the hookAmount the event assigns to the pool's hook.
methodology.UserFees: Zero. Users are not charged by the hook; a swapper receives cashback rather than paying anything.

methodology.Fees: Treasury-bound pair commission (swap + book take + limit place) plus labeled wrap/window fees. spread_amount and community-tax extra-debit are not fees.
methodology.Revenue: Treasury commission credited to the protocol on swaps, book takes, limit placements, wrap/unwrap, and UST1 mint/redeem. Excludes LP spread and community-tax debits.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: Net protocol income from treasury-bound commissions on trading and ancillary services (wrap/unwrap, UST1 window). No share is routed to LPs or token holders.
methodology.HoldersRevenue: Money going to governance token holders
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: 0 — LPs earn inventory/spread, not a transferred commission.

methodology.Volume: Quote-side volume settled by Ignix bonding curves. Post-graduation Uniswap swaps are excluded.
methodology.Fees: Platform fees and launch taxes paid by users trading on Ignix bonding curves.
methodology.UserFees: All tracked bonding-curve fees are paid directly by traders.
methodology.Revenue: The platform-fee portion retained by Ignix.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: All Ignix revenue (platform fees portion) accrues to the protocol.
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: Launch taxes and anti-snipe fees allocated to launch creators and token-holder vaults.

methodology.Fees: Successful mainnet round-settlement fees calculated from the BidGrid ResetEvent allocation fields. User deposits, payouts and premine transfers are not counted as fees.
methodology.Revenue: Gross profit from BidGrid round fees after excluding the jackpot amount paid back to winning miners.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: The 1.5% protocol fee from each round's total deployed SOL, retained as the protocol treasury allocation.
methodology.HoldersRevenue: Round-fee allocations assigned to BDGR buybacks, BDGR staking rewards and the Burn Pot.
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: The jackpot allocation paid back to winning miners from the non-winning-tile fee.

methodology.Volume: Input value of every order placed on the Hyperbridge IntentGateway (same-chain and cross-chain), counted on the source chain.
methodology.Fees: 0.05% protocol fee deducted from order inputs at placement.
methodology.Revenue: The 0.05% protocol fee, retained by the gateway.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: The 0.05% protocol fee, retained by the gateway.

methodology.Fees: Swap fees charged on Hookers launches, in native ETH. A creator picks a launch style from the protocol's mechanism registry. Hooked styles skim a directional buy/sell fee inside the hook, set by the creator between 100 and 1000 bps. Hookless styles use the pool's own Uniswap v4 LP fee, collected through LiquidityCustody. The registry is read on chain, so styles added later are included automatically.
methodology.Revenue: The 30 bps protocol fee routed to FeeRouter, plus the share spent buying back and burning HKRS, the protocol's own token.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: A flat 30 bps of trade volume routed to FeeRouter. It is carved out of the creator's advertised fee rather than added on top, and applies identically to every launch style.
methodology.HoldersRevenue: HKRS bought back and burned, valued in ETH. This covers the automatic buyback hook on the HKRS pool, plus the discretionary buybacks the team runs out of the protocol's fee share, which are measured from the HKRS burned and priced from the HKRS pool. Buybacks on third-party launches are excluded and counted as supply side, since they accrue to those tokens' holders. Discretionary buybacks are funded from fees already counted as protocol revenue, so this figure overlaps ProtocolRevenue rather than adding to Revenue.
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: Fees paid out to launch creators: the creator-nominated fee slots on creator-fee styles, LP fees on hookless styles, and buyback and burn on third-party launches.

methodology.UserFees: Same as Fees: all swap fees are paid by traders.
methodology.Fees: Swap fees charged by Cantex pools (pool fee rate applied to each swap), denominated in CC.
methodology.Revenue: The protocol's share of swap fees (per-pool admin fee share).
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: The protocol's share of swap fees (per-pool admin fee share).
methodology.HoldersRevenue: Money going to governance token holders
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: The liquidity providers' share of swap fees.
methodology.Volume: 24h swap volume across all Cantex AMM pools. Every pool is CC-paired, so volume is single-counted as the Canton Coin leg of each on-chain swap, fetched from the Cantex public API (api.cantex.io/v1/public/volume) for the requested window and priced via Canton Coin's CoinGecko listing.
Sum of direct aggregated-swap volumes and order fill volumes (limit, DCA and trailing-stop executions) routed through the Epsilon router on Robinhood Chain, valued on the input token leg.
methodology.Fees: All fee legs charged on trades, measured from on-chain token transfers out of the router: protocol commission (including captured surplus), aggregation fees, keeper execution fees and referral fees. All fees are paid by traders out of trade proceeds.
methodology.Revenue: Protocol commission and aggregation fees, both collected by protocol-owned collectors.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: All revenue accrues to the protocol treasury (FeeVault and aggregation collector); there is no token.
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: Keeper execution fees paid to order executors and referral fees paid to third-party referrers/integrators (permissionless rev-share).

methodology.UserFees: All position, borrowing, liquidation, and UI fees actually paid by traders after referral discounts.
methodology.Fees: Position fees paid after trading discounts, plus borrowing, liquidation, and UI fees. Funding transfers between traders are excluded.
methodology.Revenue: The position, borrowing, and liquidation fee amounts accrued as claimable protocol fees and withdrawable through FeeHandler.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: The protocol fee share of position, borrowing, and liquidation fees held through FeeHandler.
methodology.HoldersRevenue: Fees going to governance token holders
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: Fees allocated to LPs, affiliates, UI integrators, and the credit fee claim vault.
methodology.Volume: Notional size of each executed position increase or decrease, including liquidation closes. Each PositionFeesCollected event represents one trader action, so no maker-side volume is added.

methodology.UserFees: Same as fees — traders pay both the maker and taker legs.
methodology.Fees: Maker and taker trading fees on Native Core CLOB fills. Each side pays independently, so both legs are counted. Taken from GET /api/v3/stats/window over the hour. Settlement assets are recorded under their Native Core registry token; CLOB-only synthetic assets without a canonical token are valued from their USDC/USDT market.
methodology.Revenue: Maker and taker fees Native retains after subtracting Native Pool yield distributed to LPs. Revenue can be negative in a distribution hour because Pool payouts include extra rewards as well as fee-funded yield.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: Maker and taker fees Native retains after subtracting Native Pool yield distributed to LPs. Revenue can be negative in a distribution hour because Pool payouts include extra rewards as well as fee-funded yield.
methodology.HoldersRevenue: Money going to governance token holders
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: Native Pool yield paid to LPs, from POST /api/v3/earn distributions. This includes fee-funded yield and extra rewards.

methodology.Fees: XAGm custody fees and redemption fees.
methodology.Revenue: XAGm custody and redemption fees accounted as protocol revenue.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: XAGm custody and redemption fees accounted as protocol revenue.

methodology.UserFees: Swap fees paid by traders only. External bribes are deposited by third parties to influence votes, so they are excluded here even though they count towards Fees.
methodology.Fees: Per-pool swap fee read from PoolFactory.getFee (default vAMM 0.30% / sAMM 0.05%, customizable per pool) applied to each swap, plus external bribes deposited by third parties to voter-incentive contracts.
methodology.Revenue: veRAPH voters’ take: staked-LP swap fees forwarded to voters plus external bribes. Equals HoldersRevenue — Raphael keeps no treasury cut of swap fees.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: Percentage of swap fees going to treasury
methodology.HoldersRevenue: Swap fees from staked LPs (fee × pool.balanceOf(gauge) / pool.totalSupply), forwarded to veRAPH voters, plus external bribes.
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: Swap fees kept by unstaked LPs (fee × (1 − stakedShare)). LPs who stake in the gauge forgo these fees in exchange for RAPH emissions.
methodology.Volume: Swap volume across Raphael Exchange (non-CL) pools, counted once per swap from the core-asset side.

methodology.Fees: 2% protocol fee charged on each settlement (jobs via escrow, campaigns via campaign vault), paid in USDC/USDT to the protocol fee recipient.
methodology.Revenue: 100% of protocol fees (2% of settlements) go to the protocol fee recipient.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: Same as revenue — the full 2% settlement fee.

methodology.Fees: 1% pool swap fee on every trade, accruing to permanently locked Uniswap V4 positions and periodically swept to creators and the protocol, plus a 0.0005 ETH launch fee paid at each token deployment.
methodology.Revenue: 30% of collected swap fees credited to the treasury claimable balance, plus the full 0.0005 ETH launch fee paid to the protocol treasury at launch.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: 30% of collected swap fees credited to the treasury claimable balance, plus the full 0.0005 ETH launch fee paid to the protocol treasury at launch.
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: 70% of collected swap fees credited to the creator claimable balance when fees are collected and allocated.

methodology.Volume: Swaps on bonding curves launched through Archade, plus swaps routed through the Archade app to other venues.
methodology.Fees: Trading fees paid by users on swaps routed through the Archade app, plus bonding curve trade fees and pool creation fees on coins launched through Archade. Fees after a coin graduates to a DEX pool are not included yet.
methodology.UserFees: Same as Fees. Every fee is paid by a trader or a coin creator.
methodology.Revenue: Archade's platform fee on app swaps, its share of bonding curve trade fees, and its share of pool creation fees.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: Same as Revenue. All of it goes to the Archade treasury.
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: Fees paid to coin creators, affiliate partners and the bonding curve program.
methodology.HoldersRevenue: None. Archade has no token.

methodology.Fees: Total yields from deposited assets in all curated vaults.
methodology.Revenue: Yields are collected by curators.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: Yields are collected by curators.
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: Yields are distributed to vaults depositors/investors.

methodology.Fees: SOL fees paid by users for Rapid Launch token deployment and trading tools.
methodology.Revenue: 86% of collector fees, kept by Rapid Launch after the 14% referral split.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: 86% of collector fees, kept by Rapid Launch after the 14% referral split.
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: 14% of collector fees, distributed to referral recipients.

methodology.UserFees: Traders pay a 1.5% fee on the quote-asset leg of every swap in a SolStocker pool. The pool's own LP fee is zero — the SolStockerFeeHook takes the whole fee.
methodology.Fees: The 1.5% swap fee charged by SolStockerFeeHook on every swap in a SolStocker-launched Uniswap v4 pool, read per swap from the five slices of the FeeCharged event and denominated in the pool's quote asset (a tokenized equity such as SPCX or NVDA). There is no launch fee and no graduation fee.
methodology.Revenue: The 0.30% platform slice plus the 0.15% slice owed to STOCKER holders — 0.45% of the trade, 30% of the fee.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: The 0.30% platform slice of the swap fee — 20% of the fee.
methodology.HoldersRevenue: The 0.15% slice accruing to holders of STOCKER, SolStocker's own token — 10% of the fee. It accrues to a dedicated recipient separate from platform revenue and is settled to STOCKER holders on Solana.
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: The 1.05% routed to third parties — 0.75% to holders of the launched coin, 0.15% to that coin's creator and 0.15% to the trader rebate pool.

methodology.Fees: Everything borrowers pay: the flat fee charged when a loan is opened or extended, penalties paid when a loan is cured after its grace period, and the protocol's cut of any appreciation on yield-bearing collateral. Lodestar charges no interest, so nothing accrues over the life of a loan.
methodology.Revenue: The portion of the above kept by the protocol: the reserve cut of borrower fees, plus all penalties and all collateral yield skim.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: The portion kept by the protocol, routed to the first-loss reserve that absorbs settlement shortfalls before lenders do.
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: The portion of borrower fees paid through to lenders in the USDT0 pool, taken from the amount the loan book actually locks for them rather than recomputed from the fee rate.

methodology.Fees: Interest paid by borrowers
methodology.Revenue: Percentage of interest going to treasury
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: Percentage of interest going to treasury
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: Interest paid to lenders

methodology.Volume: Volume of Hyperliquid HIP-4 outcome trades placed through the builder code.
methodology.NotionalVolume: Shares of HIP-4 outcome trades placed through the builder code, each valued at its $1 payout.
methodology.Fees: Builder-code fees paid by users on Hyperliquid HIP-4 outcome trades placed through the builder code.
methodology.Revenue: Builder-code fees on Hyperliquid HIP-4 outcome trades, all kept by the builder.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: Builder-code fees on Hyperliquid HIP-4 outcome trades, all sent to the builder's protocol.

methodology.UserFees: Swap fees paid by traders on every Ilyris swap.
methodology.Fees: Swap fees paid by traders on every Ilyris swap, a base fee per pool plus a variable fee that rises while the market is volatile.
methodology.Revenue: The protocol's share of swap fees (10% on every pool since launch), sent to the pool's fee recipient wallet.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: The protocol's share of swap fees (10% on every pool since launch), sent to the pool's fee recipient.
methodology.HoldersRevenue: Money going to governance token holders
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: The remaining 90% of swap fees, which stay in the bins and accrue to liquidity providers.
methodology.Volume: Value of tokens traders sold into Ilyris pools, fees included.
Settlement SwapExecuted (SYNC and SODAX opens) plus CoW, UniswapX, and Velora fills tagged to the Settlement fee recipient.
methodology.Fees: Settlement FeeCollected plus partner fees on tagged CoW, UniswapX, and Velora fills.
methodology.Revenue: 100% of Settlement, UniswapX, and Velora fees. 75% of CoW partner fees (CIP-75).
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: Same as revenue.
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: CoW's 25% CIP-75 share of tagged partner fees.

methodology.Fees: Loopr basket mint fees (paid in-kind by minters, in the basket's own constituent tokens), the LOOPR-token creator + protocol tax collected via launchpad hook, and ETH deposited into Loopr's community vault.
methodology.Revenue: Loopr's 30% cut of each basket's mint fee, the LOOPR token creator + protocol tax paid to Loopr's own wallet, and ETH deposited into Loopr's community vault.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: Loopr's 30% cut of each basket's mint fee, the LOOPR token creator + protocol tax paid to Loopr's own wallet, and ETH deposited into Loopr's community vault.
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: The 70% of each basket's mint fee paid to that specific basket's own (possibly third-party, permissionless) creator.

methodology.Volume: Volume of all swaps on Pez's launch curves. Graduated pools trade on Uniswap v4 and are counted under the Uniswap v4 listing.
methodology.Fees: Pez curve trade fees and creator taxes on every launched token, plus the graduated Uniswap v4 pool fees of the PEZ platform token, realized through PoolFeesSwept events. Other graduated pools are counted under the Uniswap v4 listing. Pez's current deployment has no launch fee.
methodology.Revenue: Protocol revenue plus holders revenue.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: Any protocol fee share read from the on-chain fee policy (zero under the current policy), plus the creator fees and taxes of the PEZ token, which the Pez team launched and collects on.
methodology.HoldersRevenue: PEZ buyback-and-lock amounts reported by PoolFeesSwept for the PEZ pool. No such buyback has happened on-chain so far, so this is currently zero.
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: Creator fee, creator tax, and launched-token buyback amounts paid from curve fees of third-party launched tokens.

methodology.Volume: Output amount of every swap routed through the SwapOnHood aggregator contracts.
methodology.Fees: 0.25% protocol fee per swap, taken in ETH when ETH/WETH is on either side, otherwise in the output token.
methodology.Revenue: All fees (0.25% of the swap volume) go to the protocol treasury.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: All swap fees(0.25% of the swap volume) are retained by the protocol treasury.

methodology.UserFees: Swap fees paid by traders. Locker distributions are not user fees.
methodology.Fees: Swap fees on the listed DLMM and DAMM factories plus WETH credited to U1 lockers. Excludes aggregator, keeper, flash-loan and liquidity-composition fees. DLMM uses SwapDetailed; DAMM uses changes in protocol and LP fee accumulators plus claims, in each historical fee token.
methodology.Revenue: The protocol's share of swap fees accruing to the fee recipient, plus WETH credited to U1 lockers (including external funding).
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: Gross protocol swap-fee share accruing to the fee treasury.
methodology.HoldersRevenue: Actual WETH distributions credited to U1 lockers (Base) by RewardsAdded, including external funding. Counted in Fees and Revenue at funding time, not again when users claim. No fixed forwarding percentage is assumed.
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: The share of swap fees that accrues to liquidity providers.
methodology.Volume: Sum of the input amount of every swap on Umbrae's DLMM (Liquidity Book style concentrated liquidity) pools on Base and Robinhood Chain and DAMM (dynamic-fee constant product) pools on Base. Pools are enumerated on chain from their factories and volume is read from each pool's swap events.

methodology.Fees: AMM swap commission only: for each hourly volume_bucket on factory pairs (reflective + cumulative), fee = offer_volume * live pair.commission_rate (fee asset = offer asset). Excludes token_bonding wrap/unwrap and converter pairs. $WESO cw20_bonding curve tax_collected is cumulative-only (project_tax_pct 10) with no time-bucketed query, so curve taxes are NOT included. Buckets retain at most 168 hours.
methodology.Revenue: fee_collector_share_permille of the AMM commission (live per pair; sampled pairs are 1000 = 100%) sent to fee_collector terra1wkdm6wcm4srahrvp09jea7csfq3yuacc4gmyft6p6n6pls9wy5js9lqhqq. No separate LP share of this commission field is counted — reflective pools may compensate LPs via the curve, not this commission — so SupplySideRevenue is omitted.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: Same as Revenue: at current on-chain shares the counted AMM commission accrues to the fee collector / protocol.
methodology.HoldersRevenue: Money going to governance token holders
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: Liquidity providers revenue

methodology.Fees: Trading commission collected on perp trades (funding payments excluded).
methodology.Revenue: Trading commission retained by the protocol after referral rebates (fees − rebates).
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: Trading commission retained by the Jetbit protocol treasury (fees − referral rebates).
methodology.HoldersRevenue: Fees going to governance token holders
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: Referral rebates — trading commission paid back out to referrers.
methodology.Volume: Real perpetual-futures notional (filled_quantity x filled_price) from Jetbit's public aggregate feed; copy-trade mirror volume and display padding are excluded.
methodology.OpenInterest: Live notional of all open positions (Σ |quantity| × mark price across open main and copy-trade positions), in USD, from Jetbit's public feed.

methodology.Fees: Taker trading fees: each market's taker_fee_ppm (0.1% on most markets) applied to that market's volume. Maker fees are not charged to takers and are excluded.
methodology.Revenue: All trading fees are collected by the protocol. Partner commissions and trader fee rebates are paid from the treasury after the fact and are not netted here.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: Same as Revenue: the protocol treasury receives all trading fees.
methodology.HoldersRevenue: Fees going to governance token holders
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: LPs revenue
methodology.Volume: Taker volume of all perpetual fills on the TRUE DEX venue (one fill counted once), summed per UTC day from the venue trade tape.

methodology.UserFees: Same as Fees; traders pay all three components.
methodology.Fees: Swap fees paid by traders on the protocol's BUCKET/ETH Uniswap v4 pool: the 1% LP fee plus the BucketFeeHook's 3% Treasury fee (FEE_BPS is a verified on-chain constant), both measured on the ETH leg of each Swap event; plus the Stockback router's 0.5% input fee (exact per-swap amount from its Swapped event).
methodology.Revenue: The hook's 3% Treasury fee, the 1% LP fee (the pool's liquidity is protocol-owned and permanently locked), and the protocol half of Stockback router fees.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: The 1% LP fee, accruing to the protocol's permanently locked liquidity position.
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: The trader's half of every Stockback router fee, credited back as stock rewards.
methodology.HoldersRevenue: The hook's 3% Treasury fee plus the protocol half of router fees: this is the stream the payout engine converts into tokenized stocks delivered to BUCKET holder wallets. Keeper gas for those deliveries is paid from this stream and varies with chain conditions; it is not modeled as a fixed split.

methodology.Volume: Sum of every buy and sell on Fox Brokers bonding curves (Buy/Sell events on curve contracts created by the launch factories), valued in USD with the protocol's on-chain oracle price of the curve's quote asset (a Robinhood Stock Token or WETH). Post-graduation SushiSwap V3 trading is not included here (it is tracked under SushiSwap).
methodology.Fees: Trading fees charged on every curve buy and sell (1% of the quote amount on the active preset: 0.8% creator, 0.2% protocol).
methodology.UserFees: Same as Fees: paid by traders on curve trades.
methodology.Revenue: Protocol share of curve trading fees (0.2%).
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: Protocol share of curve trading fees (0.2%).
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: Creator share of curve trading fees (0.8%), paid to the token creator's fee recipient.

methodology.Volume: Gross native SHIDO notional from Trade.nativeAmount on the production v2 bonding-curve factory, counting one side of each buy/sell. Buy refunds are excluded. No legacy-factory activity, BubbleSwap/router activity, post-graduation Shido DEX trading, LP activity or graduation liquidity is counted.
methodology.Fees: Actual protocol and creator trading fees from Trade, plus the graduationFee from Graduated. Accrual basis in native SHIDO, valued using its 1:1 WSHIDO wrapper. No fixed fee-rate estimates, claim double-counting, gas fees or post-graduation fees.
methodology.UserFees: Protocol and creator trading fees directly paid by bonding-curve traders. Graduation fees are excluded because they are deducted from the curve reserve before migration rather than charged directly to an end-user.
methodology.Revenue: Protocol trading fees plus graduation fees, excluding the creator trading-fee share and all post-graduation revenue.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: Same as Revenue (protocol trading fees + graduation fees): fees allocated to the protocol when accrued at the factory. Subsequent treasury spending or announced buybacks are not measured by this adapter.
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: Creator trading fees accrued by Trade events. This is creator income, not LP fees or revenue of holders of the Bubble Protocol token.

methodology.Fees: The protocol fee taken from every round's tile deposits (10% at launch, read per round from the RoundClosed event) plus the full winning bid of every weekly tile ad auction, paid in SOL or ATTN. Player deposits are paid out to winning bidders and are not counted.
methodology.UserFees: The round protocol fee paid by tile bidders plus the winning ad auction bids paid by advertisers in SOL or ATTN.
methodology.Revenue: The round protocol fee plus 10% of each winning SOL ad bid and all of each winning ATTN ad bid, sent to the protocol treasury.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: All revenue stays in the protocol treasury; its use (buybacks, staking rewards, build budget) is decided off-chain and not tracked here.
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: The 90% of each winning SOL ad bid forwarded into that tile's jackpot vault, paid to the tile's bidders on a jackpot hit.

methodology.Volume: Notional volume of Hyperliquid trades routed through AlphaPilot's builder code.
methodology.Fees: Builder code fees paid on Hyperliquid trades routed through AlphaPilot; excludes Hyperliquid exchange trading fees.
methodology.Revenue: Builder code fees collected by AlphaPilot from Hyperliquid trades.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: Builder code fees collected by AlphaPilot from Hyperliquid trades.

methodology.UserFees: Users pay fees on each swap.
methodology.Fees: Users pay fees on each swap.
methodology.Revenue: The protocol receives 20% of the fees paid by users.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: The protocol receives 20% of the fees paid by users.
methodology.HoldersRevenue: Money going to governance token holders
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: 80% of user jetton fees are distributed among LPs, based on the amount of user liquidity utilized in a particular swap.

methodology.Fees: Native ETH creator rewards claimed from PonsV2FeeEscrow for World is Flat ($WIF).
methodology.Revenue: 100% of claimed Pons creator rewards are retained by the WIF treasury.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: All claimed Pons creator rewards flow to the WIF treasury.

methodology.Fees: Everything borrowers and traders pay on gage: the deal or origination fee taken when a loan funds, trade fees on sold reclaim rights and lender units, the cash-out platform fee, and the borrower's fixed cost paid to lenders at repayment (repayment cap minus principal). Fixed-cost loans have no interest accrual: the cost is booked when the loan is repaid. Intent lend-asset generations lend a stock token, and their amounts are in that token.
methodology.Revenue: Deal, origination, trade and cash-out fees, the Earn performance fee on lender returns, and on Intent V1 the execution fee each fill takes from the partner vaults' return and the protocol's 10% of a partner vault's performance fee.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: The Earn performance fee (curator and protocol shares).
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: The borrower's fixed cost paid to lenders at repayment, before the Earn performance fee, the Intent execution fee and partner vault performance fees for loans an Earn strategy or a partner vault funded.
methodology.HoldersRevenue: Deal, origination, trade and cash-out fees, the Intent execution fee and the protocol's share of partner vault performance fees: since D57 every one of them buys GAGE for the permanent GAGE-only floor bands of the GAGE/sGAGE pool.

methodology.Fees: The protocol fee on every referral bounty that pays out: 10% of the reward, paid by the referrer.
methodology.Revenue: All protocol fees (10% of referral rewards) go to the ref_market treasury.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: All protocol fees (10% of referral rewards) go to the ref_market treasury.

methodology.Volume: Volume of bonding-curve (pre-graduation) swaps on Cook Market launched pools, measured in the pool's pair token. Post-graduation Uniswap v4 volume is excluded.
methodology.Fees: Swap fees (1% of the swap) and optional creator tax charged by the Cook hook on every swap, before and after graduation, there is no launch fee
methodology.Revenue: Part of the swap fees (protocolFeeShareBps, 10% at launch) sent to the Cook treasury
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: Part of the swap fees (protocolFeeShareBps, 10% at launch) sent to the Cook treasury
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: Remaining swap fees and 100% of the creator tax paid to token creators

methodology.Fees: Includes 2% property NFT sale fees and interest earned from property NFTs.
methodology.Revenue: Includes 2% property NFT sale fees and 10% of interest earned from property NFTs.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: Includes 2% property NFT sale fees and 10% of interest earned from property NFTs.
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: Includes 90% of interest earned from property NFTs paid to NFT owners.

methodology.Fees: The tax BaseStonk's Uniswap v4 hook takes on every swap in a launched token's pool, from the hook's FeeTaken event. Each launch sets its own buy and sell rate. A buy pays the tax in the launch token and a sell in the pair; token-denominated amounts are converted into the pair at the pool price the same transaction's Swap reports.
methodology.Revenue: The platform's cut of the tax plus what reaches BSTONK holders: half the tax capped at 1% of the trade to the treasury, any part of the creator's cut the payee list left unplaced and the hook swept to the treasury, and the share of the creator's cut paid to BSTONK's dividend distributor, to the BSTONK basket vault, or burnt as BSTONK.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: The treasury's take: half the tax capped at 1% of the trade, plus unplaced creator fees swept to it.
methodology.HoldersRevenue: Value to BSTONK holders, paid by the hook in the transaction the fee was taken: BSTONK's own pool pays its creator cut to BSTONK's dividend distributor and burns half of it, and launches carry the BSTONK basket vault as a payee; the vault pays BSTONK holders in rounds. Base only - BSTONK lives on Base.
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: The creator's cut of the tax less what the treasury swept and what reached BSTONK holders: the creator's wallets, the launch token's own holders through its dividend distributor, the burn of the launch token and the hook-owned liquidity wedge, as each launch configured them.
methodology.Volume: The pair side of every swap in a taxed pool, including the creator's dev buy at launch and excluding the hook's own buyback and liquidity swaps. Counted under Uniswap v4 as well.

methodology.Fees: 0.35% redeem fee on private transfers (withheld from the gross amount before zAssets are minted to the recipient, live since 2026-06-02) plus liquidity-based unwrap fees charged by the LiquidityManagers.
methodology.Revenue: All fees (redeem and unwrap) are retained by the protocol: the redeem fee is never minted, and unwrap fees accrue to the LiquidityManager fee surplus.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: All fees (redeem and unwrap) are retained by the protocol.

methodology.UserFees: Swap fees paid by traders only. External bribes are deposited by third parties to influence votes, so they are excluded here even though they count towards Fees.
methodology.Fees: Total swap fees paid by traders. Per-pool fee rate read from CLPool.fee() applied to each swap's input amount.
methodology.Revenue: veRAPH voters’ take: staked-LP swap fees plus the unstaked-LP rake (CLPool.unstakedFee), plus external bribes. Equals HoldersRevenue — Raphael keeps no treasury cut of swap fees.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: Percentage of swap fees going to treasury
methodology.HoldersRevenue: Fees earned by staked liquidity (CLPool.stakedLiquidity / liquidity) plus the rake taken from unstaked liquidity, forwarded to veRAPH voters, plus external bribes.
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: Swap fees kept by unstaked liquidity providers, net of the unstaked-LP rake.
methodology.Volume: Swap volume across Raphael Exchange Slipstream (CL) pools, counted once per swap from the core-asset side.

methodology.Fees: Everything users pay the protocol: the price of every cat minted, the trading fee the hook takes on the $HASH pool, and the secondary-market royalty the collection routes to the hook. The mint price is derived per cat from the contract's own curve - the number of cats created so far times PRICE_STEP - rather than read from a transaction value, so a mint sent with excess ether cannot inflate it.
methodology.UserFees: Same as Fees. Every one of the three flows is paid by a user: the miner pays the entry price, the trader pays the swap fee, and the secondary-market buyer pays the royalty.
methodology.Revenue: Fees minus the rent paid out to living cats.
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: Rent paid to the cats already alive. Every mint splits its price between the cats that came before it and the hook; cat holders are suppliers whose asset earns, not holders of a governance token, so their cut is a cost of revenue. Measured as the mint price minus the hook's cut, which is exact and needs no reconstruction from the rent accumulator.
