The hook's cut is what it was owed in the window rather than what it was sent: a transfer that fails its gas stipend is held in the collection's hookDue and forwarded later, so the change in that balance is added back.
methodology.HoldersRevenue: The share of revenue that joins the hook's buyback queue and is spent buying $HASH back on the pool and burning it. Measured at the fee source - the moment the hook receives and splits the money - rather than when a buyback executes, since the queue is drained gradually under a per-block cap.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: The developer's share of revenue, at the hook's devBps rate, read from the chain rather than hardcoded.

methodology.TransactionsCount: Transactions containing a completed Route swap (original engines, fee collectors, provider and builder executors, the Route v2 executors and RouteEntry, plus the Arc executor), counted once per transaction; quotes, pool hops and RouteEntry vault zaps are not counted.

methodology.Fees: Flat SOL fees paid by users to create a token, manage a token, create an OpenBook market and bulk send tokens on DexLab, received by the DexLab fee wallet on Solana.
methodology.Revenue: All fees (SOL paid by users to create a token, manage a token, create an OpenBook market and bulk send tokens on DexLab) are kept by DexLab. There is no supplier side and no token holder share.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: All fees (SOL paid by users to create a token, manage a token, create an OpenBook market and bulk send tokens on DexLab) are kept by DexLab. There is no supplier side and no token holder share.

methodology.Fees: The 1% hook fee and the ~3.33% tax PonsV2MemeHook charges on every swap of the genesis SHROOM/MU pool, read from the hook's own sweep events and denominated in MU after the hook converts the SHROOM side. Neither rate is assumed: both come from the events, and the split between Pons and the creator is read from the hook at the block being priced.
methodology.UserFees: Same as Fees. The hook fee and the tax are charged to swappers.
methodology.Revenue: SHROOM token revenue only: MU allocated for holder dividends in pool-filtered sweeps, excluding Pons. This is not treasury revenue and includes no treasury LP earnings.
methodology.HoldersRevenue: MU allocated to all SHROOM holders from creatorAmount, recognized at the hook sweep. Actual recipient payments can occur later. Treasury holders are included in this token-wide allocation, so do not add treasury dividend receipts again.
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: The 30% of the hook fee taken by Pons, the launchpad the token was issued through.

methodology.Fees: Treasury income only: earned fees from treasury-owned SHROOM LP positions plus actual MU dividend receipts. Token balances and returned LP principal are not income. All-holder SHROOM dividend allocations are reported separately in shroom.ts; do not sum the two scopes.
methodology.Revenue: Treasury income only: earned fees from treasury-owned SHROOM LP positions plus actual MU dividend receipts. Token balances and returned LP principal are not income. All-holder SHROOM dividend allocations are reported separately in shroom.ts; do not sum the two scopes.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: Treasury income only: earned fees from treasury-owned SHROOM LP positions plus actual MU dividend receipts. Token balances and returned LP principal are not income. All-holder SHROOM dividend allocations are reported separately in shroom.ts; do not sum the two scopes.

methodology.Volume: USDC wagered: both stakes of every market at the moment they lock into escrow (a market is only created on-chain once fully matched). This is betting volume, not deposits — funding a balance is not counted, only money committed to a bet. Each dollar is counted exactly once: the two stakes come from two different bettors, so this is the pot, not the maker/taker double count an orderbook has to halve. Cancelled markets refund the stakes, but the matched notional stays counted, in line with other prediction markets.
methodology.Fees: Protocol fee plus judge fee, both charged on the pot when the winner claims.
methodology.Revenue: The protocol fee share of claims, paid to the protocol fee collector.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: The protocol fee share of claims, paid to the protocol fee collector.
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: Judge fees paid to the human judges who resolve bets.
methodology.HoldersRevenue: Zero. There is no token.

methodology.UserFees: Percentage of rewards paid to protocol
methodology.Fees: Commission charged by the validators kHYPE delegates to, on the staking rewards they produce for kHYPE.
methodology.Revenue: The half of that commission Kinetiq invoices back to each validator operator (invoice_rate_bps, 5000 to date).
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: From 2026-04-09, 30% of the invoiced amount is kept by the treasury; it was 100% before.
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: The half of the commission the validator operators retain for running the nodes.
methodology.HoldersRevenue: 70% of the invoiced amount, used to buy back KNTQ for sKNTQ holders from 2026-04-09.

methodology.Fees: Sum of `fee` fields from `OptionExercised` (settlement fee on each exercised leg) and `PositionClosed` (matched-pair close fee). Both are charged at `1 / sf_fee_divisor` of the exercised/closed collateral and paid in USDC.
methodology.Revenue: Equal to Fees (sum of `OptionExercised` and `PositionClosed` fees): the protocol has no governance token, and every fee is transferred to the on-chain `feeCollector_address` (which the owner can rotate via `setFeeCollector` / `FeeCollectorChanged`).
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: Equal to Fees (sum of `OptionExercised` and `PositionClosed` fees): the protocol has no governance token, and every fee is transferred to the on-chain `feeCollector_address` (which the owner can rotate via `setFeeCollector` / `FeeCollectorChanged`).
methodology.HoldersRevenue: Fees going to governance token holders
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: LPs revenue
methodology.NotionalVolume: Sum of `amount` from each `optionIssued` event on StochasticOptions: USDC collateral committed by writers when minting a paired (long + short) position. Following the Prodigy/Dopex/Rysk convention of counting raw token amount (no oracle multiplication), this is the unit count of options minted — `1 USDC = 1 option unit` per protocol design.
methodology.PremiumVolume: Sum of USDC paid by option buyers on SFSwapV0Pair AMM pools, direction USDC→tradeToken only (the `amount0In` field of each `Swap` event). The reverse direction (tradeToken→USDC) is a writer unwinding their previously-sold leg and does not count as new premium inflow. Pair addresses are discovered from `PairCreated` events on the factory (one-time event per (token, tokenId) tuple).

methodology.Fees: Trading fees paid in KNTQ on Hyperliquid spot, which is the side of a KNTQ trade the HIP-1 deployer's share applies to.
methodology.Revenue: All of the trading fees paid in KNTQ on Hyperliquid spot. deployerTradingFeeShare on KNTQ is 1.0, so the deployer keeps the whole KNTQ-denominated fee.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: All of the trading fees paid in KNTQ on Hyperliquid spot. deployerTradingFeeShare on KNTQ is 1.0, so the deployer keeps the whole KNTQ-denominated fee.

methodology.Fees: 5.5% platform fee on marketplace resales + 2.5% platform fee on rental payments + the 2.5% creator royalty on resales, which is passed through to the original creator rather than kept by the protocol.
methodology.Revenue: Only the treasury-bound platform fees (resale + rental). Excludes the creator royalty.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: All treasury-bound platform fees (5.5% on resales and 2.5% on rentals). There is no token-holder split.
methodology.Volume: Gross marketplace trade value: secondary sale prices plus rental payments.
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: The 2.5% creator royalty on resales, paid to the original creator, not the protocol treasury.

methodology.Fees: Curve mode: 1% base fee plus optional creator tax on every bonding-curve buy/sell, plus the flat (owner-adjustable, re-read live) launch fee, plus post-graduation Uniswap v4 pool fees realised at sweep. Instant-v4 mode: the 1% LP fee of SolonPad's own plain Uniswap v4 launch pools, realised when the permissionless FeeSplitter crank forwards it.
methodology.Revenue: Curve mode: the protocol's share of curve fees (per-token policy, read live) plus all launch fees. Instant-v4 mode: the ~50% of LP fees forwarded to the platform treasury.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: Same as Revenue.
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: Curve mode: the creator and buyback-vault shares of curve fees, the full creator tax, and the creator/buyback share of post-graduation pool fees. Instant-v4 mode: the ~50% of LP fees forwarded to the launch creator's BeneficiaryVault position.

methodology.Fees: Swap fees paid by traders: each swap's amount times its pool's fee rate. Pools with a dynamic-fee plugin set the rate inside every swap without emitting it, so the rate is read from slot0 at the end of each hourly window.
methodology.Revenue: The protocol's share of swap fees, set per pool and per token in basis points of the fee.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: The protocol's share of swap fees.
methodology.HoldersRevenue: Money going to governance token holders
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: The part of swap fees the protocol does not take, which accrues to liquidity providers.
methodology.Volume: Every swap on a Lunya pool, from Swap events.
Pre-bonding curve buys and sells. Graduated pool swaps are counted under Lunya DEX.
methodology.Fees: Creation fees, curve trading fees, anti-snipe surcharge, graduation fees, and leftover quote at graduation. Excludes Lunya DEX swap fees.
methodology.Revenue: Creation fees, the protocol share of curve fees, the full anti-snipe surcharge, graduation fees minus the trigger reward, and leftover quote at graduation.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: The same as Revenue.
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: Creator share of curve fees, and the graduation trigger reward.

methodology.Volume: Volume of all buys and sells on Surged bonding curves. Swaps in graduated Uniswap pools are excluded.
methodology.Fees: Launch fees, curve trading fees, snipe tax, creator tax and swap fees from graduated Uniswap v3 pools (realised when swept).
methodology.Revenue: All launch fees plus the protocol share of curve trading fees, snipe tax and graduated pool swap fees.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: All revenue goes to the protocol fee recipient.
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: The creator share of curve trading fees, snipe tax and graduated pool swap fees, plus the full creator tax.

methodology.Fees: Trading fees from Peach bonding-curve trades and the launchpad's cut of graduated-pool LP fees, including creator tax, counted once when the fee accrues. Fees without a USD price are excluded.
methodology.Revenue: The platform's own share of fees, after creator, partner, referral and launched-token buyback shares.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: Same as Revenue - all of it goes to the protocol.
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: Creator, partner and referral shares of fees, plus the share allocated to launched-token buybacks. These launched tokens are not the Peach governance token.

methodology.Fees: Everything traders pay copyfomo on every copied buy and sell (a 2% service fee plus the gas copyfomo fronts for them, billed back as one stablecoin transfer to the copyfomo treasury, counted on the day the fee is collected), plus the creator fees of the copyfomo token $COPY: the Pons launchpad hook takes 3% of every swap of the COPY/COIN pool on Robinhood Chain, of which 2.7% goes to the creator (1% hook fee, 70% to the creator, plus a 2% creator tax). Counted on the day of the trade, valued at the hourly COIN price. The fees are swept into COIN by Pons and claimed by copyfomo in batches later; the claims are not what is counted.
methodology.UserFees: The part paid by copyfomo users: service fee plus gas billed back. Excludes the $COPY creator fees, which are paid by $COPY traders.
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: Referral rewards paid to copyfomo referrers, plus the actual on-chain cost copyfomo pays on users' behalf: the EVM bundler gas and the SOL spent by the Solana fee payer (transaction fees and token-account rent).
methodology.Revenue: Fees minus SupplySideRevenue, i.e. after the EVM bundler gas, the Solana fee payer cost and referral rewards: the service fee plus copyfomo's margin on gas, plus the $COPY creator fees (the 'token fees' figure on copyfomo.com/data). The 'protocol fees, after gas' figure on copyfomo.com/data is the service part before referral rewards.
methodology.HoldersRevenue: Buyback & burn of $COPY, funded by the creator fees: what the copyfomo creator wallets pay (COIN or USDG) in every transaction where they buy $COPY from the pool and burn $COPY in the same transaction (the buyback account buys and burns in one user operation). Counted on the day of the buy, which follows the trades that generated the fees. A holder cashback leg (USDG distributed to $COPY holders) is planned and will be added when it goes live.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: Revenue minus HoldersRevenue: service revenue and the creator fees kept by copyfomo.

methodology.Fees: Fees paid by users on heks: a fee on every swap in a launched coin's pool, plus the flat fee a creator pays to launch one. The swap fee is charged in the pool's pair asset. It is the protocol fee — 1% in steady state, higher in a launch's first ten seconds to price out snipers — plus, on coins launched from V2.2 whose creator set one, a creator tax of up to 10%. Both are read from the vault's own events: Collected carries the protocol fee and its split, TaxCredited the creator tax.
methodology.UserFees: All fees are paid by users: the swap fee and the creator tax by traders, the launch fee by the creator.
methodology.Revenue: The protocol's 30% share of every swap's protocol fee, plus the launch fee in full. The creator tax is never shared with the protocol.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: The protocol's 30% share of every swap's protocol fee, plus the launch fee in full. There is no heks token, so none of this is distributed to holders.
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: The 70% of every swap's protocol fee that goes to the coin's creator, plus the creator tax in full on coins that set one. A creator can redirect both to the holders of their own coin at launch; they leave the protocol either way.

methodology.Fees: Actual MON fees accrued to the protocol treasury and sent to the buyback vault at round settlement, plus separately paid auto-bet gas subsidies. Excludes MON allocated back to players and does not count gross stakes as fees.
methodology.Revenue: MON round settlement fees retained by the treasury and buyback vault; excludes auto-bet execution fees paid to the gas-subsidy wallet.
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: User-paid auto-bet execution fees transferred to the execution wallet as gas subsidies, included in Fees but excluded from Revenue; measures the subsidy paid, not actual transaction gas expenditure.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: MON round fees allocated directly to the protocol treasury; excludes gas subsidies, the separate buyback budget and GONE inventory valuations.
methodology.HoldersRevenue: Successful GONE staking rewards funded by the buyback vault, valued in MON at the matching buyback's actual execution rate (MON spent / GONE bought), then priced in USD by the SDK. Includes pending rewards only when successfully funded; excludes mining allocations, no-staker treasury diversions, other funders and later claims. Execution-price valuation includes trading costs and is not an independent GONE market price.

methodology.Fees: USDC-side Uniswap V3 swap fees accrued on Tolly's locked launch pools. Excludes the project-token-side fee leg, which is burned outright but has no reliable USD price.
methodology.Revenue: The 10% protocol-treasury share plus the 9% spent buying and burning TOLLY.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: The 10% share paid to the treasury.
methodology.HoldersRevenue: The 9% share market-bought back into TOLLY and burned.
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: The 64% creator share, the 12% launched-token holder-reward share, and the 5% that buys and burns the launched token itself.

methodology.Fees: 1% total fee on every Sashimi bonding-curve trade, read directly from each trade's own fee amount, plus the flat 1 USDC launch fee. Excludes post-graduation Uniswap v3 fees, which are not yet tracked here.
methodology.Revenue: 60% of the curve trading fee, per the documented protocol/creator split, plus all launch fees.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: Same as Revenue.
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: 40% of the curve trading fee, paid to the token's creator.

methodology.Fees: 1% trading fee on RadarDEX Reflection-launch pools, always denominated in USDC regardless of the pool's own quote asset, read from each fee distribution event.
methodology.UserFees: Same as Fees: the full trading fee is paid by traders.
methodology.Revenue: None. RadarDEX takes no cut of Reflection-launch fees; the entire 1% goes to the launched token's holders and its deployer.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: None, for the same reason as Revenue.
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: The full 1% trading fee: 50% streamed to the launched token's holders pro-rata by balance, 50% to the deployer.

methodology.Fees: The full swap fee on every ubi.fun trade: the creator and protocol legs from FeeEscrow, plus the USDC-denominated half of referral payouts.
methodology.Revenue: The team's 15% share of the total swap fee, confirmed on-chain against a real PlatformFeeSplitter distribution.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: Same as Revenue.
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: The creator's fee share, the 24% daily USDC holder-pool dividend, and the USDC-denominated half of referral payouts.

methodology.Fees: The fee a V5 or V6 launch pool charges on each trade, taken by that launch's hook inside the swap itself and read from the hook's own event, so the rate is never assumed here. It is 1% at regime; an anti-sniper launch charges more on buys during its opening window, on a curve that decays over the first blocks - 95%, then 70%, 40% and 10% - before settling at the same 1%, while sells in that window pay the regime rate. The fee is taken in either the launched token or its quote asset, whichever side the trader paid in. Both generations are read: V6 only took over new launches, it did not stop V5's existing pools from trading. V1-V4 legacy launches (pre-hook, plain Uniswap v3 with a per-launch lock contract) are not covered.
methodology.Revenue: The protocol's share of each fee, which is a split of the fee and not a rate on the trade: it keeps 50% under the default split, 30% when the launch opted into Holder Rewards, and 10% of any fee taken during a launch's opening window, which has its own fixed split. All three are set by the contract and not adjustable after launch.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: The protocol's share of each fee, which is a split of the fee and not a rate on the trade: it keeps 50% under the default split, 30% when the launch opted into Holder Rewards, and 10% of any fee taken during a launch's opening window, which has its own fixed split. All three are set by the contract and not adjustable after launch.
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: Everything not kept by the protocol: the creator's share, the remainder streamed to the launched token's own holders via the Reward Vault on Holder-Rewards launches, and - on fees taken during the opening window - the 80% earmarked to the launch's Treasury Reserve, which buys the launched token back to burn it.

methodology.Fees: Every leg of aka.fun's per-trade fee distribution: platform, creator/RWA-treasury, referral, and community drop, in USDC.
methodology.Revenue: The platform's share: 20% of the fee with a referral, or 35% without one (the forfeited referral cut goes to the platform).
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: Same as Revenue.
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: The creator/RWA-treasury share, the community drop share, and the referral payout when present.

methodology.Fees: Curve mode: flat 1% fee on every bonding-curve buy/sell, read from each trade's own gross USDC amount. Post-graduation: 1% swap fee on CircleWarp's own WarpDex pools (a custom Uniswap V2 fork), taken from whichever side of the swap is the input token. Token creation itself is free (no launch fee).
methodology.Revenue: Curve mode: 50% of the curve trading fee. Post-graduation: 30% of the WarpDex pool swap fee.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: Same as Revenue.
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: Curve mode: 50% of the curve trading fee, paid to the token's creator. Post-graduation: 30% of the pool swap fee to the creator, plus the 40% LP share that stays in the pool as reserve growth (the LP position itself is burned at graduation, so this permanently compounds into the pool rather than paying out to a live LP holder).

methodology.Fees: 1% swap fee on every trade of a launched token, creator-set buy/sell taxes on tax tokens, and the 1 USDC fee per token launch.
methodology.Revenue: 25% of swap fees plus token creation fees, kept by the protocol.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: Same as Revenue; ARK has no token, so nothing goes to holders.
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: 75% of swap fees plus all token taxes, paid to token creators.

methodology.Fees: The full USDC mint-settlement price paid by miners for every ArcLotls organism, read from the three downstream shares (rent, treasury, buyback) the mint payment is split into on-chain, which always sum to 100% of the mint price. Excludes the LOTL opening-trade tax (a one-time anti-snipe launch mechanic) and any undocumented trading-fee revenue not yet observed on-chain.
methodology.Revenue: Mint fees minus the share paid out as rent to NFT holders: the treasury share plus the share earmarked for the LOTL buyback-and-burn reserve.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: The treasury share of every mint (25% as observed on-chain).
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: The rent share of every mint (60% as observed on-chain), paid out to NFT holders weighted by organism stage. Accrued when funded, not when claimed.
methodology.HoldersRevenue: The share of every mint earmarked for buying LOTL back and burning it (15% as observed on-chain), measured at the fee source (when USDC lands in the buyback reserve) rather than at execution.

methodology.Volume: Swap volume on Tsunami's bonding-curve launches, all of which trade as Uniswap v4-style pools on Calamari's dedicated PoolManager on Ink, measured in each pool's quote currency
methodology.Fees: 1% swap fee charged by Tsunami's fee hook on every swap (buy and sell alike)
methodology.Revenue: The protocol's share of the swap fee: 100% before the creator-fee hook upgrade, then the documented default share (70% original factory, 99% second factory) after - a curve can be configured with a different split
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: Same as Revenue: all protocol-side fees go to the Tsunami treasury, there is no token holder distribution
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: The token creator's documented default share of the swap fee (30% original factory, 1% second factory) once the creator-fee hook was live - a curve can be configured with a different split

methodology.Fees: Total swap fee (LP + protocol) from each trade's Swap event.
methodology.Revenue: Protocol's cut of the swap fee, via v4-core's protocol-fee switch (0% until a pool is stamped, then up to 0.1% each direction).
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: Same as Revenue - Calamari has no token or holder distribution.
methodology.HoldersRevenue: Money going to governance token holders
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: Remainder of the swap fee, paid to LPs.
methodology.Volume: Swap volume on Calamari's own PoolManager on Ink, priced off the native/core-asset side of each trade.
Volume of all swaps on Wonk Fun launched pools (bonding-curve phase and post-graduation), measured in the pool's pair token (base)
methodology.Fees: Swap fees (currently 1% of the swap) and optional creator tax charged by the Wonk Fun hook on every swap, before and after graduation, there is no launch fee
methodology.Revenue: protocolFeeShareBps of the swap fees sent to the Wonk Fun treasury, currently 1%
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: All revenue goes to the Wonk Fun treasury, there is no token holder distribution
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: Remaining swap fees and 100% of the creator tax paid to token creators

methodology.Fees: Swap fees paid by traders, plus bribes paid to the protocol to attract AERO Rewards to pools.
methodology.Revenue: Swap fees earned by AERO-earning liquidity, the protocol share of fee-earning liquidity fees and bribes, all distributed to sAERO holders.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: Percentage of swap fees going to treasury
methodology.HoldersRevenue: Swap fees earned by AERO-earning liquidity, the protocol share of fee-earning liquidity fees and bribes, all distributed to sAERO holders.
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: Swap fees kept by fee-earning liquidity providers, and all fees of the original Aero Lite pools on Arc, which have no gauges.
methodology.Volume: Swap volume on Aero Slipstream (concentrated liquidity) pools, counting one side of each swap.

methodology.Fees: Trade fees on every buy/sell of Dynamito tokens (1-3% tier plus the anti-snipe surcharge in the first 5 seconds) and the 3% blast-off fee at graduation.
methodology.Revenue: 40% of trade fees plus 50% of blast-off fees, kept by Dynamito.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: Same as Revenue (40% of trade fees plus 50% of blast-off fees): all of it is kept by the Dynamito treasury. No token holder distribution yet; when the $TNT buyback programme starts, its share will be reported as HoldersRevenue.
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: 40% of trade fees and 50% of blast-off fees paid to creators, plus the 20% of trade fees paid to the Meteora protocol.

methodology.Fees: Trading fees collected by vibes.fun: the 1% platform fee on every trade against the Raydium LaunchLab bonding curves it configures, and, once a coin graduates, the quote-side trading fees of its permanently locked liquidity, harvested with the Fee Key vibes.fun holds. Raydium's own protocol fee is excluded. Amounts are in each pool's quote token.
methodology.UserFees: Same as fees, paid by traders.
methodology.Revenue: 30% of fees: the share vibes.fun keeps, split between its treasury and $VIBES buyback and burn.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: 15% of fees, sent to the vibes.fun treasury (Squads multisig).
methodology.HoldersRevenue: 15% of fees, used to buy back and burn $VIBES.
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: 70% of fees, paid to the holders of the coin that generated them, or to its creator when the creator chose creator fees.

methodology.Fees: All REP369 transaction tax paid by users. The adapter reads fee-component settings from the REP369 contract and applies on-chain fee-update events in chronological order.
methodology.Revenue: REP369 tax allocated to REP holder rewards plus the sell-side burn allocation. Automatic liquidity is treated as supply-side revenue.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: No separate protocol treasury fee is present in the current REP369 fee configuration.
methodology.HoldersRevenue: REP rewards plus the REP369 sell-side burn allocation.
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: The portion of REP369 transaction tax allocated to automatic liquidity.

methodology.Fees: All trading fees settled into FociFeeEscrow during the day (curve fees, creator tax, converted post-graduation hook fees, curve referral fees), plus hook referral fees claimed that day. Recognised when swept by the keeper, not when traded.
methodology.UserFees: Same as Fees: every fee is paid by traders on buys and sells.
methodology.Revenue: Protocol fee recipient's share plus the share paid to holder-reward distributors.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: Escrow credits to the protocol fee recipient (the protocol's frozen share of each launch's trading fee).
methodology.HoldersRevenue: Escrow credits to FociRewardsDistributor contracts — launches that elected to pay their creator share to token holders.
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: Escrow credits to creators (their fee share and the creator tax) and to referrers, plus hook referral claims.

methodology.Fees: LP fees earned by the TickerSpring vaults during the UTC day, including uncollected fees. V7 vaults: the change in cumulative harvested plus pending native-token fees from saved on-chain observations. Vaults that replaced V7 (listed by https://api.tickerspring.com/v1/merged/vaults): the fees their Harvest events collected plus the change in uncollected position fees, read on-chain at the day's first and last blocks. Excludes principal, stock-price returns, UP and RAM emissions, retired vaults and lending.
methodology.Revenue: Earned vault LP fees allocated to operations (10%) and the SPRING buyback reserve (20%), subject to raw-token rounding.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: The operations allocation of earned vault LP fees (10%).
methodology.HoldersRevenue: The allocation reserved to buy and permanently burn SPRING (20%), measured when vault fees accrue rather than when the buyback executes.
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: Earned LP fees retained for vault depositors after protocol allocations (approximately 70%).

methodology.Fees: The tax ArgusPad's per-launch hook charges on every buy and sell, the trading fee each launch's pool charges (on Portals 3-7 the 1% pool fee earned by the permanently locked launch position; on Portal 8 a 1% base fee the hook charges in the quote asset in its place), and the extra tax charged on buys in a launch's first seconds. Counted in the asset the fee is charged in, at the moment it is charged, so the protocol's later sale of the launched tokens it was paid is not counted a second time. Fees charged in the launched token itself (Portals 3-7 only; Portal 8 takes every fee in the quote asset) are reported in that token's own units and are priced only if DefiLlama has a price for it; it has none for these tokens today, because a launched token's only market is the pool ArgusPad seeded, and pricing it there overstates by about 40% against what ArgusPad's own sales of them actually realise.
methodology.Revenue: The share of fees reaching the ArgusPad treasury at the rate each launch fixes at creation - 10% of every fee on Portals 3-7 and 30% on Portal 8 - plus the whole of the early-buy snipe tax, which is paid straight to the treasury.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: The share of fees reaching the ArgusPad treasury at the rate each launch fixes at creation - 10% of every fee on Portals 3-7 and 30% on Portal 8 - plus the whole of the early-buy snipe tax, which is paid straight to the treasury.
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: The rest of the fees, which leave the protocol divided at the weights each launch fixed at creation: the token creator's share, the dividends paid to holders of that launched token, the share added back into the launch's permanently locked liquidity, the share used to buy and burn the launched token, and on Portal 8 the share used to buy the launched token and lock it permanently.

methodology.Volume: Gross quote-token value traded against DaWabLauncher bonding curves: fee-inclusive quote paid on buys plus gross quote redeemed from curve liquidity on sells. Post-graduation AMM swaps are excluded.
methodology.Fees: The 1.00% protocol trading fee paid on DaWabLauncher bonding-curve buys and sells, read directly from each trade event. DaWabLauncher charges no separate market-creation or graduation fee.
methodology.Revenue: All DaWabLauncher bonding-curve trading fees are retained as protocol revenue.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: All DaWabLauncher bonding-curve trading fees are allocated to the protocol.

methodology.Volume: Gross USDG crate spend (crate price + network fee on every open), no netting.
methodology.Fees: Crate spend net of instant-sell buyback payouts (Orderbook trades signed by the Treasury). Can be negative on heavy-buyback days.
methodology.Revenue: Treasury share of each open (crate price minus Pot contribution, plus network fee) minus buyback payouts. Gross of off-chain card fulfillment (every crate delivers a physical graded card).
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: Treasury share of each open (crate price minus Pot contribution, plus network fee) minus buyback payouts.
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: The Pot contribution of each open: a fixed bps of the crate price funding the community jackpot paid back to players.

methodology.Fees: Gross realized Vault yield above the high-water mark plus crystallized management fees. Yield is inferred by grossing up newly crystallized performance fees at each Vault's on-chain fee rate.
methodology.Revenue: Management and performance fee shares crystallized by MoneyFi, valued at the period-end net share price.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: Crystallized management and performance fees allocated to MoneyFi.
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: The remainder of crystallized gross performance yield allocated to Vault depositors after MoneyFi's performance fee.

methodology.Fees: 1% base fee on every bonding-curve buy and sell, plus the creator's optional tax, plus the anti-snipe tax charged in the first 3 seconds of a launch, plus a flat launch fee per token (read live from each chain's factory), plus 2% of the raise taken when a curve graduates to Uniswap v4.
methodology.Revenue: The protocol's share of the base curve fee (10% normally, 30% once a chain is past its first 100 launches), half of the anti-snipe tax, all launch fees, and the full 2% graduation fee.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: The protocol's share of the base curve fee (10% normally, 30% once a chain is past its first 100 launches), half of the anti-snipe tax, all launch fees, and the full 2% graduation fee.
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: The launch creator's share of the base curve fee (90% for the first 100 launches on a chain, 70% after), their full optional creator tax, and half of the anti-snipe tax charged on their token.

methodology.UserFees: Open fees and profit fees paid by traders.
methodology.Fees: Flat 0.5 USDG open fee per order unless refunded, plus a 5% fee on settled trader profits. Trader losses go to the treasury that backs payouts and are not counted as fees.
methodology.Revenue: Fees minus the builder carve; there are no liquidity providers.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: Revenue minus holders revenue.
methodology.HoldersRevenue: MOG bought back and burned by the buyback wallet, valued at the MOG price. 70% of profit fees accrue to that wallet; only the MOG it burns is counted.
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: Builder carve paid to the frontend that placed the order, out of the operations share.
methodology.Volume: Notional traded on mog perpetual markets: margin times leverage of every filled order, plus the notional of every trader close. Liquidations, payout-barrier exits and delist sweeps are not counted.
Bonding-curve USDC notional from Trade events. Native 18-dec amounts are converted to 6-dec Arc USDC. Post-graduation swaps on the Load routers are excluded.
methodology.Fees: 1 USDC create fee, 1% bonding-curve trade fee, and 0.25% Load router fee on Instant/graduated swaps.
methodology.Revenue: Protocol share: all create fees plus 20% of the 1% curve fee (0.20% of curve volume) plus Load router platform fees. The 5% launch-referrer cut of the create fee is included here because it is not emitted on-chain.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: All create fees plus 20% of the 1% curve fee (0.20% of curve volume) plus Load router platform fees. The 5% launch-referrer cut of the create fee is included here because it is not emitted on-chain.
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: 80% of the 1% curve fee to creators, plus trader-referral share of the 0.25% router fee.

methodology.Volume: Civilization anti-snipe pad PadBuy.quoteIn (WETH, Nightshades faction launches) + post-bond faction pool swaps (WETH-side notional of every user swap in the hooked Uniswap v4 faction pools; reopen-window buys grossed up by the same-tx SnipeTaxCollected; the vault's own night rebalances excluded).
methodology.Fees: The Civilization anti-snipe pad snipe tax on Nightshades faction curve buys (PadTaxCollected — 50% next-night boost pot / 10% faction pool / 13.33% StockBooster / 13.33% protocol / 13.34% game creator, WETH); the sunrise reopen snipe tax levied by the game hook on hooked v4 pool trades after each night (SnipeTaxCollected, same five-way split); the 1% LP fee on every user swap in the hooked faction pools (100% protocol-owned game liquidity — the vault is the pools' only permitted LP); and Nightshades faction NFT royalties (ERC-2981 10% of secondary sales) as flushed from the immutable FactionRoyaltySplitter (75% game vault survivor liquidity / 25% team).
methodology.Revenue: The 13.33% protocol treasury leg of the pad + sunrise reopen snipe taxes, and the 1% LP fee accruing to the protocol-owned faction pool liquidity.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: 13.33% of the pad + sunrise reopen snipe taxes → protocol treasury; the faction pools' 1% LP fee → the vault's protocol-owned game liquidity position (compounds into game LP, not distributed).
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: Pad + sunrise reopen tax legs to the next-night boost pot (50%), the faction's own locked pool (10%), StockBooster (13.33%) and the game creator (13.34%), plus both legs of the flushed NFT royalties.

methodology.Fees: Gross Uniswap V3 pool fees collected by every registry-listed Smart LP (Volatility Farming) vault (FeesCollected fees0/fees1).
methodology.Revenue: The $STONKBROKER-buyback half of the 10% performance fee.
methodology.HoldersRevenue: The $STONKBROKER-buyback half of the 10% performance fee.
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: 90% of vault pool fees auto-compounded to depositors plus the StockBooster Clock In dividend half of the 10% performance fee.

methodology.Volume: NFT AMM fills (ethFeePaid ÷ fee bps) and Stonk Interns paid mint releases (DormantReleased.ethPaid, the $20 ETH leg).
methodology.Fees: ETH fees on NFT AMM trades + NFT-backed loans; $STONKBROKER broker activation/upgrade fees; Stonk Interns mint fees (ETH leg, $STONKBROKER leg, $1 promotion fee) and intern activation fees; and the Relay swap-desk 1% app fee (Base USDC forwarded to StockBooster).
methodology.Revenue: 30% of NFTFi ETH fees, the full $STONKBROKER activation fee (burn + protocol), and the Stonk Interns protocol share (75% of the ETH mint leg, 100% of the STONK leg and promotion fee, the full intern activation fee).
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: 30% of NFTFi ETH fees → ProtocolFeeSink; protocol half of $STONKBROKER activation fees; Stonk Interns treasury legs and the protocol half of intern activation fees.
methodology.HoldersRevenue: Half of the $STONKBROKER broker and intern activation/upgrade fees burned.
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: 70% of NFTFi ETH fees → StockBooster stock dividends; 25% of the Stonk Interns mint ETH leg → intern Clock In payroll; Relay swap-desk 1% app fees forwarded to StockBooster.

methodology.Volume: Broker Box ticket notional (PullOpened.ticketWei) + sell-back payouts (SoldBack ethOut + SoldBackUsdg usdgOut) + Certificate Counter stock purchases (CertificateBought.spendWei).
methodology.Fees: Broker Box gachapon 10% edge (EdgeSkimmed) + the 5% sell-back spread retained in the machine bankroll + the Certificate Counter flat $2 fee.
methodology.Revenue: Broker Box protocol accrual (5% of ticket) + sell-back spread + the treasury half of the Certificate Counter fee.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: Broker Box protocol accrual + sell-back bankroll spread + the treasury half of the Certificate Counter fee.
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: Broker Box creator + booster edge (5% of ticket on official machines) → StockBooster Clock In stock drops, plus the StockBooster half of the Certificate Counter fee.

methodology.Volume: Safe Launch / Stonklauncher window buys AND sells on every pad generation (V1 ETH, V1 quoted, V2, r2 — buy = tax-inclusive quoteIn/ethIn, sell = quoteOut/ethOut + taxPaid, quote-token denominated on quoted/WETH lanes) + anti-snipe WallBought.ethIn + StonkCurvePool Trade.quoteAmount on the bonding-curve launcher.
methodology.Fees: Safe Launch / Stonklauncher snipe tax on window buys and sells across all pad generations (16.5% creator / 16.5% protocol / 50% locked-LP or ICO Bonus / 17% StockBooster + Clock In Card referrers); the anti-snipe fair-launch snipe tax (time-decay tax on launch-curve buys, 90% StockBooster / 10% launch dev); and StonkCurvePool 1% trade fees (33/33/33 waterfall).
methodology.Revenue: The 16.5% protocol leg of the Safe Launch / Stonklauncher snipe tax and 33.34% of bonding-curve trade fees.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: 16.5% of the Safe Launch / Stonklauncher snipe tax → protocol accrual; 33.34% of bonding-curve trade fees → protocol.
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: Safe Launch tax legs to the launch creator (16.5%), StockBooster + Clock In Card referrers (17%), and the permanently locked LP reserve / ICO Bonus (50%); 90% of the anti-snipe launch tax → StockBooster dividends and 10% → launch dev; bonding-curve creator (33.33%) + StonkBrokers Directed Clock In / pot (33.33%).

methodology.Fees: Token creation, bonding-curve trading (including any launch-window surcharge), Genius hook trading and paid Alpha promotion fees. Fees accrue at launch/trade/promotion; settlements are excluded. Meme-denominated hook fees use the same swap’s quote/meme execution-price ratio, rounded down to quote base units.
methodology.Revenue: The Genius platform share of trading fees under each launch’s immutable policy, plus separately labeled creation and Alpha promotion fees. The creator-selected destination allocation (Foundation or creator), creator share and launched-meme buyback allocations are excluded.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: The same protocol-retained portion as Revenue. Genius.fun has no protocol token receiving these fees.
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: Creator-selected destination allocations (Foundation or creator), creator shares and accrued funding for buybacks of individual launched meme tokens, calculated from immutable per-launch policies with contract integer rounding.

methodology.Fees: Every USDC a user pays the protocol: the 1% trade fee on the USDC side of each trade, on the bonding curve and in the graduated token's Uniswap v4 pool alike; the fee to create a token (1 USDC at deployment); the snipe tax on buys in a token's first 120 blocks; and the USDC left over once a graduating token's Uniswap v4 pool has been seeded.
methodology.Revenue: The platform's share: 0.30% of a trade where the trader has a referrer bound on chain and 0.50% where they do not, plus all launch fees, all snipe tax and the graduation dust.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: Same as Revenue (0.30% of a trade where the trader has a referrer bound on chain and 0.50% where they do not, plus all launch fees, all snipe tax and the graduation dust). There is no protocol token, so nothing is distributed to holders.
methodology.HoldersRevenue: Money going to governance token holders
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: 0.50% of every trade to the token's creator and 0.20% to the trader's referrer, both claimable from the FeeManager.

methodology.Fees: The 1% Uniswap V3 LP fee earned by every locked LIFT v1 launch position, counted in the pool's quote asset when the position's fees are harvested (token-side fees burned by the first-generation locker are excluded), plus the flat fee paid for every token launch.
methodology.UserFees: Swap fees paid by traders of LIFT v1 tokens and launch fees paid by token deployers.
methodology.Revenue: The LIFT treasury share of harvested swap fees plus all launch fees.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: The LIFT treasury share of harvested swap fees plus all launch fees.
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: The token creator share of harvested swap fees, fixed per position when it is created.
methodology.HoldersRevenue: No fees are distributed to holders of a protocol token.

methodology.Fees: Fees the LIFT v2 hook takes in the pool's quote asset (USDC or EURC) on every swap of a LIFT v2 token: the base fee, including the anti-snipe surcharge in a launch's first blocks, plus the fee each creator sets for buys and sells. Counted when the swap happens, plus the flat fee paid for every token launch.
methodology.UserFees: Swap fees paid by traders of LIFT v2 tokens and launch fees paid by token deployers.
methodology.Revenue: The LIFT treasury share of the base fee plus all launch fees. LIFT takes no share of the creator swap fee.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: The LIFT treasury share of the base fee plus all launch fees. LIFT takes no share of the creator swap fee.
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: Everything else goes to the creator side of each launch: the rest of the base fee and the whole creator swap fee, split by the launch's fixed settings between the creator, buyback and burn of the launched token, dividends to holders of the launched token, and liquidity added to the launch's locked pool.
methodology.HoldersRevenue: No fees are distributed to holders of a protocol token.

methodology.Volume: Notional volume of Hyperliquid perpetual trades placed through WatchCrypto's trading terminal.
methodology.Fees: Builder code fees paid by users on Hyperliquid perpetual trades placed through WatchCrypto; excludes Hyperliquid exchange trading fees.
methodology.Revenue: Builder code fees collected by WatchCrypto from Hyperliquid perpetual trades.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: Builder code fees collected by WatchCrypto from Hyperliquid perpetual trades.

methodology.UserFees: Same as Fees; every fee is paid by the trader.
methodology.Fees: All swap fees paid by traders on Arctide pools, in USDC: the pool's LP fee, its protocol fee (set by the token creator) and Arctide's fixed 0.25% treasury fee, read from the Router's SwapExecuted events.
methodology.Revenue: Arctide's 0.25% treasury fee on every swap, plus the protocol fees of the pools whose protocol recipient is Arctide itself (the $TIDE and $DUCK pools).
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: 30% of Revenue, retained by Arctide.
methodology.HoldersRevenue: 70% of Revenue, used to buy back and burn $TIDE.
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: LP fees credited to liquidity providers, plus protocol fees paid to token creators' chosen addresses.
methodology.Volume: USDC size of every swap on Arctide pools, read from the Router's SwapExecuted events (grossNative: USDC sent by the buyer, or USDC taken out of the pool by a sell, before fees). Bonding-curve trades on the launchpad are not included yet.

methodology.Fees: Pool swap fees paid by traders (pool-level swapFee × amount in).
methodology.Revenue: Protocol share of swap fees (ProtocolFeesCollector / ProtocolFeeController percentage read live from kiltr.net/api/fees).
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: Protocol share of swap fees, using the v2 or v3 percentage from kiltr.net/api/fees.
methodology.HoldersRevenue: Money going to governance token holders
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: Swap fees remaining with liquidity providers (Fees − Revenue).
methodology.Volume: Sum of swap amounts through Kiltr pools (subgraph daily snapshots; each swap counted once).

methodology.UserFees: Fees paid directly by Denaria users to Denaria: the GMX UI fee and the flat service fee. Affiliate rewards are excluded because they are a rebate out of the fee the trader pays to GMX.
methodology.Fees: Fees collected by Denaria: the GMX UI fee charged on Denaria orders, the affiliate reward earned by the DENARIA referral code on GMX position fees, and the flat per-operation service fee paid to the Denaria fee wallet. GMX position, borrowing and funding fees are not Denaria fees and are counted under GMX V2 Perps.
methodology.Revenue: All Denaria fees (GMX UI fees, affiliate rewards, service fees) are revenue.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: All revenue (GMX UI fees, affiliate rewards, service fees) accrues to the Denaria fee wallets.
methodology.HoldersRevenue: None: Denaria has no token.
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: None: Denaria has no liquidity providers of its own on GMX.
methodology.Volume: Notional USD size of every GMX V2 position increase or decrease on a Denaria position, from the PositionFeesCollected event: orders placed through Denaria (identified by the Denaria uiFeeReceiver) plus liquidations and ADL executed by GMX keepers on positions carrying the DENARIA referral code. Same basis as GMX V2 marginVolumeUsd; this volume is also counted by GMX V2 Perps.
Curve notional of every NFT fill on the Anvil 2 way desks: Buy.paid net of the protocol fee plus Sell.received grossed up by it, in each desk's quote token.
methodology.Fees: The 9.99% fee charged in the quote token on every desk fill (InternExchange FeeRouted toDesk + toEngine + toTreasury).
methodology.Revenue: The 9% treasury share of the fee.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: The 9% treasury share of the fee.
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: The 66% share paid to the desk whose staked liquidity filled the trade plus the 25% share routed to the Stonk Interns Clock In engine as dividends to activated intern NFT holders.

methodology.Fees: Token creation fees paid in STRK and extra trading fees charged by the original Launchy router.
methodology.Revenue: Creation fees plus Launchy's original router fee share. Launchy-created Ekubo pool fees are reported separately under Launchy Pools.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: All Launchy revenue is directed to the platform treasury.
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: Creator fees from the original Launchy router.

methodology.Fees: Swap fees generated in Launchy-created Ekubo pools. These fees are also reported by Ekubo.
methodology.Revenue: Launchy's 30% share of guarded-pool swap fees. The original pool has no Launchy LP share.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: Launchy's share of guarded-pool fees allocated to its treasury.
methodology.HoldersRevenue: Money going to governance token holders
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: Creator and Ekubo shares of Launchy-created pool swap fees.

methodology.Fees: What users pay to cross the bridge. The asset's controller on Arc charges the same rate in both directions - on the way in it mints the fee to the protocol and the rest to the user, on the way out it burns the gross and re-mints the fee - and an optional fast-lane router charges its own cut on top for skipping the queue, on the origin chain when depositing and on Arc when redeeming. Anything charged on Arc is taken in the claim token (bCRCL, bGLD, bUSDT, bBTCB), which is a 1:1 claim on the asset held in custody and is therefore valued as that origin asset; a fast-lane deposit is charged on the origin chain instead, before the asset becomes a claim, so it is taken in the origin token directly. Either way the fee is denominated in the same four origin assets.
methodology.Revenue: All the bridge fees and the fast-lane fees go to the protocol's treasury with nothing paid out of it.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: All the bridge fees and the fast-lane fees go to the protocol's treasury with nothing paid out of it.
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: None. The bridge has no liquidity providers - claim tokens are backed by custody reserves, not by a pool, so there is no supplier to pay.

methodology.Volume: Every Swapped event emitted by a Meow router, counted once per swap using the core-asset side of the trade (input amount when the input token is a core asset, otherwise the output amount delivered). Routers are read from MeowRouterRegistry at the end of the window; inner venue hops are not counted.
methodology.Fees: Meow's own output fee (0.25% by default, lower for wallets holding the configured token), taken from each swap's output and emitted as FeeCollected. Fees charged by the underlying pools are not included.
methodology.Revenue: All swap fees accrue to the Meow treasury.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: All swap fees are retained by the Meow treasury.
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: No part of the fee goes to liquidity providers, integrators or referrers.

methodology.UserFees: Same as Fees: every part is paid by users.
methodology.Fees: Creator tax on swaps of coins launched through Kicker pots (floor, launcher, buyback and platform parts) plus the 0.5% fee on pot deposits, in the pot's core asset.
methodology.Revenue: The platform shares (10% of taxes on coins launched with terms and the platform part of deposit fees) plus the core that pots spend buying and burning KICKER (Burn events with KICKER as the burned token). Creator tax onto pot floors is not revenue.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: The platform shares, received by KickerBuyer. KickerBuyer later spends them on KICKER buybacks and burns; that spend is not counted again.
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: Creator tax collected onto pot floors (accrues to pot depositors), launcher shares and buyback shares with any target but KICKER of taxes on coins launched with terms, and pot creator / referrer parts of deposit fees.
methodology.HoldersRevenue: Core that pots spend buying and burning KICKER, counted when the burn executes (Burn event, KICKER burned, tokens > 0), from the buyback share of taxes on coins launched with KICKER as their burn target. Pot shares (K) are redeemable vault shares, not a governance or value-accrual token, so floor accrual is not holders revenue.

methodology.UserFees: Swap fees directly paid by traders.
methodology.Fees: Concentrated liquidity swap fees paid by traders. Each swap is charged on its input amount at the dynamic CLPool.fee() in effect for that swap (read from the state right before the swap's block; 3000 means 0.30%), net of any registered tx.origin discount.
methodology.Revenue: Concentrated liquidity fees routed to veArchery voters through gauges, equal to HoldersRevenue.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: Percentage of swap fees going to treasury
methodology.HoldersRevenue: Voter fee share is measured from CLPool.gaugeFees() deltas plus CollectFees events and applied per token.
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: Concentrated liquidity provider fees not routed to veArchery voters.
methodology.Volume: Swap volume from Archery concentrated liquidity pools on Arc. Each swap is counted once on the pricing side of the pair.

methodology.Fees: Fees from the GAS/USO pool that reach Gas (95% of the swap tax and of the LP fee; Doppler keeps the other 5%), plus what players pay to buy NFT cars (in $GAS) and to repair them (in USO). The 15-minute launch sniper tax on 2026-09-23 (forwarded to a team wallet during the launch tax decay) is not counted.
methodology.Revenue: All car sales and repairs, plus the 25% of pool fees sent to the buybacks wallet.
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: Pool fees sent to the prize pool, which pays players in USO when they claim at gas stations (75% of pool fees since 2026-09-23 06:03 UTC, all of them before). The team sells the prize pool's $GAS into USO by hand.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: The treasury's 20% of car sales and all car repairs.
methodology.HoldersRevenue: Pool fees and car-sale shares sent to the buybacks wallet 0x18eD3E25Fb4786EA60021E2e9A2Da0A52602f503: 25% of pool fees, and 80% of car sales since 2026-09-23 05:59 UTC (paid in $GAS and held in that wallet). Buybacks are made by hand when the team decides and have not started yet. Before 2026-09-23 05:59 UTC the 80% car-sale share was burned.

methodology.Volume: Gross input amount (amountIn, before the TartSwap router fee) of every TartSwapExecuted event emitted by TartSwapRouterV2 on BNB Smart Chain. The router forwards the swap to PancakeSwap V2 and holds no liquidity of its own.
methodology.Fees: Router fee taken on the input leg of every swap through TartSwapRouterV2 (TartSwapExecuted.feeAmount, 35 bps by default, per-account custom fees possible). Excludes PancakeSwap's LP fee on the forwarded swap.
methodology.UserFees: Same as Fees: the router fee is paid entirely by the swapper.
methodology.Revenue: Share of the swap fee that TartFeeDistributor routes to the treasury and reserve legs, per its on-chain split() at the end of the period.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: Same as Revenue: the treasury and reserve swap fees are held by the protocol.
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: Share of the swap fee that TartFeeDistributor routes to the farm and staking reward legs, which are converted and streamed to LP and CREPE stakers.

methodology.Fees: 1% (100 bps) app fee charged on swaps routed through Relay, collected in USDC. Reported per origin chain of the swap.
methodology.Revenue: All app fees accrue to the Based protocol; there is no supply-side or holder share.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: Identical to Revenue: the full app fee is kept by the protocol.

methodology.Fees: All stock- and launched-token-denominated swap charges in V1 and V2 V4 pools, including opening-period charges and caller incentives; all V2 bonding-curve trading fees and opening-window token burns; plus launch fees. Token charges are recorded in raw units and contribute to USD totals only when DefiLlama pricing supports them; missing prices leave USD coverage incomplete. Excludes strategy profits and buybacks, Uniswap LP fees, external routing fees, and Pons/$HEDGE taxes.
methodology.Revenue: The designated protocol share of stock trading fees on the curve and in pools as they accrue, the creator share of launches made by the protocol recipient itself, plus launch fees; excludes royalties of other creators and launched-token strategy allocations.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: The same protocol allocations as Revenue, including earned but unswept or unclaimed amounts.
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: Stock trading fees less the protocol allocations go to creators, strategies and sweep callers; all launched-token charges go to token burns and sweep callers, with no platform revenue. Token amounts require DefiLlama price coverage for USD inclusion.

methodology.Fees: USDC creation fee paid by users to create an AI agent on Arc through the Fuci agent factory (1 USDC per agent at launch; read from each AgentCreated event), plus the fee on escrow jobs paid out to an agent (1% of the job at launch; read from each FuciEscrow Released event), plus Fuci Launch trading fees: the 1% Uniswap v4 LP fee on every swap in a launch pool and the snipe tax on early buys.
methodology.UserFees: Users pay all of the fees.
methodology.Revenue: Creation fees, escrow fees and the Fuci Launch snipe tax (all sent to the Fuci treasury, a Safe multisig), plus Fuci Launch LP fees paid in $FUCI, which are all burned.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: Creation fees, escrow fees and the Fuci Launch snipe tax, all sent to the Fuci treasury (a Safe multisig).
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: Fuci Launch LP fees paid in the launched token. They are burned too, which benefits that token's holders.
methodology.HoldersRevenue: $FUCI burned by the Fuci launchpad's collectAndBurn, which collects each launch's LP fees and burns them, usually once a day.

methodology.Fees: 2% performance fee on the realised profit of each copied position, charged only on profitable closes.
methodology.Revenue: The 0.8% of realised profit kept by the protocol, measured directly as USDG transfers into the treasury.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: The 0.8% of realised profit kept by the protocol, measured directly as USDG transfers into the treasury.
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: The 1.2% of realised profit paid to the copied trader (leader), derived from the fixed fee split.

methodology.UserFees: Swap fees paid by traders on every swap.
methodology.Fees: Swap fees paid by traders, taken from each Swap event's swapFeeAmount. The Vault charges the fee on the input token; it is booked on the same leg as the volume. When that leg is the output token (a non-core token sold for a core asset), the fee is converted at the trade's own rate, amountOut * swapFeeAmount / amountIn - no external price is used. The amount is exact; only its denomination changes. Because amountIn includes the fee itself and the trade's average rate is slightly worse than the pool's marginal rate, the converted fee reads low by about the pool's fee rate plus the trade's own price impact - a share of the fee, never of volume, and always in the under-counting direction.
methodology.Revenue: The protocol's share of the swap fee, read per pool from the protocol fee controller.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: Same as Revenue - the protocol's share of the swap fee goes to the protocol fee controller.
methodology.HoldersRevenue: Zero - no part of the fee is distributed to token holders today.
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: The rest of the swap fee: the part that stays in the pool for liquidity providers, plus the pool creator's share when a pool creator has set one.
methodology.Volume: Value swapped through the Ranges Vault, counted once per trade from the core asset leg when the trade has one, otherwise from the token sold into the pool.

methodology.Fees: Interest paid by Alula borrowers plus operation fees on deposits, withdrawals, borrows, repayments and collateral moves.
methodology.Revenue: The take rate on borrower interest (set per pool) plus operation fees, paid to the protocol and its insurance fund.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: The take rate on borrower interest (set per pool) plus operation fees, paid to the protocol and its insurance fund.
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: Borrower interest net of the take rate, earned by lenders.

methodology.UserFees: Same as Fees: what the trader paid on each swap.
methodology.Fees: Two things the trader pays. The pool fee on each swap - two of these pools run Ellipse's market-hours hook and charge 1%, 2% or 3% depending on whether the underlying market is open or shut, so for those the rate is read from the swap itself rather than assumed, and the rest are fixed at creation. Plus Ellipse's own 0.5% on swaps routed through its front end, read from the event its fee collector emits when it is emptied, which reports what actually reached the treasury rather than what was sent.
methodology.Revenue: Ellipse's 0.5% interface fee, kept in full. It is charged on every swap routed through its front end, which is a wider set than the pools whose volume is reported here, so it is not 0.5% of that volume and should not be read as a rate on it. It is dated when the collector is emptied rather than when each swap paid it; a keeper does that hourly.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: Ellipse's 0.5% interface fee, kept in full. It is charged on every swap routed through its front end, which is a wider set than the pools whose volume is reported here, so it is not 0.5% of that volume and should not be read as a rate on it. It is dated when the collector is emptied rather than when each swap paid it; a keeper does that hourly.

methodology.SupplySideRevenue: The pool fee, which goes to the liquidity providers.

Launchpad launches are not counted: those pools are opened for other people's tokens on Uniswap's shared PoolManager, so their volume belongs to that DEX.

methodology.SupplySideRevenue: Fees paid to NFT depositors, builder rewards, and the FWA rewards and caller incentive paid from buybacks.

methodology.Fees: The full native-USDC entry price accepted for every BoneYard NFT mint, read from Boneyard's Minted.price event. Excludes BONE genesis reserve, BONE emitted by burns, secondary royalties, and hook swap levies.

If seedLiquidity diverts bootstrap that cannot be paired with BONE into the Hook buyback reserve, that previously booked protocol revenue is reclassified out on BootstrapDivertedToBuyback. Hook-bound revenue is 100% of each of the first eight genesis mints and 35% of later mints.
methodology.HoldersRevenue: Native USDC allocated by Hook.BuybackAccrualAdded from post-LP mints for market-buying and burning BONE, plus any pre-LP bootstrap reclassified to that reserve by BootstrapDivertedToBuyback at liquidity seeding. It is counted when funded, not when the owner executes the capped buyback. BONE is the protocol's own value-accrual token.

methodology.Revenue: All swap fees go to the Felynx treasury.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: All swap fees go to the Felynx treasury.

methodology.Revenue: All commission (2.5% of converted proceeds and of the LP fees their orders earn), paid to the TickerSpring treasury.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: All commission (2.5% of converted proceeds and of the LP fees their orders earn), paid to the TickerSpring treasury.
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: LP fees earned by order liquidity, net of commission, credited to order makers.

methodology.ProtocolRevenue: The protocol's share of trading fees plus the launch fees in full.

First, the fee a trader paid on a swap in a pool the plugin runs in, at the rate the plugin set for that swap; the plugin takes no share of that fee, so nothing of it is charged to the user on the protocol's behalf. Second, the arbitrage the plugin realised inside the pool and paid out, read from the ProfitDistributed event where a deployment settles through a distributor and from the donatedToLps leg of ProfitShared where the plugin pays the pool's liquidity providers directly.
methodology.Revenue: The protocol's share of the captured arbitrage, taken from the distributor's own share config as it stood at the block of each capture. Nothing of the swap fee is the protocol's, and the captures donated straight to liquidity providers leave it nothing either.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: The protocol's share of the captured arbitrage, taken from the distributor's own share config as it stood at the block of each capture. Nothing of the swap fee is the protocol's, and the captures donated straight to liquidity providers leave it nothing either.
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: The swap fee in full, which the pool's liquidity providers and its AMM earn, plus the part of every capture that the share config pays to the pool's beneficiaries.

methodology.Fees: All yield generated by Arrowfarm concentrated liquidity vaults: LP trading fees and gauge rewards harvested by the strategies, the performance fee charged on them, and trading fees sent straight to the treasury.
methodology.Revenue: Performance fees charged on harvests (arrow fee and strategist fee, paid in WETH) plus trading fees that strategies send to the treasury. The harvest caller fee is not counted as revenue.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: Strategist performance fees and trading fees sent to the Arrowfarm treasury.
methodology.HoldersRevenue: The arrow performance fee in WETH is sent to the ArrowBuybackBurner, which buys ARROWFARM and burns it.
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: Yield that stays with vault depositors after the performance fee (LP trading fees and gauge rewards), plus the harvest caller fee paid to whoever calls harvest.

methodology.Fees: Hyperliquid builder code fees paid by users on perpetual trades placed through GDEX.
methodology.Revenue: Hyperliquid builder code fees collected by GDEX. Referral rewards GDEX later pays out off-chain from its treasury are not deducted.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: Hyperliquid builder code fees collected by GDEX. Referral rewards GDEX later pays out off-chain from its treasury are not deducted.
methodology.HoldersRevenue: Fees going to governance token holders
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: LPs revenue
methodology.Volume: Notional volume of Hyperliquid perpetual trades (including HIP-3 markets) placed through GDEX.
Notional volume of Hyperliquid trades routed through Hypercall's builder code.
methodology.Fees: Builder code fees paid on trades routed through Hypercall; excludes Hyperliquid trading fees.
methodology.Revenue: Builder code fees collected by Hypercall on those trades.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: Builder code fees retained by Hypercall on those trades.

methodology.Fees: The total trading fees paid by users, excluding L1 transaction fees. Only the 50 largest SundaeSwap pools by current TVL (across all versions) are counted, and the same current set is used for past dates, so pools that were large in the past but are not in today's top 50 are excluded.
methodology.Revenue: A fixed ADA cost per transaction that is collected by the protocol. Only the 50 largest SundaeSwap pools by current TVL (across all versions) are counted, and the same current set is used for past dates, so pools that were large in the past but are not in today's top 50 are excluded.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: The share of the fixed ADA cost per transaction kept by the treasury: 85% since May 2024, 100% before. Only the 50 largest SundaeSwap pools by current TVL (across all versions) are counted, and the same current set is used for past dates, so pools that were large in the past but are not in today's top 50 are excluded.
methodology.HoldersRevenue: The share of the fixed ADA cost per transaction going to holders: 15% since May 2024, 0% before. Only the 50 largest SundaeSwap pools by current TVL (across all versions) are counted, and the same current set is used for past dates, so pools that were large in the past but are not in today's top 50 are excluded.
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: A percentage cut on all trading volume, paid to Liquidity Providers. Only the 50 largest SundaeSwap pools by current TVL (across all versions) are counted, and the same current set is used for past dates, so pools that were large in the past but are not in today's top 50 are excluded.

methodology.UserFees: Traders pay all of the fees above.
methodology.Fees: Every trade pays the pair swap fee (0.30%) to liquidity providers, a 0.70% Motoswap protocol fee on the quote side, and on coins that graduated from moto.fun a 0.30% creator fee.
methodology.Revenue: The whole 0.70% protocol fee: the shares for MOTO stakers, MOTO buyback and burn, the treasury and the Rakeback program.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: The treasury share and the Rakeback program share of the 0.70% protocol fee.
methodology.HoldersRevenue: The share of the 0.70% protocol fee paid to MOTO stakers plus the share used to buy back and burn MOTO.
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: The 0.30% pair fee to liquidity providers and the creator fee to coin creators.
methodology.Volume: Volume of swaps on Motoswap pairs, read from the pair Swap events of every pair created by the Motoswap factory. Pairs quoted in MOTO are measured on their MOTO side, valued at the Motoswap MOTO/WETH pair price.

methodology.UserFees: Same as Fees - traders pay all of it; liquidity providers are not charged.
methodology.Fees: Everything traders pay on a swap: the pool's swap fee from the Swap event (protocol fee included), plus what a Latch launch pool's guard takes itself - the creator tax, and on newer launch guards the guard's part of the trade fee - read from the guard's TaxTaken and FeeTaken events. Only Latch's own launch guards are read.
methodology.Revenue: What reaches the protocol, counted when the fee is taken: the protocol fee each Swap event carries; the protocol's share of a launch pool's liquidity fees under the pool's permanent LP lock split, only where the locks provably hold all of the pool's liquidity; and the protocol's share of the creator tax and guard trade fee under the split the guard stores for that pool. A split that cannot be read is never guessed: that amount is left out of Revenue.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: All of Revenue. Latch has no token, so nothing is diverted to holders.
methodology.HoldersRevenue: Money going to governance token holders
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: Fees minus Revenue: swap fees earned by liquidity providers, and the shares of locked-liquidity fees, creator tax and guard trade fees that go to launch creators and integrators (and any guard-taken amount whose split could not be read).
methodology.Volume: Gross input of every swap on CLPoolManager and BinPoolManager, one leg per swap. Swaps in Latch's own test tokens (LTT1/LTT2 on Robinhood Chain) are excluded: they have no market and no price.

methodology.Fees: Aerodrome LP fees distributed to MAMO stakers.
methodology.Revenue: Aerodrome LP fees distributed to MAMO stakers.
methodology.HoldersRevenue: Aerodrome LP trading fees distributed to MAMO stakers via the multi-rewards contract.

methodology.Fees: Integrator fee TRNCH adds to swaps and bridges made on TRNCH (0.5% on a single swap, 1% on a swap of a token from the TRNCH Heat ranking or on a basket of swaps, 1% on bridges, 0.5% on swaps built through the TRNCH Bot API and MCP server for AI agents), paid to the TRNCH treasury Safe through LI.FI, KyberSwap, 0x, Uniswap, SushiSwap and 1inch. Router and DEX fees are excluded.
methodology.UserFees: Users pay the full TRNCH integrator fee.
methodology.Revenue: All integrator fees received by the TRNCH treasury Safe are kept by TRNCH.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: All integrator fees go to the TRNCH treasury.

methodology.Volume: Native coin paid on buys and received on sells on ADEXTO bonding curves, gross of fees. Trades by the ADEXTO team's own wallets are excluded.
methodology.Fees: All swap fees paid by traders on ADEXTO bonding curves, read from each Swap event: the creator, curve reserve, buyback and protocol legs. Rates are set per market at launch and never change; the launch presets are 1.00% on factory 1.0.0 and 0.12.0 markets and 0.40% on factory 0.11.0 markets.
methodology.UserFees: All swap fees paid by traders.
methodology.Revenue: The protocol leg of every swap, paid to the ADEXTO protocol treasury: 0.10% of the trade on factory 0.11.0, 0.12.0 and 1.0.0 markets, where it is a factory constant. Factory 0.10.0 markets have no protocol leg.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: The protocol leg of every swap, paid to the ADEXTO protocol treasury: 0.10% of the trade on factory 0.11.0, 0.12.0 and 1.0.0 markets, where it is a factory constant. Factory 0.10.0 markets have no protocol leg.
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: The creator leg paid to each market's creator, the reserve leg that stays in the market's curve, and the buyback leg that buys and burns the market's own token.

methodology.Fees: Borrow origination, repayment and explicit liquidation fees, and lending entry and exit fees, valued in USD when charged.
methodology.Revenue: All of the fees (Borrow, Repay, Deposit, Withdraw); the protocol keeps them in full.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: All of the fees (Borrow, Repay, Deposit, Withdraw): 77% is set aside for $LOAN buybacks at token launch and 23% goes to the treasury. No buyback has executed yet; holders revenue will be reported once they do.
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: Interest paid to lenders

methodology.Fees: Carriers pay XNET for mobile data offloaded onto WiFi. Until settlement arrives, Fees are conservatively accrued from measured daily offload. Closed unsettled months use XNET's official monthly projection and newer days use a conservative API-GB rate. Carrier payments typically settle about two months later, and historical accrual is reconciled to the amount actually paid.
methodology.Revenue: Carriers pay XNET for mobile data offloaded onto WiFi. Until settlement arrives, Fees are conservatively accrued from measured daily offload. Closed unsettled months use XNET's official monthly projection and newer days use a conservative API-GB rate. Carrier payments typically settle about two months later, and historical accrual is reconciled to the amount actually paid.
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: Passed XIP-13.1 lets designated operators choose fiat instead of token distributions. Their 75% operator cash share is Supply-Side Revenue and is attributed to the service month reconciled by the carrier settlement that funds the payout, preserving the observed NET60+ settlement cadence.
methodology.HoldersRevenue: Accrued service-period tokenholder allocation. Historically 80% of ordinary carrier Fees accrued to buyback-and-burn; under passed XIP-12, 60% does. The XIP-13.1 fiat slice contributes its 5% facilitation/BBB allocation. Values are provisional wherever the underlying Fees are provisional and reconcile with settlement. This is accrual attribution; actual on-chain buyback or burn execution can occur later.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: Historically 20% of ordinary carrier Fees was allocated to operations. Under passed XIP-12, Protocol Revenue is 40%: 20% operations and 20% protocol-owned liquidity. For the XIP-13.1 fiat slice, 20% is retained for XNET operations.

methodology.Fees: Builder fees received by crotrade from trades on Polymarket v2
methodology.Revenue: Builder fees received by crotrade from trades on Polymarket v2
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: No builder fees are kept by crotrade
methodology.HoldersRevenue: Builder fees received by crotrade, all distributed to its token holders

methodology.Revenue: All trading fees; no share goes to liquidity providers.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: None, all trading fees go to CRONUS holders.
methodology.HoldersRevenue: All trading fees go to CRONUS holders through buybacks: distributed to holders before 2026-09-22, burned since.

methodology.Fees: Actual quote-asset swap charges emitted by the verified TaxHook FeesAccrued event. V1 launches charge no trading tax. No token mint allocation, gas, deposits, claim payments or buyback execution is counted as a new fee.
methodology.Revenue: Treasury allocation of each fee on an accrual basis; excludes creators, referrers and launched-token buybacks.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: The same treasury allocation as Revenue. Fledgo has no own-token holder revenue.
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: Creator recipients, attributed referrers and launched-token buyback allocations. Missing referrers retain their allocation for creators. Buybacks benefit the launched token, not a Fledgo governance token.
