methodology.Fees: Yield from RealFi's reserve portfolio (treasury bills, money market funds, CLO ETFs, floating-rate bonds and private credit), counted when it is minted on-chain as new USDrf at each weekly staking epoch, net of portfolio losses burned from the sUSDrf staking vault. Excludes income RealFi earns off-chain on unstaked USDrf reserves that is never minted on-chain. Mint and redeem fees are currently 0 bps.
methodology.Revenue: Share of each epoch's minted yield sent to the RealFi protocol fee address instead of the sUSDrf staking vault.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: Share of each epoch's minted yield sent to the RealFi protocol fee address instead of the sUSDrf staking vault.
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: Share of each epoch's minted yield added to the sUSDrf staking vault, which raises the USDrf redeemable per sUSDrf, net of portfolio losses burned from the vault.

methodology.Fees: ZC burned by users to publish in the Book, relay fees on private posts, payments and withdrawals, and deposit vetting fees of the ZC privacy pool. The launcher share of Stockereum's swap fee on ZC trades is a token tax and is not counted.
methodology.Revenue: All fees: burns accrue to holders, the rest to the protocol; no supply-side payments except relay fees earned by third-party relayers.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: Relay fees earned by the team-run relayer and deposit vetting fees kept by the Entrypoint.
methodology.HoldersRevenue: ZC permanently burned by users to post.
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: Relay fees on zipcoin Entrypoint withdrawals submitted by relayers other than the team's.

methodology.Volume: Stablecoin amount of every completed P2P trade, read from the VailoxEscrow EscrowComplete events. Each trade is counted once (the off-chain fiat leg is not added) and cancelled or refunded trades are excluded.
methodology.Fees: Escrow fees paid by sellers and buyers on completed P2P trades, read from EscrowComplete events. Fees are tiered by trade size (fixed fee below 50 USD, then 1.25% down to 0.25%) with a lower rate for verified merchants. Cancelled or refunded trades pay no fee.
methodology.UserFees: All escrow fees are paid directly by the trading users.
methodology.Revenue: All escrow fees are kept by the protocol.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: All escrow fees go to the protocol treasury.

methodology.Fees: Everything PeddleQuest charges: the fee quest creators pay on top of the reward pool they deposit, the flat quest creation fee, the protocol's share of rewards that winners did not claim before the deadline, payments for trending and banner promotion slots, and the fee users pay to mint an optional completion badge.

methodology.Revenue: All fees (quest creation, deposit, unclaimed, promotion and badge) are kept by the protocol. Quest rewards themselves go to winners and are not counted as fees or revenue.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: Fees (quest creation, deposit, unclaimed, promotion and badge) accrued to the protocol treasury (a Safe multisig).
methodology.HoldersRevenue: The share of badge mint fees routed on-chain to buyback and burn. Zero while that route is switched off, which it has been since launch.

methodology.Fees: 0.5% protocol fee on shielded pool deposits and 0.5% on withdrawals (Ethereum, Base, BNB Chain, Robinhood Chain, Solana), deposit check fees on Solana, plus ZEC rewards received by the Nullmask team wallet from MASK token holder distributions (Solana).
methodology.Revenue: 0.5% protocol fee on shielded pool deposits and 0.5% on withdrawals (Ethereum, Base, BNB Chain, Robinhood Chain, Solana), deposit check fees on Solana, plus ZEC rewards received by the Nullmask team wallet from MASK token holder distributions (Solana).
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: 0.5% protocol fee on shielded pool deposits and 0.5% on withdrawals (Ethereum, Base, BNB Chain, Robinhood Chain, Solana), deposit check fees on Solana, plus ZEC rewards received by the Nullmask team wallet from MASK token holder distributions (Solana).

methodology.Fees: Lock creation fees paid by users to Titan Locker, read from FeeCollected events on every lock manager: a flat ETH fee, or a share of the deposited token for ERC-20 and vesting locks.
methodology.Revenue: All lock creation fees go to the Titan Locker fee receiver.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: All lock creation fees go to the Titan Locker fee receiver.
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: No fees are shared with liquidity providers or other parties.
methodology.HoldersRevenue: Titan Locker has no token, so no fees go to token holders.

methodology.Fees: Copy trading fees fomo-mcp users pay on every copied buy and sell (1% on copies under $100, 0.5% from $100), plus the creator fees of the fomo-mcp token $FOMOMCP on the Pons launchpad.
methodology.UserFees: Copy trading fees paid by fomo-mcp users. Excludes the $FOMOMCP creator fees, which are paid by $FOMOMCP traders.

methodology.ProtocolRevenue: All fees (copy trading fees and $FOMOMCP creator fees) are kept by fomo-mcp.

methodology.ProtocolRevenue: Launchpad fee kept by Crystal after the token creator's split.
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: Launchpad fee paid to the token creator.

methodology.Fees: USDW trading fees accrued to the protocol, measured as the increase in FeeRouter.totalPlatformFees() on each chain where Wager Predict is deployed.
methodology.Revenue: The same increase in FeeRouter.totalPlatformFees(). That counter is the platform's collected trading fees.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: The increase in FeeRouter.totalPlatformFees() kept by the protocol.

methodology.Fees: Fees charged on bets in every V5, V6 and V7 room: the room stakers' fee (V5 / V6), the platform fee and the room creator's fee.
methodology.UserFees: Fees charged on bets, paid by players.
methodology.Revenue: The platform fee on bets, sent to the ElcasTreasury (V5) or the ElcasBurner (V6, V7).
methodology.HoldersRevenue: The ElcasTreasury / ElcasBurner swaps the platform fee to $ELCAS and burns it.
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: The fee kept by each room's pool for its stakers and the fee paid to each room's creator.

methodology.UserFees: Open and close fees and borrow paid by traders.
methodology.Fees: Open and close fees (a share of the position size, set per market) and hourly borrow paid by traders.
methodology.Revenue: The platform's share of open and close fees (currently 10 %), accrued for the platform's fee address.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: The platform's share of open and close fees, accrued for the platform's fee address.
methodology.HoldersRevenue: Fees going to governance token holders

methodology.OpenInterest: Long and short position size open in every market at the end of the period.

methodology.UserFees: The fee taken from each settled round's losing side.
methodology.Revenue: The platform's share of each round's fee (currently 1 % of the losing side).
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: The platform's share of each round's fee, accrued for the platform's fee address.
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: The market's house vault LPs, the market's creator and whoever settles the round (bounty).

methodology.Fees: Platform fees, integrator app fees and swap costs paid by users on Relay bridges and swaps, excluding execution costs (network gas).

methodology.ProtocolRevenue: Platform fees kept by Relay. This is an upper bound: Relay pays qualifying integrators an undisclosed 0-67% revenue share out of it.

methodology.Revenue: AlfaClub's platform key-trading fee, room-token launch fees and 15% of room-token swap fees, plus the creator shares in AlfaClub's own room, the room behind the ALFA token.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: AlfaClub's platform key-trading fee, room-token launch fees and 15% of room-token swap fees, plus the creator shares in AlfaClub's own room, the room behind the ALFA token.
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: Creator key-trading fees, plus 85% of room-token swap fees: 50% to the room's keyholders and 35% to the creator. Creator shares in AlfaClub's own room count as Revenue instead.

methodology.Revenue: Mosh's share of the creator fees (creatorFeeShareBps, 20% at launch), the raise fee (raiseFeeBps, 5% of the filled raise), and, where the Mosh treasury holds a bundle's fee claims itself, its pro-rata part of the backers' share.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: Mosh's share of the creator fees (creatorFeeShareBps, 20% at launch), the raise fee (raiseFeeBps, 5% of the filled raise), and, where the Mosh treasury holds a bundle's fee claims itself, its pro-rata part of the backers' share.
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: The bundle backers' share of the creator fees (80% at launch), including any team share a bundle's creator set out of it, less the part the Mosh treasury holds as a backer.

methodology.Fees: 2% fee on realized PnL at close, 2% fee on margin lost in liquidations, and LP profits above the $5M cap swept to PAPER stakers. Trader wins and losses that stay in the LP are not counted.
methodology.Revenue: All fees: half of the 2% fees to PAPER stakers, half to the dev fee recipient, and LP profits above the $5M cap to PAPER stakers.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: Half of the 2% close and liquidation fees, paid to the dev fee recipient.
methodology.HoldersRevenue: Half of the 2% close and liquidation fees plus LP profits above the $5M cap, paid in USDC to PAPER stakers.
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: LPs revenue

methodology.Volume: Notional volume of Hyperliquid perpetual trades (including HIP-3 markets) placed through Auspex.
methodology.Fees: Hyperliquid builder code fees paid by users on trades placed through Auspex; excludes Hyperliquid's own trading fees.
methodology.Revenue: Builder code fees collected by Auspex. Referral rewards Auspex later pays out from its treasury are not deducted.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: Builder code fees collected by Auspex. Referral rewards Auspex later pays out from its treasury are not deducted.

methodology.UserFees: Open and close fees and borrow paid by traders.
methodology.Fees: Open and close fees (a share of the position size, set per market) and hourly borrow paid by traders.
methodology.Revenue: The protocol's share of open and close fees (currently 10 %), collected in the protocol's FeeVault.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: The protocol's share of open and close fees, collected in the protocol's FeeVault.
methodology.HoldersRevenue: Fees going to governance token holders
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: The rest of the open and close fees and all borrow go to each market's LP vault; the market's creator takes up to 20 % of the open and close fees.
methodology.Volume: Notional of positions opened plus notional closed (full and partial closes, take profit / stop loss), across every margin token's book.
methodology.OpenInterest: Long and short position size open in every market at the end of the period.

methodology.UserFees: All swap fees are paid by the swapper.
methodology.Fees: Swap fee charged on the output token of each swap (protocol share plus LP share), read from the Swapped event. The coverage toll a swap may pay when it drains a leg below its coverage floor stays in the leg's reserves as a buffer and is not counted.
methodology.Revenue: Protocol share (protoFee) of the swap fee. Zero on coop fills, which book no protocol fee.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: The protocol share (protoFee) of the swap fee goes to the BTR treasury.
methodology.HoldersRevenue: Money going to governance token holders
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: LP share (lpFee) of the swap fee, accrued to the liquidity providers of the output leg.
methodology.Volume: Input-token amount (amountIn) of every swap on BTR pools, read from the pool Swapped event and counted once per swap. Includes the protocol's own coop-arbitrage fills (CoopArb): they are real pool swaps that pay an LP fee, and while they were the only flow the series read zero.

methodology.Fees: SOL service fees paid by users to Tsunammi for the Create Token flow.
methodology.Revenue: All tracked Create Token service fees are retained as Tsunammi protocol revenue.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: SOL received by Tsunammi's dedicated Create Token fee collector.

methodology.Volume: The USDC side of every swap on the bonding curves of tokens launched with Ryntra Launch (Meteora DBC pools on its configs, created by its pool payer), from the swap events. Trading after a token graduates is Meteora DAMM v2's volume and is not counted. Double counted: Meteora already lists this volume.
methodology.Fees: Everything traders pay on the bonding curves of tokens launched with Ryntra Launch (Meteora DBC pools on its configs, created by its pool payer), including the 20% Meteora keeps; after graduation, the referral fee Meteora pays Ryntra on trades made through Ryntra; and what Ryntra takes as the partner of a graduated curve (its share of the migration fee, and later the fees of the DAMM v2 liquidity locked for it) when its fee claimer withdraws them. The creator's share of the migration fee and the quote above the graduation threshold (not a fee) are not included.
methodology.UserFees: What traders pay: the bonding curve fee, the referral fee Ryntra earns on graduated-pool trades and the graduated pool's fees; not the migration fee, which comes out of the curve's reserve.
methodology.Revenue: Ryntra's 60% of the configs' share of the bonding curve fee, the referral fees Meteora pays it, and its graduation income when withdrawn.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: Ryntra's 60% of the configs' share of the bonding curve fee, the referral fees Meteora pays it and its graduation income, all of it for the protocol: Ryntra has no token and distributes nothing to holders.
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: The token creator's 40% of the configs' share of the bonding curve fee, Meteora's protocol fee, and the referral fees Meteora pays other apps.

methodology.Volume: One side of every trade made through Ryntra. On Solana, from the trader's own token movements in the trade: the stablecoin they paid or received, else the SOL, else the token they paid — gross of Ryntra's fee (a fee taken from what they received is added back). On Arc, from the swap's own events: the side in USDC, EURC, WETH or cirBTC of a KyberSwap swap, gross of the router's fees (the amount the fee was taken from), and the input a trader sent Circle's swap Adapter. A trade is Ryntra's when it paid Ryntra's fee inside it. Trades on the bonding curve of a token launched with Ryntra are counted under Ryntra Launch. Double counted: the venues the trades are routed through already list this volume.
methodology.Fees: Fees people pay Ryntra on trades made through it. On Solana: what the swap router (Jupiter, or DFlow when Jupiter routes through it) pays into Ryntra's fee wallet and its Jupiter referral account inside the trade. On Arc: the developer fee of a Circle swap and the fee leg of a KyberSwap swap that name Ryntra's fee address, read from Circle's fee collector and KyberSwap's router events. Plain transfers into these accounts are not fees.
methodology.UserFees: Fees traders pay Ryntra inside the trades they make through it.
methodology.Revenue: Trading fees kept by Ryntra: the whole fee paid into its fee wallet on Solana and from KyberSwap on Arc, what reached its Jupiter referral account less Jupiter's 20% share, and the Circle developer fee less the share (about 10%) Circle's fee collector routes to its protocol recipient. Cashback and invite rewards are paid later, when people claim them, and are not deducted.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: Trading fees kept by Ryntra, all of it for the protocol: Ryntra has no token and distributes nothing to holders.
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: Jupiter's 20% share of the fees that reached Ryntra's Jupiter referral account, and the share (about 10%) of the Circle developer fee that Circle's fee collector routes to its protocol recipient on Arc.

methodology.Volume: Total stake matched each day, read from the SX Bet V3 escrow's fill events. Every bet is funded by both sides, so both stakes are counted.
methodology.Fees: Commission SX Bet takes on the profit of winning bets, counted when the escrow pays it to SX's fee wallet at settlement. On V3 the rates are set per account and can apply to singles as well as parlays; losing and voided bets pay nothing.
methodology.Revenue: Commission taken from the profit of winning bets and kept by SX. Market makers get none of it.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: All commission goes to SX: first a fee wallet, and from 4 September 2026 the treasury contract that also holds the SX community fund.
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: Zero. Market makers get no share of the commission.

methodology.Volume: SOL paid by buyers and SOL paid out to sellers on the bonding curves, before fees.
methodology.Fees: Everything charged on the launchpad: DEEP's fee on each bonding-curve buy and sell (1.25%), the reward fee a token's creator chose at launch (0% to 5% of each trade), the fee to launch a token ($2, paid in SOL) and the migration fee taken from the SOL a curve raised when its token graduates (1%, less the network rent of the new pool's accounts).
methodology.Revenue: DEEP's share: its 1.25% fee on bonding-curve trades, the token launch fees and the migration fees. Reward fees are not included.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: DEEP's 1.25% fee on bonding-curve trades, the token launch fees and the migration fees, all paid into DEEP's on-chain fee vault, which pays 10% to the team that builds DEEP and 90% to the DEEP treasury.
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: The reward fee of each token, paid in full to the token's creator or, for a Holder Rewards token, to the holders of that token.

methodology.Fees: Everything charged on DeepSwap: the swap fee (0.35% of a buy and 0.75% of a sell), the reward fee the pool charges on top of it (0% to 5%, fixed when the pool was created) and the flat fee in SOL to open a pool. Pools of graduated launchpad tokens are opened by the launchpad, which pays that fee out of the token's migration fee; it is reported with the launchpad, not here.
methodology.Revenue: DEEP's share of the swap fee (0.25% of a buy, 0.65% of a sell) and the pool creation fees.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: DEEP's share of the swap fee (0.25% of a buy, 0.65% of a sell) and the pool creation fees, all paid into DEEP's on-chain fee vault, which pays 10% to the team that builds DEEP and 90% to the DEEP treasury.
methodology.HoldersRevenue: Money going to governance token holders
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: The liquidity providers' share of the swap fee (0.10% of each swap, left in the pool) and each pool's reward fee, paid in full to the pool's creator or, on a Holder Rewards pool, to the holders of the pool's token.
methodology.Volume: The quote-token side (SOL on a TOKEN/SOL pool) of every swap, before fees.

methodology.Fees: Swap fees paid by users
methodology.Revenue: Percentage of swap fees going to treasury and/or token holders
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: Percentage of swap fees going to treasury
methodology.HoldersRevenue: Money going to governance token holders
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: Liquidity providers revenue

methodology.Fees: Swap fees paid by users
methodology.Revenue: Percentage of swap fees going to treasury and/or token holders
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: Percentage of swap fees going to treasury
methodology.HoldersRevenue: Money going to governance token holders
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: Liquidity providers revenue

methodology.Fees: QUOTUM trading tax collected by TaxSink, measured in NVDA when claimed, excluding Pons platform fees and direct funding transfers.
methodology.Revenue: Claimed QUOTUM trading tax less cash NVDA forwarded to PAY_TO, including backing funding, with claims and transfers recognized when executed; retained funding and later buybacks can make attribution differ within a period.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: The fixed 40% share of claimed QUOTUM trading tax transferred to the protocol recipient in NVDA.
methodology.HoldersRevenue: NVDA spent on successful QUOTUM buybacks and burns at the daily bell, excluding failed purchases and direct token burns.
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: Cash NVDA forwarded by TaxSink to PAY_TO, including seat-use funding and backing funding recorded in keeper reports. This measures executed transfers, not inference consumption.

methodology.Fees: Trading fees paid by users on every Vaultex coin: 2% of each buy and sell on the bonding curve, in the coin's quote asset (SOL, USDC and more), read from Meteora DBC swap events. Most of it goes to the coin creator, split by the creator percentage of each Vaultex pool config (DBC create-config event).
methodology.Revenue: Vaultex's share of the trading fee on every bonding-curve trade, claimed into the Vaultex treasury.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: Vaultex's share of the trading fee on every bonding-curve trade, claimed into the Vaultex treasury.
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: The coin creator's share of every trade (which creators can share with their holders through Drip and Drop), Meteora's protocol fee, and the referral fee paid to the frontend that hosted the swap.

methodology.Fees: The 0.5% fee users pay on every swap made through Monolith Exchange, collected by Jupiter into Monolith's referral fee accounts.
methodology.UserFees: The 0.5% fee users pay on every swap made through Monolith Exchange.
methodology.Revenue: The 80% of the 0.5% swap fee that Monolith Exchange keeps after Jupiter's 20% share.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: The 80% of the 0.5% swap fee that goes to the Monolith Exchange treasury.
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: The 20% of the 0.5% swap fee that Jupiter keeps as the routing provider.

methodology.UserFees: The 4% paid by the owner who repays the loan.
methodology.Fees: On repayment, 3% of principal is paid to the funder and 1% of principal is paid to the protocol. The principal returned to the funder is not a fee.
methodology.Revenue: The 1% protocol fee paid to the protocol address on repayment.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: The 1% protocol fee paid to the protocol address on repayment.
methodology.Volume: USDG principal deposited into CapsuleLend when a card loan is funded.
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: The 3% paid to the funder when the owner repays.

methodology.Fees: BOT paid by consumers to request AI inference, plus forfeited dispute bonds. Inference fees are counted when a request is fulfilled - timed-out requests refund in full, so escrowed-only requests are excluded.
methodology.Revenue: The protocol's share (protocolFeeBps, currently 10%) of each fulfilled inference fee, plus forfeited challenge bonds, accrued to the treasury.
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: The operator's share of each fulfilled inference fee, paid on fulfillment.
methodology.UserFees: BOT paid by consumers to request AI inference.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: The treasury share of each fulfilled inference fee plus forfeited dispute bonds.

methodology.UserFees: Swap fees charged by DeepCore pools, read from each Swap event (protocol fee included), plus the fee DeepCore's router charges on fills it routes to other venues, read from its Filled events. Launch-pool creator taxes and launch-guard trade fees are not counted.
methodology.Fees: Swap fees charged by DeepCore pools, read from each Swap event (protocol fee included), plus the fee DeepCore's router charges on fills it routes to other venues, read from its Filled events. Launch-pool creator taxes and launch-guard trade fees are not counted.
methodology.Revenue: The protocol fee slice each Swap event carried, plus the router fee on routed fills. Both are paid to the protocol.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: The protocol fee slice each Swap event carried, plus the router fee on routed fills. Both are paid to the protocol.
methodology.HoldersRevenue: Money going to governance token holders
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: The rest of each swap fee, earned by liquidity providers.
methodology.Volume: Gross input of every swap on DeepCore's CLPoolManager and BinPoolManager, one leg per swap, read from Swap events. Trades the DeepCore router fills on other venues are not counted as volume.

USDC players spend opening Raflux gacha packs of physical trading cards (Super Gacha on Solana, FluxBox on Base), at the full pack price including any part covered by a coupon. Packs are sold at fixed prices of 10, 25, 50 and 100 USDC (1 USDC packs on Base at launch); each pack pulls a physical card, often with a USDC bonus, that the player can ship home or sell back for USDC.
methodology.Fees: Pack purchases minus USDC returned to players: refunds of cancelled pulls, card cash-outs, sell-backs, USDC prizes and reimbursed card shipments. This is the 10% fee Raflux keeps when a card is exchanged for USDC plus the game result of pulls, so it is negative on days when players win more than they pay.
methodology.Revenue: Pack purchases minus USDC returned to players, kept by Raflux. No share goes to LPs, referrers or token holders.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: Pack purchases minus USDC returned to players, all of it sent to the Raflux treasury.

methodology.UserFees: Swap fees paid by traders on every swap.
methodology.Fees: Swap fees paid by traders on every swap.
methodology.Revenue: Protocol share of swap fees, read per pool from the vault (protocol swap fee set by the protocol fee controller).
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: Protocol share of swap fees, which goes to the Bush treasury.
methodology.HoldersRevenue: Money going to governance token holders
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: Swap fees kept by liquidity providers, plus the pool creator fee where a pool sets one.
methodology.Volume: Value of all tokens swapped through Bush pools.
Notional volume of Hyperliquid perpetual trades (including HIP-3 markets) placed through Kokoah, counted from its builder code.
methodology.Fees: Hyperliquid builder code fees paid by users on perpetual trades placed through Kokoah; excludes Hyperliquid's own trading fees.
methodology.Revenue: Builder code fees collected by Kokoah. Referral rewards Kokoah later pays out off-chain from these fees are not deducted.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: Builder code fees collected by Kokoah. Referral rewards Kokoah later pays out off-chain from these fees are not deducted.

methodology.Fees: The desk's fee on the gross premium of each weekly call the vault sells (20% at launch), fixed at the sale and recognized one hour later when the Safe can no longer void the sale; a voided sale charges no fee. The premium itself is not counted as fees: it is the buyer's payment for the option, which depositors carry against the risk of the call settling in the money (see the options adapter's premium volume). A call sold outside the desk (not possible with the current operator) counts the fee the operator reports at settlement.
methodology.Revenue: All of the desk fee on the gross premium of each weekly call the vault sells, paid to the HedgeHood treasury Safe at settlement.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: All of the desk fee on the gross premium of each weekly call the vault sells, paid to the HedgeHood treasury Safe at settlement.

methodology.Volume: DEX Volume: Cash volume: USDC collateral paid by traders on BUYs and received on SELLs (gross_amount of every successful settle_fill instruction). Counts the trader side only; the house counterparty leg is not counted. Volume follows the live match calendar, so days with no live fixtures show zero by design.
methodology.Fees: On-chain BUY fee from FillEvent (SELLs and settlements are fee-free).
methodology.UserFees: On-chain BUY fee from FillEvent, paid by traders (SELLs and settlements are fee-free).
methodology.Revenue: 100% protocol revenue — no LPs, no token, no revenue share.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: 100% protocol revenue — no LPs, no token, no revenue share.

methodology.Fees: Trading fees paid on sprout.fun bonding curves (1% or 3% per launch) and in the Choice v2 pools that launches graduate into (same rate, taken by the Sprout hook).
methodology.Revenue: Trading fees minus the share credited to launch creators and referrers (the platform share).
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: Share of trading fees credited to launch creators, and on the curve to referrers.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: Part of the platform share that is not used for SPROUT buyback and burn.
methodology.HoldersRevenue: 80% of the platform share funds SPROUT buyback and burn (ratio taken from the Sprout docs).

methodology.UserFees: Users pay a 0.25% fee on each swap.
methodology.Fees: Each swap pays a 0.25% fee.
methodology.Revenue: 1/6 of swap fees (~0.0417%) accrue to the protocol via the factory feeTo LP mint.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: 1/6 of swap fees (~0.0417%) go to the protocol feeTo address.
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: 5/6 of swap fees (~0.2083%) go to liquidity providers.
methodology.Volume: Volume is calculated from Swap events on VibeSwap pairs created by the VibeFactory.
Notional volume of Hyperliquid perpetual trades routed through Mixin Perps' builder code.
methodology.Fees: Builder code revenue from Hyperliquid Perps Trades.
methodology.Revenue: Builder code revenue from Hyperliquid Perps Trades.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: Builder code revenue from Hyperliquid Perps Trades.

methodology.Fees: The service fee copypump charges on every copied buy and sell, collected as a USDC transfer to the copypump treasury and counted on the day it is collected (the collector batches fees per user, so a fee can land the day after its trade).
methodology.UserFees: The service fees copypump charges on every copied buy and sell, collected as a USDC transfer to the copypump treasury and counted on the day it is collected (the collector batches fees per user, so a fee can land the day after its trade).
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: The cost copypump pays on users' behalf: the SOL the copypump fee payer loses co-signing every copied trade (signature fee, priority fee, rent of the token accounts the route creates), net of the rent it recovers when the emptied accounts are closed back to it. Priced at the daily SOL price.
methodology.Revenue: Fees minus the fee payer cost: what copypump keeps. The 'app revenue, after gas' figure on copypumpfun.com/data.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: Fees minus the fee payer cost: what copypump keeps.

methodology.Fees: 1% swap fees on Pumper-launched tokens' Uniswap V3 pools and on the PUMPER pools, plus creator-set buy/sell taxes and the V4 hook / Lock-curve fees (1% base fee + tax) on Pumper-launched tokens. Launched tokens are taken from PumperProtocolRegistry.
methodology.Revenue: 15% of every launched token's fees and taxes: 10% to adminVault and 5% to the PUMPER buy-and-burn vault. PUMPER's own pool fees carry no protocol cut.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: The 10% of launched token fees and taxes paid to adminVault, the protocol treasury.
methodology.HoldersRevenue: The 5% of launched token fees and taxes sent to the PUMPER buy-and-burn vault, which buys and burns PUMPER.
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: 5% of launched token fees and taxes sent to the FEFER buy-and-burn vault (FEFER is a separate token), and 80% split between each token's creator, stakers, buyback-and-burn and liquidity in a ratio the creator fixes at launch; plus 100% of PUMPER pool fees, paid to its LPs.

methodology.Fees: Service fees charged by Polycool on every Polymarket buy and sell routed through the app (1.00% of the notional for new users, decreasing with lifetime volume to 0.50% above $100K, pulled from the trader's wallet into the Polycool treasury as USDC.e or pUSD), plus the Polymarket builder fees on those trades, which the trader pays inside Polymarket's trade fee and Polymarket pays out to Polycool daily.
methodology.UserFees: Service fees and Polymarket builder fees, both paid by the trader on every Polymarket buy and sell routed through Polycool.
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: Referral rewards: referrers earn 25% of the service fees generated by the users they referred. Counted when paid, as pUSD transfers from the referral payout wallet (the treasury since 2026-10-22) to referrers (claims before 2026-07-01, about $270 in total, were paid from the treasury and are not tracked).
methodology.Revenue: Service fees and Polymarket builder fees, minus referral rewards paid out. No liquidity providers.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: Service fees and Polymarket builder fees kept by Polycool after referral rewards are paid out.

methodology.Fees: The 1% bonding curve trading fee on every Ferzan coin before it graduates (Meteora's DBC fee on Solana, including Meteora's protocol share).
methodology.UserFees: The 1% fee paid by traders on every Ferzan coin before it graduates.
methodology.Revenue: Ferzan's share of the curve fee: 50%, less 10% to a referrer when one is set. On Solana, half of the DBC trading fee.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: Ferzan's share of the curve fee: 50%, less 10% to a referrer when one is set. On Solana, half of the DBC trading fee.
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: The coin creator's 50%, referrer payouts, and on Solana Meteora's protocol fee.
methodology.HoldersRevenue: None.

methodology.Fees: Fees paid by traders of coins launched on Incognito Launchpad (Solana): the launchpad's 0.25% platform fee and the coin creator's 0.5% fee on every trade against the Raydium LaunchLab bonding curves it configures, and, once a coin graduates, the quote-side trading fees of its permanently locked liquidity, harvested with the Fee Key the launchpad holds. Raydium's own protocol fee is excluded. Amounts are in each pool's quote token.
methodology.UserFees: The launchpad's 0.25% platform fee and the creator's 0.5% fee on every Incognito Launchpad bonding-curve trade, plus the quote-side trading fees of graduated launches' locked liquidity, all paid by traders.
methodology.Revenue: The platform fee and the harvested locked-liquidity fees, both received by the launchpad treasury.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: The 0.25% platform fee on bonding-curve trades and the harvested locked-liquidity fees, all sent to the launchpad treasury.
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: The creator fee of each bonding-curve trade, paid to the wallet that launched the coin.

methodology.Volume: Filled notional of Hyperliquid perpetual trades carrying Ditto's builder address.
methodology.Fees: Actual Hyperliquid builder fees paid on Ditto-routed perpetual trades; excludes venue trading fees.
methodology.Revenue: Builder fees collected by Ditto on its routed perpetual trades.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: Builder fees collected by Ditto on its routed perpetual trades.

methodology.Volume: Volume of Hyperliquid spot trades placed through the builder code.
methodology.Fees: Builder-code fees paid by users on Hyperliquid spot trades placed through the builder code.
methodology.Revenue: Builder-code fees on Hyperliquid spot trades, all kept by the builder.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: Builder-code fees on Hyperliquid spot trades, all sent to the builder's protocol.

methodology.Fees: SOL paid to Peep by its users: the 0.75% fee on swaps between SOL and a token made in Peep. Swaps between SOL and USDC/USDT, token-to-token swaps and tips carry no Peep fee. Peep's 5% share of paid group joins is not counted: a group join carries no on-chain marker that tells it apart from any transaction with the same two transfers.
methodology.UserFees: SOL paid by Peep users: the 0.75% fee on swaps between SOL and a token.
methodology.Revenue: SOL kept by Peep: the whole 0.75% fee on swaps between SOL and a token.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: SOL received by the Peep treasury: the whole 0.75% fee on swaps between SOL and a token.
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: None: Peep shares no part of its swap fee with referrers, integrators or Jupiter.

methodology.UserFees: Every fee traders pay on Bordrless DEX trades: the protocol fee, LP fee, coin creator fee and holder reward fee.
methodology.Fees: Every fee traders pay on trades on the Bordrless DEX, including launched coins after they graduate: the protocol fee, LP fee, coin creator fee and holder reward fee.
methodology.Revenue: The protocol fee, paid to the Bordrless treasury: half is kept, half buys back $BORDR.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: Half of the protocol fee, kept by the treasury.
methodology.HoldersRevenue: Half of the protocol fee, spent buying back $BORDR.
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: Fees paid to liquidity providers, coin creators and coin holders.
methodology.Volume: Sum of trades on the Bordrless DEX, including launched coins after they graduate.
Sum of trades on the Bordrless launchpad bonding curve, before a coin graduates.
methodology.Fees: Every fee traders pay on trades on the Bordrless launchpad bonding curve, before a coin graduates: the protocol fee, LP fee, coin creator fee and holder reward fee.
methodology.UserFees: Every fee traders pay on Bordrless launchpad bonding curve trades: the protocol fee, LP fee, coin creator fee and holder reward fee.
methodology.Revenue: The protocol fee, paid to the Bordrless treasury: half is kept, half buys back $BORDR.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: Half of the protocol fee, kept by the treasury.
methodology.HoldersRevenue: Half of the protocol fee, spent buying back $BORDR.
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: Fees paid to liquidity providers, coin creators and coin holders.

methodology.Fees: Creator trading fees that Pons pays to Credence vaults for the tokens Credence deployed, creator fees paid into creator vaults for X accounts, and the Credence fee charged on every launch.
methodology.UserFees: Creator trading fees paid by traders of Credence tokens on Pons, and the Credence fee paid by token creators at launch.
methodology.Revenue: What Credence keeps: 20% of each token vault's creator fees, which buys back and burns $PFWA, the protocol's cut of creator vault fees, and launch fees.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: Revenue sent to the Credence Safe: the protocol's cut of creator vault fees and the launch fees.
methodology.HoldersRevenue: The 20% of each token vault's creator fees that is spent buying $PFWA sent to the dead address, counted when the fees are collected.
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: 80% of each token vault's creator fees, bridged to Polygon to fund the token's Polymarket bet (whose winnings buy back and burn the token), and the creator vault fees held for the X account they belong to.

methodology.Fees: Everything traders and market creators pay on PFWA Markets: the trading fee on buys and on sells after a market's deadline, the early-sell penalty on sells before the deadline, and the fee to create a market. Activity of PFWA's own wallets (team, market seeder, market-making agent) is excluded.
methodology.UserFees: Everything traders and market creators pay on PFWA Markets: trading fees, early-sell penalties and market creation fees.
methodology.Revenue: The protocol's share of all fees: the protocol's leg of every trading fee (both legs on markets the protocol created), half of every early-sell penalty, and the market creation fee, including the part spent buying back and burning $PFWA.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: The fees sent to the PFWA treasury: the protocol's leg of every trading fee (both legs on markets the protocol created), half of every early-sell penalty, and the part of each market creation fee not used for the $PFWA buyback.
methodology.HoldersRevenue: ETH spent buying $PFWA that is burned: half of each v2 market creation fee is swapped for $PFWA in the same transaction and sent to the dead address.
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: The market creator's leg of the trading fee on markets created by users, and the half of each early-sell penalty paid into the market's bonus pot for the winning side.

methodology.Fees: The 5% of the ETH side of every swap in a Sherwood game pool that is paid into the round's prize pot. Direct deposits into the pots are not fees and are excluded.
methodology.UserFees: The 5% of the ETH side of every swap in a Sherwood game pool, paid by the swapper into the round's prize pot.
methodology.Revenue: The share of the pot fees that buys back and burns $PFWA: 10% in Season 1 (ETH/$PFWA pool) and 7% in Season 2 (ETH/$IMD pool) of what is left after the Dice randomness fees.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: Zero: the protocol keeps none of the pot fees.
methodology.HoldersRevenue: The share of the pot fees spent buying back and burning $PFWA (10% in Season 1, 7% in Season 2, after Dice randomness fees), counted when the swap pays the fee. Burns funded by direct pot deposits are excluded.
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: The Dice Protocol fees paid from the pot for Flip moves, then the share of the remaining pot fees paid to players: the round's prizes (80% in Season 1, 78% in Season 2), the share rolled into the next round's pot (10% and 5%), and in Season 2 the 10% that buys back and burns $IMD, the game pool's token.

methodology.Fees: Fees paid by traders on MoveFast launchpad pools: the platform trading fee, any pool fee, and the token tax each launch's creator sets. The part of the tax that burns the launched token is not included.
methodology.Revenue: The platform trading fee on every MoveFast trade (1.5% of the trade), sent to the MoveFast treasury.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: The platform trading fee on every MoveFast trade (1.5% of the trade), sent to the MoveFast treasury.
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: The token tax paid out to holders and creators of the launched tokens, plus any pool fee kept in the pool's reserves.

methodology.Fees: Settled yield from mxBTC's HyperCore funding strategy after borrowing and trading costs, converted to UBTC and measured at distribution, plus instant redeem/unstake fees; excludes unsettled strategy income.
methodology.Revenue: The foundation's share of settled mxBTC yield plus instant redeem/unstake fees, valued in UBTC.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: The foundation's share of settled mxBTC yield plus instant redeem/unstake fees retained by the protocol, valued in UBTC.
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: Settled yield allocated to smxBTC stakers and the insurance-fund reserve that backstops mxBTC.
methodology.UserFees: Instant redeem/unstake fees paid by users to skip the delayed exit flow, valued in UBTC.

methodology.Fees: Swap fees paid by traders on Choice v1 pools, which is 0.3% of the swap output.
methodology.Revenue: One sixth of each swap fee, kept by the protocol in the Choice treasury multisig.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: One sixth of each swap fee, sent to the Choice treasury multisig.
methodology.HoldersRevenue: Money going to governance token holders
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: Five sixths of each swap fee: two thirds stays in the pool for liquidity providers and one sixth goes to the Injective burn auction, which burns INJ.
methodology.Volume: Value traded on Choice v1 liquidity pools on Injective, counted on the input side of each swap; Choice v2 pools are a separate listing.

methodology.Fees: The 1% fee the Feast hook takes on every buy and sell of a Feast coin, paid in the coin's quote asset (a Binance tokenized stock or BNB). Excludes the PancakeSwap Infinity LP fee and the one-off 1% fee on the FEAST token sale.
methodology.UserFees: The 1% fee traders pay on every buy and sell of a Feast coin.
methodology.Revenue: The 20% platform share of every fee, plus the self-burn and creator shares of fees in the FEAST/BNB pool, all of which are used to buy and burn the FEAST platform token.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: No part of the fee goes to a team treasury: the platform share is used only to buy and burn FEAST.
methodology.HoldersRevenue: The 20% platform share of every fee, sold by the platform sink for FEAST which is burned, plus the self-burn and creator shares of fees in the FEAST/BNB pool, which buy and burn FEAST.
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: The rest of each fee, split as the coin's creator fixed it at launch: the creator's share, the referrer's share on referred trades, and the share used to buy back and burn the launched coin itself.

methodology.Volume: Service payments in USDC on Base settled through Central City's immutable fee routers with the fee included: the full price the router moves for each payment (90% to the seller, 10% fee to the treasury). Fee-on-top payments, where the router moves only the fee, are not counted. Includes payments made by all agents created on Central City, counted under the same rules.
methodology.Fees: The 10% protocol fee on qualifying Feed service payments, which AI agents make in USDC on Base for services on Central City's Feed (other payments carry no fee), charged by Central City's immutable fee routers and sent straight to the Central City treasury. Includes payments made by all agents created on Central City, counted under the same rules.
methodology.Revenue: The full 10% protocol fee on qualifying Feed service payments, which AI agents make in USDC on Base for services on Central City's Feed, kept by Central City: the immutable fee routers send it straight to the Central City treasury. Includes payments made by all agents created on Central City, counted under the same rules.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: The full 10% protocol fee on qualifying Feed service payments, which AI agents make in USDC on Base for services on Central City's Feed, sent by Central City's immutable fee routers straight to the Central City treasury. Includes payments made by all agents created on Central City, counted under the same rules.

methodology.Fees: Relay fees paid by users on private withdrawals, transfers and holder exits (30 bps plus a fixed gas quote), and the immutable 30 bps service fee on private swaps through the fee route adapters. Ragequit is free.
methodology.UserFees: Identical to Fees: every relay fee is paid by the end user out of the amount moved.
methodology.Revenue: All Relay fees. Lincoln has no liquidity providers or token holders sharing fees.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: Swap service fees are paid to the treasury Safe; relay fees accrue to the protocol-operated relays.

methodology.Fees: Fees charged when positions settle: a 0.5 basis point close charge on the order value plus the market fee (currently 2%) on the gain of winning trades and on the loss of losing and liquidated trades. Opening a position is free and there are no funding payments.
methodology.Revenue: All settlement fees, split between the protocol and CARDBOARD stakers.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: Half of settlement fees, allocated to the protocol fee recipient.
methodology.HoldersRevenue: Half of settlement fees, distributed in USDC to CARDBOARD stakers. Referral bonuses are paid from the same budget and are not separated.
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: LPs revenue

methodology.Fees: Profit fee of 2% on the gain of every winning trade, taken from the payout. Opening a position, losing trades and liquidations are free and there is no funding. The house bankroll's trading profit is not counted.
methodology.Revenue: All profit fees, kept by Jupiter in a fee balance of the YOLO program separate from the house bankroll; there are no liquidity providers.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: Half of profit fees, kept by Jupiter.
methodology.HoldersRevenue: Half of profit fees, used to buy back JUP under Jupiter's policy of spending 50% of revenue on JUP buybacks.
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: LPs revenue

methodology.Volume: Gross USDC players pay to open card packs, including draws that are later refunded.
methodology.Fees: USDC players pay to open card packs, net of refunds and instant buybacks of won cards, plus marketplace fees on card trades.
methodology.Revenue: Pack sales net of refunds and buybacks, minus payouts to third-party card stakers, referral commissions and draw fees sent to the Jackpot, plus marketplace fees. Payouts for cards staked by the platform's own wallets stay in revenue.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: Pack sales net of refunds and buybacks, minus payouts to third-party card stakers, referral commissions and draw fees sent to the Jackpot, plus marketplace fees, all kept by the TopMarket treasury.
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: Card prices and profit shares paid or credited to third-party stakers whose cards were won, referral commissions settled to referrers, and draw fees routed to the Jackpot prize pool since October 2026.

methodology.UserFees: Swap fees paid by traders, at the dynamic fee the Nami plugin sets for each swap.
methodology.Fees: Swap fees paid by traders, at the dynamic fee the Nami plugin sets for each swap.
methodology.Revenue: Swap fees of gauged pools, paid to Nami token holders: 90% to veNAMI voters and 10% to ogNAMI stakers.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: Swap fees paid to Nami fee receivers other than Algebra, veNAMI voters and ogNAMI stakers.
methodology.HoldersRevenue: Swap fees of gauged pools paid to veNAMI voters (90%) and ogNAMI stakers (10%).
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: Swap fees of permissionless pools: 99% to liquidity providers and 1% to Algebra as the DEX licence fee.
methodology.Volume: Swap volume across all Nami V4 concentrated liquidity pools.
Perps trading volume routed through the HypurrTrade terminal on Hyperliquid.
methodology.Fees: Builder fees paid by users on perps trades routed through HypurrTrade (0.05% until 2026-10-08, 0.1% since); excludes Hyperliquid's own trading fees.
methodology.Revenue: Builder fees collected by HypurrTrade from Hyperliquid perps trades.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: Builder fees collected by HypurrTrade from Hyperliquid perps trades.

methodology.UserFees: Equals total swap fees paid by users.
methodology.Fees: Users pay each pool's configured fee tier (0.01% to 5%) on every swap.
methodology.Revenue: No protocol fee is taken: the factory owner is burned, so feeProtocol can never be turned on.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: No protocol fee is taken.
methodology.HoldersRevenue: Money going to governance token holders
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: 100% of swap fees are distributed to liquidity providers.
methodology.Volume: Swap volume from all CommunityV3 pools deployed via the factory on Ethereum.

methodology.Fees: Management and performance fees paid by vault investors (the manager's and FBYT's parts), plus the SOL trading fee paid on every vault swap and the SOL fee paid to create a vault.
methodology.UserFees: All fees: investors pay the management and performance fees, managers (or their trading delegates) pay the trading and vault creation fees.
methodology.Revenue: FBYT's share of the management and performance fees, plus all trading and vault creation fees.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: FBYT's share of the management and performance fees, plus all trading and vault creation fees.
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: The money managers' share of the management and performance fees.

methodology.Volume: Completed swaps routed by WormSwap, counted once using the received input before its router fee; the received output is used when only that leg is a core asset, and BNB/WBNB wrapping is excluded.
methodology.Fees: User-paid swap and BNB/WBNB wrapping fees actually credited to WormSwap's fee distributor before protocol allocations, excluding external token transfer taxes, underlying DEX fees, Arena payments and donations.
methodology.Revenue: Net swap and wrapping fee receipts retained by WormSwap and allocated entirely to TANUKI buybacks and burns, with no supplier or referral share.
methodology.HoldersRevenue: Net swap and wrapping fee receipts earmarked for TANUKI buybacks and burns, recognized when received rather than again when the burn batch executes.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: WormSwap allocates none of its net router fee receipts to a discretionary treasury; all are reserved for TANUKI buybacks and burns.
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: WormSwap pays no supplier or referral share from its router fee; underlying PancakeSwap liquidity-provider fees belong to PancakeSwap.

methodology.Fees: The 10% tax traders pay on PSTR buys and sells, plus the USDC yield earned by the PAPER the treasury has staked on Papertrade, valued at the HYPE it is swapped to and counted when the buyback contract spends it. Tax paid by the buyback contract's own purchases is excluded, since it is paid out of that yield.
methodology.UserFees: The 10% tax traders pay on PSTR buys and sells.
methodology.Revenue: All fees: the trade tax goes to the team and the treasury and the yield goes to the team and the buyback.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: The trade tax (one tenth to the team, nine tenths to the treasury that acquires and stakes PAPER), the team's 10% share of the staking yield, and the tax the buyback contract pays on its own PSTR purchases.
methodology.HoldersRevenue: The staking yield the buyback contract spends buying PSTR and burning it, net of the 10% tax it pays on those purchases.

methodology.Volume: USDC value of every share traded across all Seeryx prediction markets (shares times fill price), counted once per fill and excluding the exchange's own test trades.
methodology.Fees: Taker fees paid by traders whose orders fill against a resting order, at 7% x price x (1 - price) per share, minus fees refunded on trades that failed to settle on Solana; deposit and withdrawal fees are not included.
methodology.UserFees: Taker fees paid by traders on every fill, at 7% x price x (1 - price) per share, minus fees refunded on trades that failed to settle; makers pay no fee.
methodology.Revenue: Taker fees kept by Seeryx after paying 20% back to makers as rebates and refunding fees on trades that failed to settle.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: Taker fees kept by Seeryx after maker rebates and refunds, collected into the fee account of the Seeryx program on Solana; Seeryx has no token, so all of it goes to the protocol.
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: Rebates paid to market makers: 20% of each fill's taker fee goes to the trader whose resting order was filled.

methodology.Fees: Fees paid by bskts users: the mint fee on buying a basket and the zap-out fee on selling one for USDG, plus each basket's yearly management fee.
methodology.Revenue: All mint, zap-out and management fees, kept by the bskts treasury.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: All mint, zap-out and management fees, sent to the bskts treasury.

methodology.Fees: The 2% fee on every buy and sell of a coin launched on Sapling, the flat fee paid to plant a coin, and Sapling's fee on buys, plantings and sales made from a Zcash account. On Robinhood Chain: the 2% creator tax plus the creator's 70% of Pons's 1% fee on every buy and sell of a coin planted through Sapling, both paid to Sapling's splitter, plus the planting fee and the Zcash account fee, paid in USDG to the treasury.
methodology.Revenue: The part of the 2% coin trading fee Sapling keeps (10% treasury, 25% $SAPLING buyback and burn, 25% $SAPLING/ZEC liquidity), plus the planting fee and the Zcash account fee. On Robinhood Chain the shares apply to what reaches Sapling's splitter: the 2% creator tax plus the creator's 70% of Pons's 1% fee.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: The treasury's share: 10% of the 2% coin trading fee, plus the planting fee and the Zcash account fee. On Robinhood Chain the shares apply to what reaches Sapling's splitter: the 2% creator tax plus the creator's 70% of Pons's 1% fee.
methodology.HoldersRevenue: 50% of the 2% coin trading fee: 25% buys and burns $SAPLING, and 25% goes to the $SAPLING/ZEC pool on PumpSwap, where about half of it buys $SAPLING, both sides are deposited and the LP tokens are burned, so no one, Sapling included, can withdraw it. On Robinhood Chain the shares apply to what reaches Sapling's splitter: the 2% creator tax plus the creator's 70% of Pons's 1% fee.
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: 40% of the 2% coin trading fee, paid to each coin's deployer, a wallet they choose, or the holders of that coin as holder rewards (on Robinhood Chain, 40% of what reaches Sapling's splitter).

methodology.Fees: Swap fees paid by traders, plus bribes paid to the protocol to attract AERO Rewards to pools.
methodology.Revenue: Swap fees earned by AERO-earning liquidity and bribes, all distributed to sAERO holders.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: Percentage of swap fees going to treasury
methodology.HoldersRevenue: Swap fees earned by AERO-earning liquidity and bribes, all distributed to sAERO holders.
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: Swap fees kept by fee-earning liquidity providers.
methodology.Volume: Swap volume on Aero volatile and stable pools.

methodology.Fees: Fees users pay Veil to shield tokens into its private pool, withdraw them, swap privately or fill a private DCA order, plus Veil's share of the relayer fee; network fees, Jupiter's swap fees and tokens swept from closed DCA escrows are not included.
methodology.UserFees: Fees users pay Veil to shield tokens into its private pool, withdraw them, swap privately or fill a private DCA order, plus Veil's share of the relayer fee they pay.
methodology.Revenue: All fees users pay Veil for shielding, withdrawals, private swaps and private DCA fills, plus its share of the relayer fee, all kept by Veil as it has no liquidity providers or stakers to pay.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: All fees users pay Veil, collected into the Veil treasury, minus the $VEIL the treasury buys back and burns with 20% of revenue, so it is negative on days when more is burned than earned.
methodology.HoldersRevenue: $VEIL bought on the market with 20% of Veil's revenue and burned, counted from the buyback wallet's on-chain burns at the token's price.

methodology.Fees: Arbitrage profit made through the vaults' pools, as each vault's profit splitter pays it out.
methodology.Revenue: 25% of the profit: half to the fee jar, which buys GOO and burns it, and half to the development fund.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: 12.5% of the profit, paid to the development fund.
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: 75% of the profit, compounded into the vault for its depositors.
methodology.HoldersRevenue: 12.5% of the profit, sent to the fee jar, which auctions it for GOO and burns the GOO.

methodology.Volume: Notional volume of Hyperliquid perpetual trades carrying ARX's builder code, including HIP-3 perpetual markets; excludes spot trades and legacy ARX builder addresses.
methodology.Fees: Actual builder-code fees paid on Hyperliquid perpetual trades carrying ARX's builder code; excludes Hyperliquid exchange trading fees and legacy ARX builder addresses.
methodology.Revenue: Builder-code fees received by ARX on Hyperliquid perpetual trades, before any subsequent referral payouts from ARX's treasury.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: Builder-code fees received by ARX on Hyperliquid perpetual trades, before any subsequent referral payouts from ARX's treasury.

methodology.Fees: EVM chains: swap fees of the pools sasa creates for every coin, counted when sasa's builder collects them: the quote-asset side (ETH, BNB or USDC) and the coin side (in the launched coin, valued where the coin has a price). Solana: the creator fees of coins launched on sasa (both halves).
methodology.UserFees: Traders pay the pool's swap fee (EVM) or the launch curve's creator fee (Solana) on every buy and sell.
methodology.Revenue: EVM: 70% of the collected swap fees, sent to sasa's fee vault. Solana: sasa's 50% of the creator fees, received by its treasury.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: EVM: 70% of the collected swap fees, sent to sasa's fee vault. Solana: sasa's 50% of the creator fees, received by its treasury.
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: EVM: 30% of the collected swap fees, sent to each coin's creator, or used to buy back and burn the coin when its creator chose buybacks. Solana: the creators' 50% of the creator fees.

methodology.Fees: A 0.25% fee on every cash-out from the Gloam shielded pool. Deposits and private payments are free.
methodology.UserFees: Users pay the 0.25% cash-out fee, taken from the amount they cash out.
methodology.Revenue: All cash-out fees go to the Gloam fee recipient.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: All cash-out fees go to the Gloam fee recipient.

methodology.Fees: The fee the Stockereum hook charges on every swap, in the quote currency, from the hook's Trade event: 1% on v2 launches, 1%, 2% or 3% (chosen by the creator) on v3 launches, plus the anti-snipe rate in the first moments after a launch.
methodology.UserFees: Traders pay the whole swap fee.
methodology.Revenue: The platform's share of the swap fee: half of the normal 1% on v2, 0.5% of the trade on 1% v3 launches and 1% of the trade on 2% and 3% v3 launches, plus any anti-snipe excess.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: The platform's share of the swap fee.
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: The rest of the swap fee, paid to the launch's creator or, on launches with holder rewards enabled, to the launched token's holders.

methodology.UserFees: Users pay the full swap fee charged by the selected V3 pool.
methodology.Fees: Traders pay the fee tier configured for the pool: 0.01%, 0.05%, 0.30%, or 1%.
methodology.Revenue: Protocol revenue is the exact amount emitted as protocolFeesToken0 or protocolFeesToken1 by each swap.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: Protocol revenue accrues in each pool according to its governance-controlled protocol fee.
methodology.HoldersRevenue: Money going to governance token holders
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: Liquidity providers receive total swap fees minus the exact protocol-fee amounts emitted by each swap.
methodology.Volume: Volume is derived from Swap events emitted by BitBlocks Finance V3 concentrated-liquidity pools on BNB Smart Chain.
Sum of amountIn from SherwoodSwap events emitted by the Sherwood Router.
methodology.Fees: Router fee (feeAmount in SherwoodSwap events), charged on the input token.
methodology.Revenue: All router fees go to the TradeWood treasury.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: All router fees go to the TradeWood treasury.

methodology.UserFees: All fees are paid by traders.
methodology.Fees: All fees traders pay, before any share goes back to Conviction Pool depositors or referrers: opening and closing fees, liquidation closing fees included, plus the borrowing fees paid while a position is open. Funding is paid between traders and is not counted.
methodology.Revenue: The share of opening and closing fees Nova keeps (governance fee).
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: The share of opening and closing fees Nova keeps (governance fee). Nova has no token.
methodology.HoldersRevenue: Fees going to governance token holders
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: The share of opening and closing fees sent to the Conviction Pool (vault, OC, referral and trigger shares) and all borrowing fees.
methodology.Volume: Notional (collateral x leverage) of every opening and closing trade on Nova's markets, partial size changes included, read from the trading diamond's FeesProcessed events. Liquidations are excluded.

methodology.Fees: Total interest paid by borrowers
methodology.Revenue: Protocol and holders share of interest
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: Protocol's share of interest into treasury
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: Interest paid to lenders in liquidity pools
methodology.HoldersRevenue: Share of interest into protocol governance token holders.

methodology.UserFees: The haircut and the win fee on profitable closes. The loss fee is not included: it comes out of the LP pool's receipt, not on top of the trader's loss.
methodology.Fees: On profitable closes, an impact haircut on the gain and a 2% fee on the gain after the haircut; on losing closes and liquidations, a 2% fee on the margin lost, taken by the protocol from what the LP pool receives.
methodology.Revenue: All fees (Win Haircut, Win Fee, Loss Fee) are kept: the haircut stays in the protocol-owned LP pool and the win fee goes to the protocol.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: All fees (Win Haircut, Win Fee, Loss Fee) are kept by the protocol.
methodology.HoldersRevenue: Fees going to governance token holders
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: LPs revenue

methodology.Volume: Notional volume of Hyperliquid perpetual trades (including HIP-3 markets) copied through FiatBear, counted from its builder code.
methodology.Fees: Hyperliquid builder code fees paid by users on trades copied through FiatBear; excludes Hyperliquid's own trading fees.
methodology.Revenue: Builder code fees collected by FiatBear on copied trades.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: Builder code fees collected by FiatBear on copied trades.

methodology.Volume: Gross quote-asset value of every buy and sell on CURB bonding curves (CurveBuy quoteIn; CurveSell quoteOut + fee + tax). Trading in graduated Uniswap v4 pools is excluded: it is counted by the Uniswap v4 adapter.
methodology.Fees: The trading tax (1%-5%, set per launch) paid on every curve and graduated-pool trade, in the quote asset. The pools' 0.05% Uniswap v4 LP fee is not included: it is earned by the pool's liquidity and already counted by the Uniswap v4 adapter.
methodology.UserFees: Traders pay the whole trading tax. Launching costs gas only.
methodology.Revenue: The platform's share of the tax (0.50% of the trade at deployment, frozen into each launch), plus the creator share of launches whose creator wallet is the treasury ($CURB).
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: The platform's share of the tax on both venues, plus the creator share of treasury-created launches ($CURB), paid to the treasury Safe.
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: The rest of the tax: to the launch's creator, or to the launch's own token holders through its distributor once holder sharing is on.

methodology.Volume: Notional volume of Hyperliquid perpetual trades (including HIP-3 markets) placed through Perpex, counted from its builder code.
methodology.Fees: Hyperliquid builder code fees paid by users on perpetual trades placed through Perpex; excludes Hyperliquid's own trading fees.
methodology.Revenue: Builder code fees collected by Perpex.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: Builder code fees collected by Perpex.

methodology.Fees: Every swap in a Phlece coin's Uniswap v4 pool pays a 0.98% base fee plus the creator's 1-10% tax, in the coin's paired asset (QuoteFeeTaken events of each coin's hook). Swaps in a coin's first 3 seconds also pay an anti-snipe surcharge. The pool's own LP fee is 0.
methodology.Revenue: 20% of every trading fee (the portal's platformBps) plus the whole anti-snipe surcharge go to the Phlece team Safe.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: 20% of every trading fee plus the anti-snipe surcharge, paid to the Phlece team Safe.
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: The other 80% of each trading fee, split by percentages the coin's creator fixed at launch between the creator, the coin's holders (dividends), buyback-and-burn of the coin, and liquidity added to the coin's locked pool position.

methodology.Fees: The fees players pay on settled positions: the open fee on each deposit and the 10% profit fee on a gain.
methodology.UserFees: The open fees and profit fees players pay on settled positions.
methodology.Revenue: The fees less the creator royalty: the protocol's share and the $OVER holders' share.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: The open fees and the profit fees less the creator royalty and the $OVER holders' share.
methodology.HoldersRevenue: 25% of the profit fees: from $OVER positions to the $OVER stakers' rewards, from USDG positions to $OVER buybacks.
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: The creator royalty: 15% of the profit fee on a winning prediction, paid to the creator of the channel predicted on.

methodology.Volume: Maker/taker volume that flows through the OrbitDEX interface
methodology.Fees: Builder Fees collected from Orderly Network
methodology.Revenue: All the fees collected
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: All the revenue goes to the protocol

methodology.Fees: Platform fees paid in USDG on every token and stock token trade made in Onagi (transfers into the Onagi fee vault), plus all Pons V2 swap fees and creator tax charged on ONAGI token trades (curve and graduated pool sweep events). Platform fees include a small reimbursement for network gas that Onagi pays on behalf of users, which is not separated on chain.
methodology.UserFees: Platform fees paid in USDG on every token and stock token trade made in Onagi, plus all Pons V2 swap fees and creator tax charged on ONAGI token trades (curve and graduated pool sweep events).
methodology.Revenue: Platform fees plus the creator share of ONAGI token swap fees that Pons credits to Onagi.
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: The Pons protocol and Pons buyback share of ONAGI token swap fees, not kept by Onagi.
methodology.HoldersRevenue: 75% of revenue: 50% is paid to eligible ONAGI holders in USDG and 25% buys ONAGI and sends it to the burn address. Computed from Onagi's published split.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: 25% of revenue goes to the Onagi treasury.

methodology.Fees: Fees paid by traders of tokens launched on Grainpad (Solana): Grainpad's platform fee (0.75% under its current config) and the token creator's fee (0.25%) on every trade against the Raydium LaunchLab bonding curves it configures, and, once a token graduates, the quote-side trading fees of its permanently locked liquidity, harvested with the Fee Keys Grainpad holds, plus the creator fee of those graduated pools, counted when the launch's creator claims it. Raydium's own protocol fee and the token transfer taxes of Grainpad reward launches are excluded. Amounts are in each pool's quote token, mostly wXMR.
methodology.UserFees: Grainpad's platform fee and the creator's fee on every Grainpad bonding-curve trade, plus the quote-side trading fees of graduated launches' locked liquidity and the creator fee of their pools, all paid by traders.
methodology.Revenue: The platform fee and the harvested locked-liquidity fees, both received by Grainpad.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: The platform fee on bonding-curve trades and the harvested locked-liquidity fees, all received by Grainpad.
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: The creator fee of each bonding-curve trade and of each graduated pool, paid to the wallet that launched the token.

methodology.Fees: pump.fun creator fees of coins launched through Furnace, paid by traders and split on-chain by the Furnace program. Excludes the founder's half of $FURN's own creator fees and coins whose fees go to a person through pump.fun fee sharing directly, since neither passes through a Furnace coin vault.
methodology.UserFees: pump.fun creator fees paid by traders of coins launched through Furnace, split on-chain by the Furnace program.
methodology.Revenue: The Furnace treasury share and the $FURN buyback & burn share of the creator fees of coins launched through Furnace, plus the part of $FURN's own creator fees held by its vault, all of which buys back and burns $FURN.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: The 10% Furnace treasury share of each coin's creator fees, after the 30% of it paid to the coin's referrer when it has one.
methodology.HoldersRevenue: Creator fees spent on buying back and burning $FURN: 10% of every coin's creator fees, plus the part of $FURN's own creator fees held by its vault.
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: Creator fees paid to the holders of each launched coin, spent on buying back and burning that coin, vested to its creator, or paid to its referrer.

methodology.Fees: DUSK paid to register and renew .dusk names (including premium pricing on new names) and the 2.5% marketplace fee on name sales, from the vault contract's fee_received events.
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: The referrer's share of a fee, credited in the vault for the referrer to claim: 20% of a registration's base price and 10% of a renewal since launch on 21 Oct 2026, capped at 30% of any fee by the vault.
methodology.Revenue: Fees (DUSK paid to register and renew .dusk names (including premium pricing on new names) and the 2.5% marketplace fee on name sales) minus referral shares, kept by the vault as protocol funds.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: Fees (DUSK paid to register and renew .dusk names (including premium pricing on new names) and the 2.5% marketplace fee on name sales).

methodology.Volume: Notional volume of Lighter perps trades (Robinhood Chain) routed through Onagi's integrator account, from Lighter's partner stats.
methodology.Fees: Onagi's integrator fee on Lighter perps trades routed through Onagi, from Lighter's partner stats.
methodology.UserFees: Onagi's integrator fee, paid by traders on top of Lighter's own fees on perps trades routed through Onagi.
methodology.Revenue: All of Onagi's integrator fee on Lighter perps trades, kept by Onagi.
methodology.HoldersRevenue: 75% of Onagi's perps integrator fee: 50% is paid to eligible ONAGI holders in USDG and 25% buys ONAGI and sends it to the burn address. Computed from Onagi's published split.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: 25% of Onagi's perps integrator fee goes to the Onagi treasury.

methodology.Fees: Builder fees received by Onagi from trades on Polymarket v2
methodology.Revenue: Builder fees received by Onagi from trades on Polymarket v2
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: 25% of builder fees received by Onagi, kept by Onagi
methodology.HoldersRevenue: 75% of builder fees received by Onagi, distributed to its token holders

methodology.UserFees: All trading fees are paid directly by traders.
methodology.Fees: Maker plus taker trading fees paid by traders, net of maker rebates.
methodology.Revenue: All net trading fees are kept by the protocol.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: All net trading fees are kept by the protocol.

methodology.SupplySideRevenue: LPs revenue
methodology.Volume: Traded notional of perpetual fills on the Vistapex order book. Each fill is counted once (not per side), and self-trades are excluded. Liquidations closed on the order book are included; ADL and backstop takeovers are not.

methodology.Fees: Trading fees paid on vibe.market card coins: the ETH fee on every Base card coin trade, the WETH side of the Uniswap pool fees earned by graduated Base card coins, and the WETH fees collected by vibe.market's Robinhood Chain pack markets. Fees paid in $SPORTS or in card coins are not priced and are excluded.
methodology.Revenue: The protocol's share of trading fees (on Base 40% of each trade's fee since August 2025, 20% before, plus the referrer shares of trades that name no referrer), and half of the graduated Base card coins' pool fees.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: The protocol's share of trading fees, paid to the vibe.market Safe.
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: Trading fees paid to pack creators and to referrers, and the creators' half of the graduated Base card coins' pool fees.

methodology.UserFees: The 0.25% fee on DUSK deposited into Sozu's pool.
methodology.Fees: Staking rewards earned by the DUSK staked through Sozu's pool, counted as the pool harvests and restakes them every hour, plus deposit fees.
methodology.Revenue: Sozu's treasury share of its fee on staking rewards (10% of rewards until 2026-09-07, 15% since), net of the operators' share, plus the 0.25% deposit fee; both are minted to the treasury as stDUSK.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: Sozu's treasury share of its fee on staking rewards, net of the operators' share, plus the 0.25% deposit fee, minted to Sozu's treasury as stDUSK.
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: Staking rewards kept by stDUSK holders (90% until 2026-09-07, 85% since) plus the share of Sozu's fee paid to the operators running its provisioners.

methodology.Fees: Trading fees paid on every buy and sell of RunUp coins (1.3% of the USDC amount, 2% for the RUNUP token), on the bonding curve and in the pool a coin graduates into, plus the 1.3% fee on RUNUP founding-sale tickets.
methodology.Revenue: The platform's cut of every coin's trading fees, plus the RUNUP token's creator share (paid to the team wallet), its buyback and burn share and its INJ holder rewards share.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: The platform's cut of every coin's trading fees (1.10% of each trade on the bonding curve, 0.40% to 0.60% after graduation depending on the coin's fee split) and the RUNUP token's creator share, which goes to the team wallet that deployed RunUp.
methodology.HoldersRevenue: The share of RUNUP token trading fees used to buy back and burn RUNUP, and the share swapped to INJ and paid to RUNUP holders.
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: Trading fees of community coins paid to their creators, to their own buybacks, perp strategy treasuries and INJ holder rewards, and fees left in graduated pools as liquidity (all coins including RUNUP), plus the RUNUP token's strategy treasury share.

methodology.Fees: Builder fees EVplusAI earns on Papertrade: a share of the PnL (0.5% since launch) of positions its users close, paid by winning traders on top of the 2% win fee and taken from the Papertrade LP's gain on losing ones. Liquidations pay none, and closes by EVplusAI's own address are excluded.
methodology.Revenue: All builder fees EVplusAI earns on Papertrade closes by its users, kept by EVplusAI.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: All builder fees EVplusAI earns on Papertrade closes by its users, credited to EVplusAI's Papertrade balance.

methodology.HoldersRevenue: Fees going to governance token holders
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: The liquidity providers' share of perp and expiry-future close, liquidation and liquidity fees (75% since launch), plus all borrow fees, kept by the pools.
methodology.Volume: Notional of every perpetual and expiry-future trade (opens, limit fills, closes, and take-profit and stop-loss fills) at its execution spot price. Liquidations and expiry settlements are not trades and are not counted.

methodology.Revenue: The 20% protocol share of the collected creator fees, used to buy back and burn $PAYGRAM.
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: The 80% share of the collected creator fees owed to the @handle or the coin holders each coin was launched for.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: Paygram keeps none of the creator fees in a treasury: its whole 20% share is used to buy back and burn $PAYGRAM.
methodology.HoldersRevenue: The 20% protocol share of the collected creator fees, used to buy back and burn $PAYGRAM.

methodology.HoldersRevenue: The ElcasBurner sells what it receives for ETH, buys $ELCAS and burns it.
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: A third of the fees to the token's creator (or, V3, as a tokenized-stock index to its holders), a third to the token's casino rooms and perps / predict markets (their stakers), the V3 keeper rewards, and the ETH launch fees of V3 that pay the keepers opening each token's rooms and markets.

methodology.Volume: Gross receipts: the USDG paid for drops committed in the period. Every drop costs the fixed price of the active gacha configuration, $10.00 under configuration 1.
methodology.Fees: Gross receipts minus prizes: the USDG paid for drops less the fixed USD prize value of every drop settled in the period, which the game pays in a Robinhood stock token or, when stock delivery is unavailable, in USDG. Prizes are the cost of the game, so this is what players lost to the house, negative in a period where they win more than they pay in. Plus the swap fees the treasury claims from its launch-liquidity position in the STONKD/USDG Uniswap v3 pool, paid in USDG and STONKD. Unclaimed LP fees are not counted.
methodology.Revenue: All of Fees: receipts minus prizes, plus the claimed LP fees. The vault that pays prizes is protocol-owned, with no liquidity providers, referrers or token distributions, so nothing is shared out.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: The house result, which accrues in the game vault controlled by the team, plus the LP fees the treasury claims. Owner deposits into and withdrawals from the vault are treasury movements and are not counted.
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: Zero: the bankroll is protocol-owned and there are no external liquidity providers.

methodology.Fees: Creator fees from coins launched on OTC (Pump.fun bonding curve and PumpSwap), paid out by Pump.fun to OTC's fee wallet, plus the creator fees of the $OTC token itself, plus the 0.5 SOL surcharge paid on every Desk NFT mint (refundable account rent excluded). Meteora launches, whose fees are claimed in the quote token, are not tracked yet.
methodology.Revenue: Share of launcher fees, $OTC creator fees and Desk mint surcharges sent to the OTC protocol wallet, plus the launcher fees used to buy back and burn $OTC or paid as SOL dividends to $OTC holders.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: Share of launcher fees sent to the OTC protocol wallet (12.5% since Oct 3 2026, 5% from Sep 13 to Oct 2, 15% from early September to Sep 12 and less in the first days after launch), plus the part of $OTC's own creator fees the Desk pot forwards to it (50% per the docs, less in earlier months), plus 0.05 SOL of each Desk mint surcharge.
methodology.HoldersRevenue: Share of launcher fees used to buy back and burn $OTC (10% since Sep 12 2026, about 5% before) and SOL dividends paid to $OTC holders (5% of launcher fees from Sep 12 to Oct 2 2026).
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: Launcher fees spent on the reward tokens airdropped to each launcher coin's holders and the account rent those payouts need (67.5% of launcher fees since Oct 3 2026, 70% before), plus the Desk pot paid out to Desk NFT owners (10% of launcher fees, the $OTC creator fees left after the protocol's part, and 0.45 SOL of each Desk mint surcharge).
